app.title.context: Name of the whole administration console, used as the browser tab and window title. 'Ingest' is the product name and stays exactly as it is; 'Admin' is short for the administration console, not a person holding that job.

apiErrors.unexpected.context: Last-resort wording when a request fails with nothing usable to report — a dropped connection or a failure that carried no server explanation at all. Shown to an administrator in the red message bar above the form they were working in, so keep it plain and non-technical.

apiErrors.status.400.context: Used when the server rejected the request as malformed and gave no diagnostic code to explain it. This is almost always a product fault rather than something the administrator typed wrong, so avoid wording that blames the reader; it appears in the red message bar above the form.

apiErrors.status.401.context: Shown when the credential the console is signing in with was refused — typically a missing, mistyped or expired key. 'API key' is the secret credential an administrator pastes into the console, never a keyboard key or a database key; keep the term recognisable, as it is also the label of the field where the key is entered.

apiErrors.status.403.en: You don't have permission to do this.
apiErrors.status.403.context: Shown when the signed-in account is recognised but lacks the permission for the action just attempted. Addresses the reader directly in the second person; it is a statement of fact, not a refusal to be softened into an apology.

apiErrors.status.404.en: That item could not be found.
apiErrors.status.404.context: Shown when the record the console asked for does not exist, usually because someone else deleted it while this page was open. 'Item' is deliberately vague because the same wording covers any record — a schema, a submission, an account — so do not narrow it to one kind of object.

apiErrors.status.408.en: The request took too long. Please try again.
apiErrors.status.408.context: Shown when the server gave up waiting for the request to complete. 'Took too long' describes the request, not the administrator's patience; the closing sentence is an invitation to retry the same action, in the imperative.

apiErrors.status.409.en: This conflicts with another change. Reload and try again.
apiErrors.status.409.context: Shown when someone else saved a change to the same record first, so the edit in progress would overwrite it. 'Reload' is an imperative instruction to load the page again, not a noun; keep both instructions as commands.

apiErrors.status.410.en: That item is no longer available.
apiErrors.status.410.context: Shown when the record once existed but has been removed for good, as opposed to never having existed. Choose wording that conveys permanence rather than a temporary absence.

apiErrors.status.413.context: Shown when what the console tried to send — typically an uploaded backup, import or report file — exceeds the size the server accepts. 'Request' means the data sent to the server, so a rendering as 'query' or 'enquiry' would be wrong.

apiErrors.status.415.en: That type of content is not supported.
apiErrors.status.415.context: Shown when an upload is in a file or content type the server does not accept, for example a spreadsheet where JSON or CSV is expected. 'Content' here means the format of the uploaded data, not editorial content.

apiErrors.status.422.en: The data could not be processed.
apiErrors.status.422.context: Shown when the request was well-formed but the server could not act on the data inside it, and no more specific reason came back. 'Processed' means handled or acted upon, not manufactured.

apiErrors.status.429.en: Too many requests — please wait a moment and try again.
apiErrors.status.429.context: Shown when the console has been throttled for sending too many requests in a short time. 'Please wait a moment' asks for a short pause before retrying; the dash may be replaced by whatever punctuation joins two clauses naturally in the target language.

apiErrors.status.500.en: Something went wrong on the server. Please try again.
apiErrors.status.500.context: Shown when the server failed unexpectedly while handling the request. Make it clear the fault is on the server side and not the administrator's doing, and keep the retry sentence as an imperative.

apiErrors.status.502.en: The server isn't responding right now. Please try again shortly.
apiErrors.status.502.context: Shown when the server cannot be reached or is not answering — an outage or a restart in progress rather than a rejected request. The neighbouring gateway and timeout failures use the same English wording, so translate all three identically.

apiErrors.status.503.en: The server isn't responding right now. Please try again shortly.
apiErrors.status.503.context: Shown when the server is temporarily out of service, for example during a deployment. 'Shortly' promises a short wait rather than a fixed time; the same English wording is shared with the other server-unreachable cases, so keep the three translations identical.

apiErrors.status.504.en: The server isn't responding right now. Please try again shortly.
apiErrors.status.504.context: Shown when the server accepted the request but nothing answered in time. Shares its English wording with the other server-unreachable cases and should read identically to them.

apiErrors.status.server.en: Something went wrong on the server. Please try again.
apiErrors.status.server.context: Catch-all for any server-side failure that is not one of the individually worded ones. Its English is identical to the plain internal-failure wording and should be translated the same way; the fault lies with the server, not the reader.

apiErrors.status.request.context: Catch-all for a rejected request when the server gave no reason and the exact cause is unknown. 'Failed' describes the request, so avoid a rendering that suggests the administrator failed at something.

apiErrors.status.unexpected.context: Used when a response cannot be classified as either a request problem or a server problem, which should effectively never happen. Keep it short and neutral; it appears in the red message bar with no further detail beside it.

apiMessages.common.not_found.context: Reported when the record an administrator asked for could not be located, either because it was deleted or because an identifier was wrong. The name of the missing record arrives from the server already in English and cannot be inflected, so build the sentence so that it works with an untranslated name dropped in; only the sentence is translated, never the diagnostic code that selects it.

placeholders.resource: Server-supplied English description of what was looked for, sometimes with its identifier, e.g. Account or Submission '3f8c1a9e-…'

apiMessages.common.conflict.en: The request conflicts with the current state. {{message}}
apiMessages.common.conflict.context: Reported when the action would clash with the way things already stand — a name already taken, a record already in the target state. 'Current state' means how the data stands right now and has nothing to do with electricity; the sentence is followed by the server's own explanation, which stays in English.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation of the clash, appended as a second sentence, e.g. Account 'north-depot' already exists.

apiMessages.common.forbidden.en: You don't have permission to do this. {{message}}
apiMessages.common.forbidden.context: Reported when the signed-in account is known but is not allowed to perform this action. Addresses the reader in the second person and is followed by the server's own English explanation of which rule blocked it.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about why the action was refused, e.g. This service is outside your assigned scope.

apiMessages.common.unauthorized.en: You need to sign in to continue.
apiMessages.common.unauthorized.context: Reported when there is no valid session or credential behind the request, usually because the session expired while the page stayed open. 'Sign in' means authenticate with the console again; keep it as an instruction to the reader rather than an abstract noun. Only the sentence is translated; the diagnostic code stays as it is.

apiMessages.common.service_unavailable.context: Reported when the server has deliberately taken a capability offline, most often the intake of new submissions during maintenance. Here 'service' means the server-side facility, not an Ingest service (the organisational unit that submits data), so avoid the term used for those elsewhere in the console.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation, often the maintenance notice an operator configured, e.g. Submissions are temporarily closed.

apiMessages.common.validation.context: Generic summary shown when one or more rules rejected what was submitted and no more specific wording exists. 'Validation' is the checking of input against rules; the individual rule messages follow, supplied by the server in English, one after another.

placeholders.message: The server's own English list of the rules that failed, joined into one piece of text, e.g. Label is required.; Timestamp is required.

apiMessages.common.internal.en: Something went wrong on the server. Please try again.
apiMessages.common.internal.context: Reported when the server hit an unhandled fault, so nothing the administrator did caused it and nothing they change will fix it. Keep the retry sentence in the imperative; only the sentence is translated, never the diagnostic code behind it.

apiMessages.common.feature_disabled.context: Reported when an optional part of the product — e-mail, webhooks, the Teams integration — is switched off in the server configuration, so the screen an administrator opened has nothing to talk to. 'Not enabled' describes a configuration setting that an operator can turn on, not a licensing or permission problem.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail naming the switched-off feature, e.g. email is disabled.

apiMessages.api.invalid_request.context: Reported when the server could not make sense of the request itself, rather than of the data an administrator entered. Treat it as a system-level fault; the server's own English explanation follows the sentence.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation of what was wrong with the request, e.g. 'from' must be earlier than or equal to 'to'.

apiMessages.api.missing_required_paramet.context: Reported when a mandatory piece of the request was left out, for example asking for an exploration chart without naming a schema. The parameter name is a literal identifier from the interface and must stay exactly as it arrives, inside the quotation marks; only the surrounding sentence is translated.

placeholders.parameter: Literal name of the missing request parameter, never translated, e.g. schema

apiMessages.api.unsupported_omit.en: The omit value “{{value}}” is not supported.
apiMessages.api.unsupported_omit.context: Reported when a request asked to skip a validation step by a name the server does not recognise; today only the reporting-period duplicate check can be skipped. 'Omit' is the literal name of the request option and stays untranslated, as does the rejected value itself.

placeholders.value: The unrecognised value that was supplied, shown verbatim, e.g. cadence

apiMessages.api.single_parameter_require.en: A single “{{parameter}}” value is required for {{operation}}.
apiMessages.api.single_parameter_require.context: Reported when an operation accepts exactly one value where several (or none) were given — the spreadsheet export, for instance, can only cover one schema at a time. Both inserted values are machine identifiers that stay in English; 'single' means one and only one, not 'unmarried' or 'simple'.

placeholders.parameter: Literal name of the parameter that needs exactly one value, e.g. schemaName
placeholders.operation: Machine identifier of the operation that imposes the limit, never translated, e.g. submissions.export.xlsx

apiMessages.api.service_outside_scope.en: Service “{{serviceId}}” is outside your assigned scope.
apiMessages.api.service_outside_scope.context: Reported when an administrator acts on behalf of a service that is not in the list of services their own account is allowed to see. 'Service' here is the Ingest organisational unit that submits data, and 'scope' is the set of those services assigned to the reader's account; the identifier shown is a technical id and is never translated.

placeholders.serviceId: Technical identifier of the service that was refused, e.g. 7c1f0b42-5a9d-4e31-9a10-2f6b8c4d5e77

apiMessages.submissions.validation.context: Generic summary when a submission — one filled-in set of values for a service and reporting period — was rejected by rules that have no more specific wording. The failing rules follow in the server's own English; the sentence appears at the top of the red message bar, above the list of individual findings.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what failed, e.g. Value 'Waste / Tonnes' below min (0).

apiMessages.submissions.duplicate_period.en: “{{displayName}}” has already been submitted for this {{cadence}} period.
apiMessages.submissions.duplicate_period.context: Raised when the service already has an accepted figure for that field in the same reporting window, so a second one would be a duplicate. The name shown is the field's human label prefixed by its schema's label, and 'period' is a reporting window such as a calendar month, never a punctuation mark; the cadence word arrives from the server in lower-case English and is not translated.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of the schema it belongs to, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.cadence: Lower-case English word for how often the field is reported, inserted untranslated, e.g. monthly, weekly, quarterly

apiMessages.submissions.pending_duplicat.en: “{{displayName}}” already has a submission awaiting approval for this {{cadence}} period.
apiMessages.submissions.pending_duplicat.context: Raised when another submission covering the same field and reporting window is still waiting for an approver to sign it off, so it is not visible yet but does occupy the window. The way out is to replace that pending submission rather than create a second one; the cadence word arrives in lower-case English and stays as it is.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of the schema it belongs to, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.cadence: Lower-case English word for how often the field is reported, inserted untranslated, e.g. monthly, weekly, quarterly

apiMessages.submissions.schema_not_assig.en: Schema “{{schemaName}}” is not assigned to this service.
apiMessages.submissions.schema_not_assig.context: Raised when data is filed against a schema — an administrator-defined form definition — that the service in question has not been given. Usually a configuration oversight rather than bad data: either the wrong schema name was used or the schema still has to be assigned to that service. The schema's machine name is shown verbatim and is never translated.

placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema as sent by the caller, shown verbatim, e.g. waste_collection

apiMessages.submissions.schema_disabled.context: Raised when the schema exists but an administrator has switched it off, so it no longer accepts new data while its history stays readable. 'Disabled' describes that deliberate configuration state, not a fault or a deletion.

placeholders.schemaName: Human label of the schema, falling back to its machine name when no label is set, e.g. Waste collection

apiMessages.submissions.value_not_define.en: Value “{{valueName}}” is not defined in schema “{{schemaName}}”.
apiMessages.submissions.value_not_define.context: Raised when a submission carries a field name that the schema does not define, typically a typo or a leftover from an older version of the form. In this product a 'value' is a named field of a schema, not a numeric amount, and both names shown are taken from the data as-is.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the unknown field as sent by the caller, e.g. tonnes_collcted
placeholders.schemaName: Human label of the schema, falling back to its machine name, e.g. Waste collection

apiMessages.submissions.calculated_value.context: Raised when someone tries to file a figure for a field the server works out itself from an expression over the other fields. 'Calculated' means derived automatically, so such a field is read-only by design and the submitted figure has to be dropped.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the calculated field, e.g. recycling_rate

apiMessages.submissions.value_disabled.context: Raised when the field itself has been switched off on the schema, so it no longer accepts data even though the rest of the form does. 'Disabled' is a deliberate configuration state chosen by an administrator.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected

apiMessages.submissions.value_required.context: Raised when a mandatory field was included in the submission but left empty. 'Required' describes the field's setting on the schema; the wording states the rule rather than instructing the reader, and it appears as one line in the list of findings.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected

apiMessages.submissions.required_value_m.context: Raised when a mandatory field was left out of the submission altogether, rather than sent empty. The human label comes first and the two machine names in brackets identify the same field for anyone editing the schema; keep the dot between them and leave both untranslated.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected

apiMessages.submissions.value_type.context: Raised when the figure sent does not fit the data type the schema declares for that field — text where a number is expected, an unparseable date, and so on. The type word arrives from the server as a lower-case English term and must be left exactly as it is, since it matches the type shown in the schema editor.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.expectedType: Lower-case English name of the required data type, never translated: string, integer, number, date or boolean

apiMessages.submissions.value_minimum.context: Raised when a number falls below the lower bound configured for that field on the schema. 'At least' means greater than or equal to, and 'received' introduces what was actually sent; both numbers are formatted by the server, so leave them as they arrive.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.minimum: Lowest number the schema accepts for this field, e.g. 0
placeholders.actual: The number that was actually submitted, e.g. -12.5

apiMessages.submissions.value_maximum.en: Value “{{displayName}}” must be no more than {{maximum}} (received {{actual}}).
apiMessages.submissions.value_maximum.context: Raised when a number exceeds the upper bound configured for that field on the schema. 'No more than' means less than or equal to; the second number is what was actually sent.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.maximum: Highest number the schema accepts for this field, e.g. 100
placeholders.actual: The number that was actually submitted, e.g. 143.2

apiMessages.submissions.value_before_min.en: Value “{{displayName}}” ({{schemaName}}.{{valueName}}) must be on or after {{minimum}} (received {{actual}}).
apiMessages.submissions.value_before_min.context: Raised when a date field is earlier than the earliest date the schema allows. 'On or after' includes the boundary date itself; the two machine names in brackets identify the field for whoever maintains the schema, and both dates arrive pre-formatted in a technical UTC form that must not be rewritten.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Reading date
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. reading_date
placeholders.minimum: Earliest date the schema accepts, in a technical UTC format, e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z
placeholders.actual: The date that was actually submitted, in the same format, e.g. 2025-12-30T00:00:00.0000000Z

apiMessages.submissions.value_after_maxi.en: Value “{{displayName}}” ({{schemaName}}.{{valueName}}) must be on or before {{maximum}} (received {{actual}}).
apiMessages.submissions.value_after_maxi.context: Raised when a date field is later than the latest date the schema allows. 'On or before' includes the boundary date itself; the bracketed machine names and both dates arrive from the server already formatted and stay untranslated.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Reading date
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. reading_date
placeholders.maximum: Latest date the schema accepts, in a technical UTC format, e.g. 2026-12-31T00:00:00.0000000Z
placeholders.actual: The date that was actually submitted, in the same format, e.g. 2027-01-04T00:00:00.0000000Z

apiMessages.submissions.value_minimum_le.en: Value “{{displayName}}” must contain at least {{minimum}} characters (received {{actual}}).
apiMessages.submissions.value_minimum_le.context: Raised when a text field is shorter than the minimum length set on the schema. Both numbers count characters, not words; 'received' introduces the length of what was actually sent.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Site reference
placeholders.minimum: Smallest number of characters the schema accepts, e.g. 3
placeholders.actual: Number of characters actually submitted, e.g. 1

apiMessages.submissions.value_maximum_le.en: Value “{{displayName}}” must contain no more than {{maximum}} characters (received {{actual}}).
apiMessages.submissions.value_maximum_le.context: Raised when a text field is longer than the maximum length set on the schema. Both numbers count characters; 'no more than' includes the limit itself.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Site reference
placeholders.maximum: Largest number of characters the schema accepts, e.g. 20
placeholders.actual: Number of characters actually submitted, e.g. 34

apiMessages.submissions.value_regex.en: Value “{{displayName}}” does not match the required format.
apiMessages.submissions.value_regex.context: Raised when a text field does not match the character pattern the schema author configured for it, for instance a site code that must look like two letters and four digits. 'Format' means that pattern rule, not a file format or a way of laying text out on screen.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Site reference

apiMessages.submissions.value_validation.context: Raised when the schema author's own rule for that field judged the submitted figure unacceptable. What follows the colon is the explanation the administrator wrote into the schema, so it arrives in whatever language they typed and must be passed through untouched.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.detail: Message written by the schema author, or a technical fallback when the rule gave none, e.g. Tonnes must not exceed last month by more than 20%

apiMessages.submissions.value_validation.en: The validation rule for “{{displayName}}” could not be evaluated: {{detail}}
apiMessages.submissions.value_validation.context: Raised when the field's own rule could not even be worked out — a broken expression on the schema rather than bad data from the service. Points the reader at the schema that needs fixing; the technical explanation after the colon comes from the expression engine in English and is not translated.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.detail: Technical explanation from the expression engine, in English, e.g. Parameter 'tonnes_colected' was not defined

apiMessages.submissions.schema_validatio.context: Raised when a rule that spans several fields of the same schema rejected the submission as a whole, for example one figure having to add up to two others. The text after the colon is the explanation the schema author wrote and stays exactly as it arrives.

placeholders.schemaName: Human label of the schema, falling back to its machine name, e.g. Waste collection
placeholders.detail: Message written by the schema author, or the rule itself when none was given, e.g. Recycled plus landfilled must equal total

apiMessages.submissions.schema_validatio.en: A validation rule for schema “{{schemaName}}” could not be evaluated: {{detail}}
apiMessages.submissions.schema_validatio.context: Raised when one of the schema's cross-field rules could not be worked out at all, which is a fault in the rule rather than in the submitted data. The technical explanation after the colon comes from the expression engine in English.

placeholders.schemaName: Human label of the schema, falling back to its machine name, e.g. Waste collection
placeholders.detail: Technical explanation from the expression engine, in English, e.g. Unexpected token ')' at position 14

apiMessages.submissions.value_not_modifi.context: Raised when a submission is being replaced and one of its figures was marked as not modifiable, so the figure already on record has to stand. 'Cannot be changed' refers to that setting on the schema, not to a temporary lock or a permission of the reader.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected

apiMessages.submissions.gating_evaluatio.en: The {{rule}} rule for “{{schemaName}} / {{valueName}}” could not be evaluated: {{detail}}
apiMessages.submissions.gating_evaluatio.context: Raised when one of the rules that decides whether a field applies at all could not be worked out, so the submitted figure was neither used nor silently dropped. The rule name arrives as the literal setting name from the schema editor and must not be translated, and the explanation after the colon is technical English from the expression engine.

placeholders.rule: Literal name of the rule as it appears in the schema editor, never translated: EnabledIf or VisibleIf
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.detail: Technical explanation from the expression engine, in English, e.g. Parameter 'site_type' was not defined

apiMessages.submissions.sample_discarded.context: Generic notice that one submitted reading was dropped while the rest of the submission was kept. A 'sample' is a single reading for one field at one point in time; this is a warning rather than a rejection, so it is listed in the amber warnings block, with the server's own English explanation following.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation of why the reading was dropped, e.g. Sample 'Waste collection / Tonnes collected' discarded by VisibleIf.

apiMessages.submissions.sample_discarded.context: Warning that one reading was dropped because a rule on the schema said it does not apply, together with the reason the schema author wrote. The rule name is the literal setting name from the schema editor; the two machine names identify schema and field and all three stay untranslated.

placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.rule: Literal name of the rule as it appears in the schema editor, never translated: EnabledIf or VisibleIf
placeholders.detail: Reason written by the schema author, e.g. Not collected at transfer stations

apiMessages.submissions.sample_discarded.context: Warning that one reading was dropped because a rule on the schema decided the field does not apply to this submission, with no explanation configured. Listed in the amber warnings block, not as an error; the rule name and both machine names arrive verbatim.

placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.rule: Literal name of the rule as it appears in the schema editor, never translated: EnabledIf or VisibleIf

apiMessages.submissions.warning_rule_tri.en: The warning rule for “{{displayName}}” was triggered.
apiMessages.submissions.warning_rule_tri.context: Notice that the schema's warning rule for that field fired: the figure looks unusual but the submission was still accepted and stored. 'Triggered' means the condition was met, so this is an alert to look at the figure, not a rejection.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected

apiMessages.submissions.warning_rule_mes.context: Notice raised by the schema's warning rule for that field, carrying the text the schema author wrote for it. The submission was accepted; only the label and the punctuation around it are translated, since the text after the colon arrives in whatever language the administrator typed.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.detail: Warning text written by the schema author, e.g. More than 20% above last month

apiMessages.submissions.warning_rule_err.en: The warning rule for “{{displayName}}” could not be evaluated: {{detail}}
apiMessages.submissions.warning_rule_err.context: Notice that the warning rule configured for that field is itself broken and could not be worked out, so no judgement about the figure was possible. A schema-configuration fault rather than bad data; the explanation after the colon is technical English from the expression engine.

placeholders.displayName: Human label of the field, prefixed by the label of its schema, e.g. Waste collection / Tonnes collected
placeholders.detail: Technical explanation from the expression engine, in English, e.g. Division by zero

apiMessages.submissions.legacy_warning.context: Carries a warning that an older server stored on a submission with no structured detail, so the whole line is the server's own text and there is nothing around it to translate. Leave the placeholder on its own and add no punctuation, wording or spacing of your own.

placeholders.message: The complete warning text as it was stored, in English, e.g. Sample 'Waste collection / Tonnes collected' discarded by VisibleIf.

apiMessages.submissions.published_cannot.en: A published submission cannot be returned to draft.
apiMessages.submissions.published_cannot.context: Raised when someone tries to turn a submission that has already been filed back into a draft. 'Published' means filed and visible in reporting, while a 'draft' is a partially filled submission saved but not yet filed; the way back is to edit the filed submission or copy it into a new draft.

apiMessages.submissions.not_awaiting_app.en: This submission is not awaiting approval.
apiMessages.submissions.not_awaiting_app.context: Raised when an approve or reject decision is recorded for a submission that is not actually waiting for one — it was already signed off, already rejected, or never needed approval. Usually means someone else decided first while this page stayed open.

apiMessages.submissions.wrong_owner.en: This submission belongs to a different account.
apiMessages.submissions.wrong_owner.context: Raised when an account tries to edit or replace a submission filed by a different account. 'Belongs to' expresses ownership of the record; the reader is not being accused of anything, so keep it factual rather than accusatory.

apiMessages.submissions.window_not_open.en: The submission window is not open. {{message}}
apiMessages.submissions.window_not_open.context: Generic wording for an attempt to file data before the reporting window for that field has begun. A 'submission window' is the stretch of time during which data for a reporting period may be sent; the server's own English explanation, usually naming the opening moment, follows the sentence.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation with the exact timing, e.g. The monthly submission window for 'waste_collection.tonnes_collected' opens at 2026-09-01 00:00:00Z.

apiMessages.submissions.window_closed.context: Generic wording for an attempt to file or change data after the reporting window for that field has ended. 'Closed' means the window is no longer accepting data — not that a dialog was dismissed or that a period was finalised by hand; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English explanation with the exact timing, e.g. The monthly window for 'waste_collection.tonnes_collected' closed at 2026-09-08 00:00:00Z.

apiMessages.submissions.create_window_no.en: The {{cadence}} submission window for “{{schemaName}}.{{valueName}}” opens at {{windowStart}}.
apiMessages.submissions.create_window_no.context: Raised when a new submission is filed too early: the window for that field has not started yet. The cadence word arrives in lower-case English, the two machine names identify schema and field with a dot between them, and the moment shown is a technical UTC timestamp — leave all of them exactly as they arrive.

placeholders.cadence: Lower-case English word for how often the field is reported, inserted untranslated, e.g. monthly
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.windowStart: Moment the window begins, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-09-01 00:00:00Z

apiMessages.submissions.create_window_cl.en: The {{cadence}} submission window for “{{schemaName}}.{{valueName}}” closed at {{windowEnd}}.
apiMessages.submissions.create_window_cl.context: Raised when a new submission arrives after the window for that field has ended, so it can no longer be filed without an administrator amending it. 'Closed at' names the moment the window stopped accepting data; the cadence word, the machine names and the timestamp all stay as they arrive.

placeholders.cadence: Lower-case English word for how often the field is reported, inserted untranslated, e.g. monthly
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.windowEnd: Moment the window stopped accepting data, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-09-08 00:00:00Z

apiMessages.submissions.modify_window_cl.en: Submission {{submissionId}} cannot be modified: the {{cadence}} window for “{{schemaName}}.{{valueName}}” closed at {{windowEnd}}.
apiMessages.submissions.modify_window_cl.context: Raised when an existing submission is edited after the window for one of its fields has ended, so the figure on record has to stand. The identifier, the cadence word, the two machine names and the timestamp are all machine-supplied and untranslated; only the sentence around them changes.

placeholders.submissionId: Technical identifier of the submission being edited, e.g. 8a2d51c7-9f04-4b6e-a3d1-77c0e9b5a412
placeholders.cadence: Lower-case English word for how often the field is reported, inserted untranslated, e.g. monthly
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.windowEnd: Moment the window stopped accepting data, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-09-08 00:00:00Z

apiMessages.submissions.ingestion_closed.context: Raised while an operator has deliberately suspended the intake of new data, for instance during maintenance, so nothing can be filed for the time being. 'Closed' means intake is paused and will resume, not that a period was finalised; the explanation that follows is whatever notice the operator configured, in their own words.

placeholders.message: The notice configured by the operator, or a default English sentence when none was set, e.g. Maintenance until 18:00 UTC

apiMessages.imports.invalid_file.context: Reported when a bulk import file cannot be read as a whole, so nothing in it was taken in. Shown in the import dialog above the per-submission results, followed by the server's own English explanation of the structural problem.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what is wrong with the file, e.g. Row 4: 'schemaName' and 'valueName' are required.

apiMessages.imports.empty_file.context: Reported when the chosen import file contains nothing at all, or only whitespace. 'Empty' describes the file's content, not a missing selection — the file was read successfully but had nothing in it.

apiMessages.imports.invalid_json.en: The import file is not valid JSON: {{detail}}
apiMessages.imports.invalid_json.context: Reported when a JSON import file is not well-formed, so parsing stopped before any data could be read. JSON is a file format name and stays as it is; the technical explanation after the colon comes from the parser in English and is not translated.

placeholders.detail: Parser's own English explanation, usually with a position, e.g. ',' is invalid after a value at line 12

apiMessages.imports.unsupported_format.en: The import format is not supported. {{message}}
apiMessages.imports.unsupported_format.context: Reported when an import was requested in a file format the server does not handle; only JSON and CSV files can be taken in. 'Format' means the file format, and the server's own English detail naming what was asked for follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail naming the rejected format, e.g. Unsupported import format 'Xml'.

apiMessages.imports.submissions_not_arra.en: The “submissions” property must be an array, not {{actualKind}}.
apiMessages.imports.submissions_not_arra.context: Reported when a JSON import file has the expected top-level property but it is not a list. The property name is a literal key inside the file and stays exactly as written, as does the JSON kind name that says what was found instead.

placeholders.actualKind: English JSON type name of what was found instead of a list, never translated, e.g. Object, String, Number, Null

apiMessages.imports.invalid_root.en: The import root kind {{actualKind}} is invalid. Accepted shapes: {{acceptedShapes}}.
apiMessages.imports.invalid_root.context: Reported when the outermost element of a JSON import file is not one of the shapes the importer accepts. 'Root kind' means the JSON type of that outermost element, and the accepted shapes are literal technical notations that must be passed through unchanged.

placeholders.actualKind: English JSON type name of the outermost element, never translated, e.g. String, Number, True
placeholders.acceptedShapes: Comma-separated list of literal shape notations, never translated, e.g. array, object.submissions, object.samples

apiMessages.imports.submission_not_objec.en: Submission {{submissionNumber}} must be an object, not {{actualKind}}.
apiMessages.imports.submission_not_objec.context: Reported for one entry in a JSON import file that is not a structured object, so it cannot describe a submission. The number counts submissions in the file starting at one, matching how they are listed in the import results.

placeholders.submissionNumber: Position of the entry in the file, counted from 1, e.g. 3
placeholders.actualKind: English JSON type name of what was found instead of an object, never translated, e.g. String, Array, Null

apiMessages.imports.samples_missing.en: Submission {{submissionNumber}} must contain a samples array (received {{actualKind}}).
apiMessages.imports.samples_missing.context: Reported when an entry in a JSON import file carries no list of readings, so there is nothing to file. 'Samples' is the literal property name in the file and stays untranslated; the type shown in brackets may come out empty when the property is absent altogether.

placeholders.submissionNumber: Position of the entry in the file, counted from 1, e.g. 3
placeholders.actualKind: English JSON type name of what was found instead of a list, or nothing at all when the property is missing, e.g. Object

apiMessages.imports.sample_names_require.en: Submission {{submissionNumber}}, sample {{sampleNumber}} requires schemaName “{{schemaName}}” and valueName “{{valueName}}”.
apiMessages.imports.sample_names_require.context: Reported for one reading in a JSON import file that does not say which schema and which field it belongs to. The two words before the quotation marks are literal property names from the file and must not be translated; the quoted parts show whatever was found there, so they are often empty.

placeholders.submissionNumber: Position of the entry in the file, counted from 1, e.g. 3
placeholders.sampleNumber: Position of the reading inside that entry, counted from 1, e.g. 2
placeholders.schemaName: Whatever the file supplied as the schema's machine name, often empty, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Whatever the file supplied as the field's machine name, often empty, e.g. tonnes_collected

apiMessages.imports.sample_invalid_json.en: Submission {{submissionNumber}}, sample {{sampleNumber}} contains invalid JSON at line {{lineNumber}}, byte {{bytePositionInLine}}: {{detail}}
apiMessages.imports.sample_invalid_json.context: Reported when one reading inside a JSON import file is malformed, pinpointing where the parser stopped. 'Byte' is the position within that line counted in bytes rather than characters; all four inserted parts are machine-supplied and the explanation after the colon stays in English.

placeholders.submissionNumber: Position of the entry in the file, counted from 1, e.g. 3
placeholders.sampleNumber: Position of the reading inside that entry, counted from 1, e.g. 2
placeholders.lineNumber: Line of the file where parsing failed, e.g. 47
placeholders.bytePositionInLine: Offset within that line, counted in bytes, e.g. 18
placeholders.detail: Parser's own English explanation, e.g. The JSON value could not be converted to System.DateTime

apiMessages.imports.submission_no_sample.context: Reported when every reading in one entry of an import file had to be rejected, leaving nothing to file for it. 'Valid' means usable after the structural checks, so the entry itself was recognised but its contents were not.

placeholders.submissionNumber: Position of the entry in the file, counted from 1, e.g. 3

apiMessages.imports.missing_column.context: Reported when a CSV import file has no header column of the given name. 'Column' refers to a column of the spreadsheet or CSV file, and the name inside the quotation marks is the literal header text the importer looks for, so it is never translated.

placeholders.column: Literal header name the importer requires, never translated, e.g. schemaName, valueName, value, timestamp

apiMessages.imports.row_names_required.context: Reported for a CSV row that does not say which schema and field its figure belongs to. The row number counts lines including the header, so it matches what a spreadsheet shows; the two words before the quotation marks are literal column names and stay untranslated.

placeholders.row: Line number in the file, counting the header row as line 1, e.g. 8
placeholders.schemaName: Whatever the row supplied in the schema-name column, often empty, e.g. waste_collection
placeholders.valueName: Whatever the row supplied in the field-name column, often empty, e.g. tonnes_collected

apiMessages.imports.row_timestamp_invali.context: Reported when the date and time in a CSV row cannot be understood; the importer reads dates in the international form, not in local conventions. The quoted text is exactly what the file contained, so it must be passed through even when it is nonsense.

placeholders.row: Line number in the file, counting the header row as line 1, e.g. 8
placeholders.timestamp: The date-and-time text exactly as it appeared in the file, e.g. 31/09/2026 24:00

apiMessages.imports.no_data_rows.en: The import file contains no data rows.
apiMessages.imports.no_data_rows.context: Reported when a CSV import file has a header but nothing underneath it, so there is nothing to take in. 'Data rows' are the lines below the header; this is a fault in the file rather than in the product.

apiMessages.imports.invalid_row.context: Generic wording for a single unusable line in an import file. The server's own English explanation follows and names the line and the problem; the sentence itself carries no line number.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about the offending line, e.g. Row 8: '31/09/2026' is not a valid timestamp.

apiMessages.imports.no_submissions.en: No submissions were found in the file.
apiMessages.imports.no_submissions.context: Reported when an import file was read successfully but described no submissions at all. Not an error in the file's structure — simply nothing to file, so keep the wording matter-of-fact.

apiMessages.imports.accounts.invalid_mar.en: This is not an Ingest accounts export.
apiMessages.imports.accounts.invalid_mar.context: Reported when the file chosen for an accounts restore does not carry the tag identifying it as an accounts export produced by this product — usually the wrong file was picked. 'Ingest' is the product name and stays as it is, and 'accounts export' is the name of that download in the console.

apiMessages.imports.accounts.invalid_jso.en: The {{fileType}} file is not valid JSON: {{detail}}
apiMessages.imports.accounts.invalid_jso.context: Reported when the file chosen for an accounts restore is not well-formed JSON. The inserted file kind is a machine word that arrives in English, and the parser's explanation after the colon is technical English that stays untranslated.

placeholders.fileType: Machine word naming the kind of file being read, inserted untranslated, e.g. accounts
placeholders.detail: Parser's own English explanation, e.g. Expected depth to be zero at the end of the JSON payload

apiMessages.imports.accounts.unsupported.en: Accounts export version {{actualVersion}} is not supported; expected version {{expectedVersion}}.
apiMessages.imports.accounts.unsupported.context: Reported when an accounts export was produced by a different version of the file format than this server understands, typically a newer server writing for an older one. Both numbers are format versions of the file, not product version numbers.

placeholders.actualVersion: Format version found in the file, e.g. 2
placeholders.expectedVersion: Format version this server reads, e.g. 1

apiMessages.imports.accounts.no_accounts.en: The accounts file contains no accounts.
apiMessages.imports.accounts.no_accounts.context: Reported when an accounts export is well-formed but lists no accounts, so a restore would do nothing. States a fact about the file rather than a failure of the product.

apiMessages.imports.accounts.entry_name_.en: An account entry was skipped because accountName “{{accountName}}” is missing.
apiMessages.imports.accounts.entry_name_.context: Reported for one account in a restore file that has no name, so it was skipped while the remaining accounts were still imported. 'accountName' is the literal property name in the file and stays untranslated; the quoted part shows what was found there and therefore normally comes out empty.

placeholders.accountName: Whatever the file supplied as the account name, which is empty or absent in this case, e.g. north-depot

apiMessages.imports.accounts.entry_faile.context: Reported for one account in a restore file that could not be created or updated, while the rest of the file was still imported. 'Skipped' means left out of the import, and the server's own English explanation of the underlying reason follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail, usually the account name and the underlying reason, e.g. 'north-depot': Account 'north-depot' already exists.

apiMessages.accounts.validation.context: Generic summary when the details entered for an account were rejected and no more specific wording applies. Shown in the red message bar at the top of the account form, with the failing rules following in the server's own English.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. 'jane@' is not a valid email address.

apiMessages.accounts.already_exists.context: Raised when an account is created or renamed to a name another account already holds; names are unique across the whole installation. The name shown is the account's own unique identifier as typed by the administrator, not a display label.

placeholders.accountName: Unique name of the account, exactly as entered, e.g. north-depot

apiMessages.accounts.invalid_email.en: “{{email}}” is not a valid email address.
apiMessages.accounts.invalid_email.context: Raised when the contact address entered for an account is not a usable e-mail address. The quoted text is reproduced exactly as typed, including any typing mistake, so it must not be normalised or corrected in the translation.

placeholders.email: The address exactly as it was entered, e.g. jane@@example.com

apiMessages.accounts.unknown_capabilitie.context: Raised when an account is granted permissions the server does not recognise, usually a stale list from an older configuration or a restore file. 'Capabilities' are the named permissions an account can hold; the listed identifiers are machine names and stay untranslated even though the surrounding sentence is translated.

placeholders.capabilities: Comma-separated machine names of the unrecognised permissions, never translated, e.g. schemas.publish, reports.export

apiMessages.accounts.invalid_assigned_se.en: One or more assigned service IDs are invalid: {{serviceIds}}.
apiMessages.accounts.invalid_assigned_se.context: Raised when the list of services an account is restricted to names something that is not an existing service. A service is the organisational unit that submits data, and 'assigned services' is the allow-list attached to the account; the identifiers are technical ids shown for support purposes.

placeholders.serviceIds: Comma-separated technical identifiers that could not be matched to a service, e.g. 7c1f0b42-5a9d-4e31-9a10-2f6b8c4d5e77

apiMessages.accounts.invalid_sso_link.context: Generic wording when a single sign-on link on an account is rejected. A 'link' here is the binding between this account and an identity at an external sign-in provider — never a hyperlink — and SSO stands for single sign-on, which most locales keep as the English abbreviation; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about the rejected link, e.g. Each SSO link needs both a provider and an email.

apiMessages.accounts.sso_links_user_only.en: Only User accounts may have SSO links; this account is {{accountKind}}.
apiMessages.accounts.sso_links_user_only.context: Raised when a single sign-on link is added to an account that stands for a machine rather than a person; only accounts of the User kind can sign in interactively. 'User' here is the literal name of that account kind as shown in the console, and the inserted word arrives in English and names the kind this account actually has.

placeholders.accountKind: English name of the account kind, inserted untranslated, e.g. Application

apiMessages.accounts.sso_link_fields_req.en: Each SSO link requires both provider “{{provider}}” and email “{{email}}”.
apiMessages.accounts.sso_link_fields_req.context: Raised when a single sign-on link is saved with the sign-in provider or the address left blank; both are needed to match a person at sign-in. The words before the quotation marks name the two fields, and the quoted parts show whatever was entered, so at least one of them comes out empty.

placeholders.provider: Whatever was entered as the sign-in provider, often empty, e.g. Microsoft
placeholders.email: Whatever was entered as the address at that provider, often empty, e.g. jane@example.com

apiMessages.accounts.duplicate_sso_link.en: The SSO link for {{provider}} / {{email}} is duplicated.
apiMessages.accounts.duplicate_sso_link.context: Raised when the same provider-and-address pair is listed twice on one account, which adds nothing and is treated as a mistake. 'Duplicated' describes the repeated entry in the list being saved, not a copy stored elsewhere.

placeholders.provider: Name of the external sign-in provider, e.g. Microsoft
placeholders.email: Address at that provider, e.g. jane@example.com

apiMessages.accounts.sso_link_in_use.en: The {{provider}} identity “{{email}}” is already linked to another account.
apiMessages.accounts.sso_link_in_use.context: Raised when the external identity someone is linking already belongs to a different account; an identity may sign in as only one account. 'Identity' is the person's login at the external provider, so keep it distinct from the Ingest account itself.

placeholders.provider: Name of the external sign-in provider, e.g. Microsoft
placeholders.email: Address at that provider, e.g. jane@example.com

apiMessages.accounts.delete_in_use.en: Account “{{accountName}}” has submitted data and cannot be deleted. Disable it instead.
apiMessages.accounts.delete_in_use.context: Raised when an administrator tries to delete an account that has already filed data, which would leave that data without an owner. 'Disable it instead' is an imperative pointing to the alternative — switching the account off keeps its history and revokes access — and 'disable' must match the wording of that control elsewhere in the console.

placeholders.accountName: Unique name of the account, e.g. north-depot

apiMessages.accounts.api_key_description.en: The API key description is {{actualLength}} characters; the maximum is {{maxLength}}.
apiMessages.accounts.api_key_description.context: Raised when the free-text note attached to an API key exceeds the length the server stores. An API key is the secret credential used to call the interface, and its description is the label that helps an administrator recognise it later; both numbers count characters.

placeholders.actualLength: Number of characters that were entered, e.g. 312
placeholders.maxLength: Largest number of characters allowed, e.g. 200

apiMessages.accounts.api_key_expiry_not_.en: The API key expiry {{expiry}} must be later than {{now}}.
apiMessages.accounts.api_key_expiry_not_.context: Raised when an API key is given an expiry date that has already passed, which would make it useless the moment it is created. 'Expiry' is the moment the key stops working; both moments are technical UTC timestamps supplied by the server and are not reformatted.

placeholders.expiry: Expiry moment that was requested, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-01-01 00:00:00Z
placeholders.now: The server's current moment, in the same format, e.g. 2026-08-11 14:32:00Z

apiMessages.accounts.api_key_expiry_too_.en: The API key expiry {{expiry}} is more than {{maxLifetimeYears}} years after {{now}}.
apiMessages.accounts.api_key_expiry_too_.context: Raised when an API key is given an expiry so far ahead that it exceeds the maximum lifetime the server permits. The number of years is the configured cap, and both moments are technical UTC timestamps that stay exactly as they arrive.

placeholders.expiry: Expiry moment that was requested, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2036-08-11 00:00:00Z
placeholders.maxLifetimeYears: Greatest number of years a key may last, e.g. 5
placeholders.now: The server's current moment, in the same format, e.g. 2026-08-11 14:32:00Z

apiMessages.schemas.validation.context: Generic summary when a schema — the administrator-defined form definition that services fill in — was rejected on save and no more specific wording applies. Appears at the top of the red message bar in the schema editor, above the list of individual findings supplied by the server in English.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. Value 'tonnes collected' is not a valid identifier.

apiMessages.schemas.already_exists.context: Raised when a schema is created or renamed to a name another schema already holds; schema names are unique across the installation. The name shown is the machine name used in submissions and expressions, not the label shown on screen.

placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema, e.g. waste_collection

apiMessages.schemas.delete_in_use.en: Schema “{{schemaName}}” is used by submissions and cannot be deleted. Disable it instead.
apiMessages.schemas.delete_in_use.context: Raised when a schema that submissions already reference is deleted, which would leave that history unreadable. 'Disable it instead' is an imperative pointing to the alternative — a disabled schema stops accepting new data while its history stays browseable — and 'disable' must match the wording of that control in the schema editor.

placeholders.schemaName: Human label of the schema, falling back to its machine name, e.g. Waste collection

apiMessages.schemas.version_negative.en: Schema version {{version}} must be at least {{minimum}}.
apiMessages.schemas.version_negative.context: Raised when a schema is saved with a negative version number. The schema version is the counter an administrator raises when the form definition changes, so that older submissions stay tied to the shape they were filed under; it is not a product or file-format version.

placeholders.version: Version number that was entered, e.g. -1

apiMessages.schemas.version_decreased.en: Schema version cannot decrease from {{previousVersion}} to {{requestedVersion}}.
apiMessages.schemas.version_decreased.context: Raised when a schema is saved with a version lower than the one already stored; the counter may only move upwards so past submissions keep their meaning. 'Decrease' refers to the number going down, and both numbers are schema versions rather than product versions.

placeholders.previousVersion: Version currently stored for the schema, e.g. 4
placeholders.requestedVersion: Lower version that was submitted, e.g. 2

apiMessages.schemas.value_name_invalid.context: Raised when a field's machine name is not a plain identifier: it has to start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits and underscores, because rules and formulas refer to fields by that name. The pattern shown is a technical expression and must be passed through exactly, as must the rejected name.

placeholders.valueName: The rejected machine name of the field, exactly as entered, e.g. tonnes collected
placeholders.pattern: Technical pattern the name must satisfy, never translated, e.g. ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$

apiMessages.schemas.since_version_negati.en: Value “{{valueName}}” has sinceVersion {{sinceVersion}}; the minimum is {{minimum}}.
apiMessages.schemas.since_version_negati.context: Raised when a field says it first appeared in a negative schema version. 'sinceVersion' is the literal name of that setting in the schema editor and stays untranslated; it records the schema version from which the field is expected in submissions.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.sinceVersion: Value that was entered for the setting, e.g. -2

apiMessages.schemas.since_version_after_.en: Value “{{valueName}}” has sinceVersion {{sinceVersion}}, after schema version {{schemaVersion}}.
apiMessages.schemas.since_version_after_.context: Raised when a field claims to have appeared in a schema version later than the schema's own — a field cannot exist before the version that introduces it. Both numbers are schema versions, and 'sinceVersion' is the literal setting name from the schema editor.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.sinceVersion: Version recorded on the field, e.g. 7
placeholders.schemaVersion: Current version of the schema itself, e.g. 4

apiMessages.schemas.target_band_out_of_o.context: Raised when the target band that colours a figure green, amber or red is inconsistent, because its edges must rise from the lower amber bound through the green range to the upper amber bound. The two edge names are literal setting names from the schema editor and are never translated; 'above' here means numerically greater than.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.lowerBand: Literal name of the edge that must not be the greater one, never translated, e.g. AmberMin, GreenMin, GreenMax
placeholders.lowerValue: Number configured for that edge, e.g. 80
placeholders.upperBand: Literal name of the edge it is compared against, never translated, e.g. GreenMin, GreenMax, AmberMax
placeholders.upperValue: Number configured for that edge, e.g. 60

apiMessages.schemas.green_min_without_am.en: Value “{{valueName}}” sets GreenMin {{greenMin}} without an AmberMin.
apiMessages.schemas.green_min_without_am.context: Raised when a field defines the bottom of its ideal range without the acceptable bound that has to sit below it, which would leave the colouring undefined. Both names are literal setting names in the schema editor and must be left in English even though the sentence is translated.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.greenMin: Number configured as the bottom of the ideal range, e.g. 65

apiMessages.schemas.green_max_without_am.en: Value “{{valueName}}” sets GreenMax {{greenMax}} without an AmberMax.
apiMessages.schemas.green_max_without_am.context: Raised when a field defines the top of its ideal range without the acceptable bound that has to sit above it. Both names are literal setting names in the schema editor and stay in English; the number shown is what was configured.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.greenMax: Number configured as the top of the ideal range, e.g. 95

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_expressio.context: Raised when a field is marked as calculated but no formula was written for it. 'Calculated' means the server works the figure out from the other fields instead of anyone entering it, so an expression is what defines it.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_value_req.context: Raised when a calculated field is also marked as mandatory, which makes no sense because nobody fills it in — the server derives it. 'Required' is the name of that setting on the field, so the sentence is about a contradiction in the configuration.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_expressio.en: Expression for “{{valueName}}” has a syntax error at {{position}}: {{detail}}
apiMessages.schemas.calculated_expressio.context: Raised when the formula of a calculated field cannot be parsed, with the character offset at which the parser gave up. The position is counted in characters from the start of the formula, and the explanation after the colon comes from the expression engine in English.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.position: Character offset in the formula where parsing stopped, e.g. 14
placeholders.detail: Expression engine's own English explanation, e.g. Unexpected token ')'

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_expressio.en: Expression for “{{valueName}}” could not be analyzed: {{detail}}
apiMessages.schemas.calculated_expressio.context: Raised when the formula parses but the server cannot work out which fields it depends on, so it cannot be safely stored. 'Analysed' means inspected for its references; the technical explanation after the colon stays in English.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.detail: Expression engine's own English explanation, e.g. Unsupported function 'lookup'

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_self_refe.context: Raised when a calculated field's formula uses the field's own name, which could never be worked out. 'References itself' describes the formula pointing back at the field it defines.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_history_r.en: Expression for “{{valueName}}” cannot use history functions: {{functions}}.
apiMessages.schemas.calculated_history_r.context: Raised when the formula of a calculated field looks at figures from earlier reporting periods; a calculated field may only combine other fields of the same submission. The function names listed are literal names used in formulas and are never translated.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.functions: Comma-separated literal names of the history functions, never translated, e.g. latest, previous

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_unknown_i.context: Raised when a formula mentions a name that matches no field on the schema, most often a typing mistake or a field that was later renamed. 'Identifier' means the name as written in the formula and is reproduced exactly, including its spelling mistake.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field whose formula is at fault, e.g. recycling_rate
placeholders.identifier: The unrecognised name exactly as written in the formula, e.g. tonnes_recycld

apiMessages.schemas.calculated_dependenc.en: Calculated values contain a dependency cycle.
apiMessages.schemas.calculated_dependenc.context: Raised when calculated fields refer to one another in a loop, so none of them can be worked out first. 'Dependency cycle' describes that circular chain of formulas; the fix is to break the loop in the schema editor.

apiMessages.schemas.layout_depth_exceede.context: Raised when the sections of a schema's form layout are nested more deeply than allowed. 'Layout' is the arrangement of fields into sections on the form the service fills in, and 'depth' counts how many sections sit inside one another.

placeholders.actualDepth: Nesting level that was reached, e.g. 5

apiMessages.schemas.layout_value_name_mi.en: A layout value node is missing valueName.
apiMessages.schemas.layout_value_name_mi.context: Raised when the form layout contains a slot meant to place a field but no field was chosen for it. 'Value node' is one entry in the layout tree, and 'valueName' is the literal setting that says which field it shows — usually the result of an unfinished edit in the layout editor.

apiMessages.schemas.layout_unknown_value.context: Raised when the form layout places a field that the schema does not define, typically left behind after a field was renamed or removed. The name is reproduced exactly as it stands in the layout.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field the layout refers to, e.g. tonnes_collected

apiMessages.schemas.layout_duplicate_val.en: Value “{{valueName}}” appears more than once in the layout.
apiMessages.schemas.layout_duplicate_val.context: Raised when the same field is placed twice in the form layout, which would show two inputs for one figure. 'More than once' counts placements across the whole layout, including inside nested sections.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field placed twice, e.g. tonnes_collected

apiMessages.schemas.layout_section_capti.en: A layout section is missing its caption.
apiMessages.schemas.layout_section_capti.context: Raised when a section of the form layout has no heading text, leaving an unlabelled group of fields on the form. 'Caption' is the heading shown above the grouped fields, and it is the name of that setting in the layout editor.

apiMessages.schemas.layout_unknown_kind.context: Raised when an entry in the form layout is of a type the server does not know; a layout entry either places a field or opens a section. Both the rejected type and the two permitted ones arrive as literal English type names and must be left untranslated.

placeholders.actualKind: Literal type name found in the layout, never translated, e.g. Group
placeholders.expectedKinds: Comma-separated literal type names that are allowed, never translated, e.g. Value, Section

apiMessages.reports.validation.context: Generic summary when a report was rejected and no more specific wording applies. A report is an administrator-authored template that is filled with submitted data and rendered for reading; the server's own English detail follows the sentence.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. Report content is empty.

apiMessages.reports.already_exists.context: Raised when a report is uploaded under a name another report already holds; report names are unique. The name comes either from the template's own metadata or from the uploaded file's name.

placeholders.reportName: Unique name of the report, e.g. monthly-waste-summary

apiMessages.reports.missing_upload.en: Upload a non-empty file in the “{{field}}” field.
apiMessages.reports.missing_upload.context: Raised when a report upload arrives with no file attached or with an empty one. 'Upload' is an imperative instruction to the reader, and the quoted name is the literal name of the upload field in the request, so it stays untranslated.

placeholders.field: Literal name of the upload field in the request, never translated, e.g. file

apiMessages.reports.content_empty.en: Report content must not be empty.
apiMessages.reports.content_empty.context: Raised when the uploaded report template has no content, so there is nothing to store or render. 'Content' means the text of the template file itself.

apiMessages.reports.name_required.en: A report name is required; file “{{fileName}}” did not provide one.
apiMessages.reports.name_required.context: Raised when a report has no usable name: the template's metadata block gave none and the file name could not stand in for one. Names the offending file so the administrator knows which upload to fix.

placeholders.fileName: Name of the uploaded file, exactly as it arrived, e.g. .md

apiMessages.reports.date_range_invalid.en: Report start {{from}} must not be after end {{to}}.
apiMessages.reports.date_range_invalid.context: Raised when the period chosen for a report has its start after its end. 'Start' and 'end' are the two ends of the date range picked in the report viewer; both moments arrive already formatted by the server and are not reformatted here.

placeholders.from: Start of the chosen range, as a technical UTC timestamp, e.g. 2026-08-01 00:00:00Z
placeholders.to: End of the chosen range, in the same format, e.g. 2026-07-01 00:00:00Z

apiMessages.reports.type_unsupported.context: Raised when a report declares a kind the server cannot render; a report either covers one submission or aggregates many. The kind arrives as a literal English name and is left as it is, matching what the report editor shows.

placeholders.reportType: Literal English name of the report kind, never translated, e.g. Single, Aggregate

apiMessages.reports.schema_not_target.en: Schema “{{schemaName}}” is not a target of report “{{reportName}}”. Targets: {{targetSchemaNames}}.
apiMessages.reports.schema_not_target.context: Raised when a report is rendered for a schema it was not written for. 'Targets' are the schemas the report declares it covers, listed after the colon by machine name; all of the names stay untranslated.

placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema that was asked for, e.g. water_quality
placeholders.reportName: Name of the report, e.g. monthly-waste-summary
placeholders.targetSchemaNames: Comma-separated machine names of the schemas the report covers, e.g. waste_collection, waste_transfer

apiMessages.reports.schema_required_for_.context: Raised when a report covers several schemas, so the server cannot guess which one to render and needs to be told. The quoted name is the literal request parameter to supply, and the listed schema names are machine names; 'provide' is an imperative addressed to the reader.

placeholders.reportName: Name of the report, e.g. monthly-waste-summary
placeholders.targetSchemaNames: Comma-separated machine names of the schemas the report covers, e.g. waste_collection, waste_transfer
placeholders.parameter: Literal name of the parameter that must be supplied, never translated, e.g. schemaName

apiMessages.reports.submission_id_requir.context: Raised when a report that describes one single submission is rendered without saying which submission to use. The quoted name is the literal request parameter, so it stays exactly as it arrives.

placeholders.reportName: Name of the report, e.g. single-return-detail
placeholders.parameter: Literal name of the parameter that must be supplied, never translated, e.g. submissionId

apiMessages.reports.submission_schema_mi.en: Submission {{submissionId}} has no samples for schema “{{schemaName}}”.
apiMessages.reports.submission_schema_mi.context: Raised when the chosen submission holds no readings for the schema the report is scoped to, so the report would have nothing to show. 'Samples' are the individual readings inside a submission; the identifier is technical and untranslated.

placeholders.submissionId: Technical identifier of the submission, e.g. 8a2d51c7-9f04-4b6e-a3d1-77c0e9b5a412
placeholders.schemaName: Machine name of the schema the report is scoped to, e.g. waste_collection

apiMessages.reports.aggregate_schema_req.context: Raised when a report that summarises many submissions is rendered without a schema to summarise. 'Aggregate' describes that kind of report — figures combined across submissions — and the quoted name is the literal request parameter.

placeholders.reportName: Name of the report, e.g. monthly-waste-summary
placeholders.parameter: Literal name of the parameter that must be supplied, never translated, e.g. schemaName

apiMessages.reports.front_matter_unclose.en: Report front matter opens with “---” but never closes.
apiMessages.reports.front_matter_unclose.context: Raised when the metadata block at the top of a report template is opened but never closed again, so the whole file would be read as metadata. 'Front matter' is that block of settings above the template body, and the three dashes are literal characters that must appear unchanged in the translation.

apiMessages.reports.front_matter_line_in.context: Raised for one line of a report template's metadata block that is neither a comment nor a setting written as name and value separated by a colon. The line number counts from the start of the metadata block, and the offending line is reproduced verbatim after the colon.

placeholders.lineNumber: Position of the line within the metadata block, counted from 1, e.g. 3
placeholders.line: The offending line reproduced exactly as written, e.g. aggregate report

apiMessages.reports.front_matter_type_in.context: Raised when the metadata block of a report template names a report kind the server does not know. Both the rejected word and the permitted ones are literal English names that stay untranslated; 'type' is the literal setting name in the metadata block.

placeholders.actualType: The rejected value exactly as written in the template, e.g. summary
placeholders.allowedTypes: Comma-separated literal names that are accepted, never translated, e.g. Single, Aggregate

apiMessages.reports.front_matter_inline_.context: Raised when a list written on one line in a report template's metadata block is not enclosed in square brackets. The expected wrapper is shown as literal characters and both inserted parts must be passed through exactly as they arrive.

placeholders.value: The list exactly as written in the template, e.g. waste_collection, waste_transfer
placeholders.expectedWrapper: Literal notation the list must use, never translated, e.g. [..]

apiMessages.reports.template_parse_faile.context: Raised when the report template itself cannot be read by the template language, so nothing could be rendered. The engine name is a product name and is never translated; the explanation after the colon is the engine's own English message.

placeholders.engine: Name of the template language, never translated, e.g. Liquid
placeholders.detail: The engine's own English explanation, e.g. Unexpected tag 'endfor' at line 12

apiMessages.reports.template_render_fail.context: Raised when a report template is well-formed but failed while being filled with data — a missing field or a division by zero, for instance. 'Rendering' is the act of producing the finished report; the engine name and the explanation after the colon stay in English.

placeholders.engine: Name of the template language, never translated, e.g. Liquid
placeholders.detail: The engine's own English explanation, e.g. Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'schema')

apiMessages.expressions.empty.en: The expression must not be empty.
apiMessages.expressions.empty.context: Raised when the schema editor asks the server to check or translate a formula and nothing was typed. 'Expression' is the formula an administrator writes for a calculated field or a rule, in the product's own small formula language; the message appears beside the formula box.

apiMessages.expressions.too_long.context: Raised when a formula is longer than the server accepts, so it is refused before being checked. The limit counts characters; the number and the word for characters form one compound in English, which most languages will need to reword.

placeholders.maxLength: Greatest number of characters a formula may have, e.g. 2000

apiMessages.expressions.parse_failed.en: The expression could not be parsed: {{detail}}
apiMessages.expressions.parse_failed.context: Raised when a formula cannot be understood by the expression engine, usually a typing slip such as an unbalanced bracket. Shown next to the formula box while the administrator is still editing, so it reads as feedback rather than a failure of the product; the explanation after the colon is the engine's own English text.

placeholders.detail: The expression engine's own English explanation, often with a position, e.g. Unexpected token ')' at position 14

apiMessages.expressions.unsupported_targ.context: Raised when a formula is asked to be translated into an output form the server cannot produce; it can render a formula as browser code or as a plain-English reading. 'Target' means that requested output form and arrives as a technical identifier, so it is never translated.
