placeholders.target: Technical identifier of the requested output form, never translated, e.g. text/javascript

apiMessages.expressions.batch_missing.context: Raised when the schema editor asks the server to analyse a whole set of formulas at once but sends no set at all. 'Batch' is that group of formulas submitted together; an empty group is fine, a missing one is not. This points at a product fault rather than anything the administrator did.

apiMessages.expressions.batch_too_large.context: Raised when too many formulas are sent to be analysed in one go. 'Batch' is the group submitted together and the limit counts formulas, not characters; the number and the following words form one compound in English that will usually need rewording.

placeholders.maxCount: Greatest number of formulas allowed in one group, e.g. 200

apiMessages.configuration.validation.context: Generic summary when server-wide settings were rejected on save and no more specific wording applies. 'Configuration' means those installation-wide settings, not the act of configuring; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. The backup file is empty.

apiMessages.configuration.backup_empty.context: Raised while restoring a full backup — the export that carries both collected data and settings — when the chosen file has no content. Shown in the red message bar on the maintenance screen; keep it distinct from the wording used for the settings-only backup, which is a separate download.

apiMessages.configuration.backup_invalid.en: The backup file is not valid JSON: {{detail}}
apiMessages.configuration.backup_invalid.context: Raised while restoring a full backup when the file is not well-formed JSON, so nothing could be read from it. The parser's explanation after the colon stays in English; the wording must remain distinguishable from the settings-only backup equivalent.

placeholders.detail: Parser's own English explanation, e.g. Invalid JSON input: expected ':' at position 214

apiMessages.configuration.backup_invalid.en: This is not an Ingest backup (expected “{{expectedFormat}}”, received “{{actualFormat}}”).
apiMessages.configuration.backup_invalid.context: Raised while restoring a full backup when the file does not carry the tag that identifies it as one — usually the wrong file, or a settings-only backup chosen by mistake. 'Ingest' is the product name, and both quoted tags are literal machine words that are never translated; the second one comes out empty when the file has no tag at all.

placeholders.expectedFormat: Literal tag the file must carry, never translated, e.g. ingest-backup
placeholders.actualFormat: Literal tag actually found in the file, empty when there is none, e.g. ingest-config

apiMessages.configuration.backup_unsuppo.en: Backup version {{version}} is unsupported; maximum supported version is {{maximumVersion}}.
apiMessages.configuration.backup_unsuppo.context: Raised while restoring a full backup written in a newer file-format version than this server can read. Both numbers refer to the backup file format, not to the product release; the practical answer is to restore on a server of the same or a newer release.

placeholders.version: Format version found in the file, e.g. 3
placeholders.maximumVersion: Highest format version this server reads, e.g. 2

apiMessages.configuration.backup_missing.en: The backup file has no collections section.
apiMessages.configuration.backup_missing.context: Raised while restoring a full backup whose contents section is absent, so the file is structurally valid but holds nothing to restore. 'Collections' is the literal name of that part of the file, where the stored records are grouped by kind, so keep it recognisable rather than paraphrasing it as 'data'.

apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.en: The configuration backup file is empty.
apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.context: Raised while restoring a settings-only backup — the export that carries schemas, accounts and settings but no collected data — when the chosen file has no content. Must stay distinguishable from the full-backup wording, since the maintenance screen offers both restores side by side.

apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.en: The configuration backup file is not valid JSON: {{detail}}
apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.context: Raised while restoring a settings-only backup when the file is not well-formed JSON. The parser's explanation after the colon stays in English, and the sentence must read differently from the full-backup equivalent so an administrator can tell which restore failed.

placeholders.detail: Parser's own English explanation, e.g. Invalid JSON input: expected ':' at position 214

apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.en: This is not an Ingest configuration backup (expected “{{expectedFormat}}”, received “{{actualFormat}}”).
apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.context: Raised while restoring a settings-only backup when the file does not carry the tag that identifies it as one — most often a full backup picked by mistake. 'Ingest' is the product name; both quoted tags are literal machine words that stay untranslated, and the second is empty when the file carries no tag.

placeholders.expectedFormat: Literal tag the file must carry, never translated, e.g. ingest-config
placeholders.actualFormat: Literal tag actually found in the file, empty when there is none, e.g. ingest-backup

apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.en: Configuration backup version {{version}} is unsupported; maximum supported version is {{maximumVersion}}.
apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.context: Raised while restoring a settings-only backup written in a newer file-format version than this server understands. Both numbers are versions of the backup file format rather than product releases.

placeholders.version: Format version found in the file, e.g. 3
placeholders.maximumVersion: Highest format version this server reads, e.g. 2

apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.en: The configuration backup file has no collections section.
apiMessages.configuration.config_backup_.context: Raised while restoring a settings-only backup whose contents section is absent, so there is nothing to put back. 'Collections' is the literal name of the part of the file where records are grouped by kind; keep the sentence distinguishable from the full-backup equivalent.

apiMessages.comments.validation.context: Generic summary when a comment could not be saved and no more specific wording applies. Comments are discussion threads administrators attach to a schema or to one of its fields; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. Comment text is required.

apiMessages.comments.thread_resolved.en: This thread is resolved. Reopen it before adding a comment.
apiMessages.comments.thread_resolved.context: Raised when someone replies to a discussion thread that has been marked as settled; a settled thread accepts no further replies until it is opened again. 'Resolved' is the state shown on the thread's badge and 'Reopen' is an imperative naming the button that undoes it, so both must match those labels.

apiMessages.comments.edit_forbidden.en: You can only edit your own comments.
apiMessages.comments.edit_forbidden.context: Raised when an administrator without the manage-any-comment permission edits someone else's comment. Addresses the reader in the second person; 'your own' refers to comments the reader wrote themselves.

apiMessages.comments.value_not_on_schema.context: Raised when a comment thread is attached to a field that the given schema does not define, usually because the field was renamed or removed after the thread was started. Both inserted parts are machine-supplied — the field's machine name and the schema's technical identifier.

placeholders.valueName: Machine name of the field the comment points at, e.g. tonnes_collected
placeholders.schemaId: Technical identifier of the schema, e.g. 5b1e7a30-2c44-4f8d-9e61-0a7b3d5c8f21

apiMessages.comments.target_type_unsuppo.en: Comment target type “{{targetType}}” is unsupported for target {{targetId}}.
apiMessages.comments.target_type_unsuppo.context: Raised when a comment thread is attached to a kind of record that cannot carry comments; today only schemas and their fields can. 'Target' is the record the thread hangs from, and its kind arrives as a literal English name that stays untranslated.

placeholders.targetType: Literal English name of the record kind, never translated, e.g. Submission
placeholders.targetId: Technical identifier of the record, e.g. 5b1e7a30-2c44-4f8d-9e61-0a7b3d5c8f21

apiMessages.comments.text_required.context: Raised when a comment is saved with nothing in it, or with only spaces. 'Text' means the body the reader typed into the comment box; states the rule plainly without instructing the reader.

apiMessages.comments.text_too_long.en: Comment text is {{actualLength}} characters; the maximum is {{maxLength}}.
apiMessages.comments.text_too_long.context: Raised when a comment is longer than the server stores. Both numbers count characters, not words; the sentence reports what was typed first and the limit second.

placeholders.actualLength: Number of characters that were typed, e.g. 4200
placeholders.maxLength: Largest number of characters allowed, e.g. 4000

apiMessages.events.validation.context: Generic summary when an event could not be saved and no more specific wording applies. An event is an occurrence an administrator records — a maintenance window, an incident, a deployment — which is then shown alongside the data on charts; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. Timestamp is required.

apiMessages.events.label_required.context: Raised when an event is saved without its short name. 'Label' is the name shown for the event on charts and in the event list, and it is the literal name of that field in the form.

apiMessages.events.timestamp_required.context: Raised when an event is saved without the moment it happened. 'Timestamp' is the date and time of the occurrence, the field the event is positioned by on charts.

apiMessages.events.interval_duration_req.en: A positive duration “{{duration}}” is required for {{eventKind}} events.
apiMessages.events.interval_duration_req.context: Raised when an event that spans a stretch of time is saved without a length, or with a length of zero or less. 'Duration' is how long the event lasted; the quoted part shows what was entered, so it is often empty, and the event kind arrives as a literal English name that stays untranslated.

placeholders.duration: Length that was entered, often empty or zero, e.g. 02:00:00
placeholders.eventKind: Literal English name of the event kind, never translated, e.g. Interval

apiMessages.events.invalid_service_ids.en: Affected service IDs must identify existing services: {{serviceIds}}.
apiMessages.events.invalid_service_ids.context: Raised when the list of services an event applies to names something that is not an existing service; leaving the list empty means the event affects all of them. A service is the organisational unit that submits data, and the identifiers shown are technical ids.

placeholders.serviceIds: Comma-separated technical identifiers that could not be matched to a service, e.g. 7c1f0b42-5a9d-4e31-9a10-2f6b8c4d5e77

apiMessages.approval.validation.context: Generic summary when an approval policy or an approval decision was rejected and no more specific wording applies. Approval is the sign-off step in which named accounts accept a submission before it counts; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. At least one approver is required when approval is required.

apiMessages.approval.global_default_not_.en: Approval mode “{{mode}}” cannot defer to the global default here.
apiMessages.approval.global_default_not_.context: Raised when a policy is set to fall back to the installation-wide default in a place where that is meaningless — the default policy itself cannot defer to itself. 'Mode' is the setting that says whether approval is off, required, or inherited, and its value arrives as a literal English name that is never translated.

placeholders.mode: Literal English name of the approval mode, never translated, e.g. UseGlobalDefault

apiMessages.approval.approver_required.en: At least one approver is required.
apiMessages.approval.approver_required.context: Raised when a policy demands approval but names nobody to give it. An approver is an account that signs off submissions; the sentence states the rule rather than telling the reader what to click.

apiMessages.approval.required_approver_r.en: At least one approver must be marked required.
apiMessages.approval.required_approver_r.context: Raised when every approver on a policy is optional, so no sign-off would ever be compulsory. 'Marked required' refers to the per-approver setting that makes that person's sign-off mandatory, as opposed to merely inviting them to review.

apiMessages.approval.duplicate_service_o.en: The service owner is listed more than once.
apiMessages.approval.duplicate_service_o.context: Raised when the approver list contains the service owner entry twice. The service owner is a special approver that resolves, for each submission, to whoever owns the submitting service, so listing it twice adds nothing.

apiMessages.approval.duplicate_approver.en: Approver account {{accountId}} is listed more than once.
apiMessages.approval.duplicate_approver.context: Raised when the same account appears twice in a policy's approver list. 'Listed more than once' is about the list being saved; the identifier shown is a technical id rather than the person's name.

placeholders.accountId: Technical identifier of the repeated account, e.g. 4d9b21ac-7e35-42f0-8c19-b6f5a0d3e714

apiMessages.approval.approver_not_found.context: Raised when a policy names an approver account that no longer exists, typically after the account was deleted. 'Does not exist' is a statement about the account, not about permissions.

placeholders.accountId: Technical identifier of the missing account, e.g. 4d9b21ac-7e35-42f0-8c19-b6f5a0d3e714

apiMessages.approval.not_designated_appr.en: Account {{approverAccountId}} is not a designated approver for submission {{submissionId}}.
apiMessages.approval.not_designated_appr.context: Raised when an account records an approve or reject decision for a submission it was not named to sign off; administrators may always decide, so this is reported for everyone else. 'Designated approver' means named in the approval policy for that particular submission; both identifiers are technical ids.

placeholders.approverAccountId: Technical identifier of the account attempting the decision, e.g. 4d9b21ac-7e35-42f0-8c19-b6f5a0d3e714
placeholders.submissionId: Technical identifier of the submission, e.g. 8a2d51c7-9f04-4b6e-a3d1-77c0e9b5a412

apiMessages.integrations.validation.context: Generic summary when an integration could not be saved and no more specific wording applies. An integration is an outbound connection that prompts a Microsoft Teams user or channel about data that is still outstanding; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. Schedule hour must be between 0 and 23.

apiMessages.integrations.connection_fail.context: Reported in the message bar after an administrator tests the stored Microsoft Teams credentials and the sign-in attempt fails. Names an infrastructure or credential problem rather than a mistake in the form just filled in; the explanation after the colon comes from the identity provider in English.

placeholders.detail: The provider's own English explanation, e.g. AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided

apiMessages.integrations.schedule_hour_i.en: Schedule hour {{hourUtc}} must be between {{minimum}} and {{maximum}} UTC.
apiMessages.integrations.schedule_hour_i.context: Raised when the hour at which an integration is due to run is outside the 24-hour clock. 'Schedule' is the recurring plan for when the prompt is sent, and UTC is kept as the English abbreviation for coordinated universal time, since the hour is stored in that zone rather than the reader's.

apiMessages.integrations.schedule_minute.en: Schedule minute {{minuteUtc}} must be between {{minimum}} and {{maximum}}.
apiMessages.integrations.schedule_minute.context: Raised when the minute at which an integration is due to run is outside the range of an hour. 'Schedule' is the recurring plan for when the prompt is sent; the minute is stored in coordinated universal time like the hour beside it.

apiMessages.integrations.schedule_day_in.en: Day {{dayOfMonth}} for {{frequency}} schedules must be between {{minimum}} and {{maximum}}.
apiMessages.integrations.schedule_day_in.context: Raised when the day of the month chosen for a recurring integration is not a possible calendar day. 'Day' means day of the month here, and the frequency word arrives as a literal English name from the schedule editor that stays untranslated.

placeholders.frequency: Literal English name of the recurrence, never translated, e.g. Monthly, Quarterly, SemiAnnually, Yearly

apiMessages.integrations.schedule_anchor.en: Anchor month {{anchorMonth}} for {{frequency}} schedules must be between {{minimum}} and {{maximum}}.
apiMessages.integrations.schedule_anchor.context: Raised when the month that fixes where a multi-month cycle starts is not a real month. 'Anchor month' is the reference month from which quarterly, half-yearly or yearly runs are counted; the frequency word is a literal English name and stays as it is.

placeholders.anchorMonth: Month number that was entered, e.g. 14
placeholders.frequency: Literal English name of the recurrence, never translated, e.g. Quarterly, SemiAnnually, Yearly

apiMessages.integrations.teams_target_re.en: A Teams {{targetKind}} target is required for {{integrationKind}}.
apiMessages.integrations.teams_target_re.context: Raised when a Microsoft Teams integration is saved without saying who or where to send the prompt to. 'Teams' is the Microsoft product name and 'target' is the chosen recipient — a person or a channel — and both inserted names arrive as literal English words that are never translated; the recipient kind comes out empty when none was chosen.

placeholders.targetKind: Literal English name of the recipient kind, empty when none was chosen, e.g. Channel, User
placeholders.integrationKind: Literal English name of the integration kind, never translated, e.g. MicrosoftTeams

apiMessages.webhooks.validation.context: Generic summary when a webhook endpoint could not be saved and no more specific wording applies. A webhook is an address on another system that this server calls whenever a chosen event happens; the server's own English detail follows.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. URL is required.

apiMessages.webhooks.delivery_failed.context: Explains why one attempted call to an outside system did not get through. Appears as hover text on the red status badge of a row in the delivery log, so it stays on one line and describes the receiving end's response, which follows in the server's own English.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about the failed attempt, e.g. Connection timed out after 10000ms

apiMessages.webhooks.name_required.context: Raised when a webhook endpoint is saved without a name. The name is only there to help administrators recognise the endpoint in the list; it is the literal name of that field in the form.

apiMessages.webhooks.url_required.context: Raised when a webhook endpoint is saved without the web address to call. Most locales keep 'URL' as the English abbreviation; it must match the label of that field in the form.

apiMessages.webhooks.url_invalid.en: Webhook URL “{{url}}” must be absolute and use one of: {{allowedSchemes}}.
apiMessages.webhooks.url_invalid.context: Raised when the address entered for a webhook is not a complete web address, or uses a protocol the server will not call. 'Absolute' means the address includes its protocol and host rather than being a fragment; the address and the listed protocol names are shown verbatim and are never translated.

placeholders.url: The address exactly as it was entered, e.g. example.com/hooks/ingest
placeholders.allowedSchemes: Comma-separated protocol names that are accepted, never translated, e.g. http, https

apiMessages.email.validation.context: Generic summary when e-mail settings, a template or an outgoing message were rejected and no more specific wording applies. The server's own English detail follows the sentence.

placeholders.message: The server's own English detail about what was rejected, e.g. SMTP host is required.

apiMessages.email.delivery_failed.context: Explains why an outgoing message could not be handed over to the mail server. Appears as hover text on the red status badge of a row in the outgoing-mail log, so keep it to one line; the mail server's own English response follows.

placeholders.message: The mail server's own English response or error text, e.g. 550 5.1.1 Recipient address rejected

apiMessages.email.address_invalid.en: “{{address}}” is not a valid email address.
apiMessages.email.address_invalid.context: Raised when an address entered for outgoing mail — the sender in the settings, or a recipient of a message — is not usable. The quoted text is reproduced exactly as typed, including the mistake, so it must not be tidied up in the translation.

placeholders.address: The address exactly as it was entered, e.g. reports@@example.com

apiMessages.email.subject_required.context: Raised when an e-mail is composed or a template saved with an empty subject line. 'Subject' is the heading line of the message, matching the label of that field in the form; a near-identical sentence exists for the outgoing queue, and the two should read consistently.

apiMessages.email.email_subject_required.context: Raised by the outgoing-mail queue when a message reaches it with no subject line, which is a fault upstream rather than something typed in a form. 'Subject' is the heading line of the message; keep the wording in step with the plain subject-required sentence used by the forms.

apiMessages.email.text_body_required.context: Raised when an e-mail template is saved without its plain-text body. Every template needs a plain-text version for readers whose mail client shows no formatting; the formatted version beside it is optional, so 'text body' names that specific field and must match its label.

apiMessages.email.template_parse_failed.en: {{engine}} template field “{{field}}” could not be parsed: {{detail}}
apiMessages.email.template_parse_failed.context: Raised when one field of an e-mail template contains markup the template language cannot read, so the template cannot be saved. The engine name is a product name and the field name arrives in English matching the label in the template editor, so both stay untranslated, as does the explanation after the colon.

placeholders.engine: Name of the template language, never translated, e.g. Liquid
placeholders.field: English name of the template field at fault, matching its label in the editor, e.g. Subject, Text body, HTML body
placeholders.detail: The engine's own English explanation, e.g. Unexpected tag 'endif' at line 4

apiMessages.email.smtp_host_required.context: Raised when the outgoing-mail settings are saved without the address of the mail server. SMTP is kept as the English abbreviation, and 'host' means the machine name or address of that server rather than a person; both must match the field's label.

apiMessages.email.smtp_port_invalid.en: SMTP port {{port}} must be between {{minimum}} and {{maximum}}.
apiMessages.email.smtp_port_invalid.context: Raised when the network port entered for the mail server is outside the usable range. 'Port' is the numbered network endpoint on the mail server, nothing to do with a harbour, and SMTP stays as the English abbreviation.

placeholders.port: Port number that was entered, e.g. 70000

apiMessages.email.from_address_required.context: Raised when the outgoing-mail settings are saved without the address that messages will be sent from. 'From address' is the sender shown to recipients and is the label of that field in the settings, so keep the two consistent.

apiMessages.email.account_contact_missin.context: Raised when an administrator sends a message to an account that has no contact address on file, so there is nowhere to send it. The remedy is to add an address to the account first; the name is the account's unique name and the bracketed identifier is its technical id.

placeholders.accountName: Unique name of the account, e.g. north-depot
placeholders.accountId: Technical identifier of the account, e.g. 4d9b21ac-7e35-42f0-8c19-b6f5a0d3e714

settings.title.context: Heading at the very top of the whole settings screen, above the list of configuration panels on the left. Plural noun naming the configuration area of the console, never a verb.

settings.general.navigationLabel.context: Entry in the left-hand list of settings panels; it opens the console preferences (display language and colour scheme). General in the sense of overall or miscellaneous. Short noun phrase, no period, in a narrow column beside an icon.

settings.general.navigationGroup.context: Heading above the group of navigation entries that the console preferences belong to; the stylesheet renders it in small capitals. Same word and same sense as the navigation entry it heads, so keep the two identical.

settings.general.title.context: Heading of the card holding the console preferences, shown once that panel is selected. Matches the wording of its navigation entry, so translate both the same way.

settings.general.description.context: Sentence under the General heading saying what the card is for. Preferences here are per-user choices about how the console looks, not deployment settings; console means this web administration interface.

settings.general.language.context: Labels the dropdown that switches the language of the console interface. The choices themselves are language names written in their own language and are never translated.

settings.general.theme.context: Labels the dropdown that chooses the colour scheme of the console. Theme in the visual-appearance sense, not a subject or topic.

settings.general.lightTheme.context: The only choice in the colour-scheme dropdown, and the text shown in the closed dropdown once chosen: the bright-background scheme. Adjective describing the appearance, not weight and not illumination.

settings.permissionDenied.en: You don't have permission to manage any settings.
settings.permissionDenied.context: Red message bar shown in place of the entire settings screen to a signed-in administrator whose account may not view or change any of the panels. Second person, full sentence; 'any' means not even one panel is available.

settings.noneEnabled.en: No configurable settings are enabled. Turn on email, webhooks, integrations, or the approval workflow in the server configuration to manage them here.
settings.noneEnabled.context: Shown in place of the settings screen when every optional subsystem is switched off on the server, so no panel would have anything to configure. The second sentence tells the reader to enable those features in the server's own configuration, which is edited outside this console; second person, and the named features are product feature names.

settings.navigation.areas.context: Entry in the left-hand list of settings panels; it opens the panel for the optional grouping tags that can be attached to accounts. Area means an organisational or geographic unit, never a surface, a subject area, or a region of the screen. Keep it identical to that panel's own heading.

settings.navigation.configuration.context: Heading above the group of navigation entries holding deployment-wide options (areas, submission periods, ingestion); rendered in small capitals by the stylesheet. Names a category of settings, so keep it a noun.

settings.navigation.submissionPeriods.context: Entry opening the panel where the boundaries of reporting periods are set. A period is a reporting window such as a day, week, month or quarter; a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for such a period. Keep it identical to that panel's heading.

settings.navigation.ingestion.context: Entry opening the panel that can stop the product accepting incoming data. Ingest is the product's word for taking data in, so use the same term you use for it elsewhere; keep it identical to that panel's heading.

settings.navigation.approval.context: Entry opening the panel with the deployment-wide default policy for signing off submissions. Approval is the act of an approver accepting a submission; singular here because one policy is configured.

settings.navigation.approvals.context: Heading above the group of navigation entries about sign-off (the default policy and its per-service exceptions); rendered in small capitals. Plural noun naming the category.

settings.navigation.rules.context: Entry opening the list of exceptions to the default approval policy, each one scoped to particular services or schemas. Rule means an administrator-defined override, not a regulation or a ruler.

settings.navigation.email.context: Entry opening the panel with the outgoing mail server details the product uses to send messages. Short noun, no period.

settings.navigation.emailTemplates.context: Entry opening the editable bodies of the messages the product sends. A template is a reusable message text with placeholders filled in at send time. Tight on space in a narrow column.

settings.navigation.notifications.context: Entry opening the panel with the rules for the reminders and alerts the product sends, and also the small-capitals heading above the whole group of mail-related entries. One translation serves both, so keep it a short plural noun.

settings.navigation.webhooks.context: Entry opening the list of HTTP endpoints the product posts events to. Webhook is a technical term the administrators reading this already know; leave it in English unless the target language has an established equivalent.

settings.navigation.integrations.context: Heading above the group of navigation entries for outbound connections to other systems (webhooks and Microsoft Teams); rendered in small capitals. Plural noun naming the category.

settings.navigation.teamsNotifications.context: Entry opening the panel that configures reminders sent through Microsoft Teams. Teams is the Microsoft product name and stays in English; the rest must stay short in a narrow column.

settings.navigation.teamsConnection.context: Entry opening the panel holding the credentials that let the product talk to Microsoft Teams. Connection means that stored link and its credentials, not an active network session.

settings.common.loading.context: Caption beside a spinner, or the single placeholder row of a table, while a settings panel waits for data from the server. Present progressive with a trailing ellipsis; it reports normal waiting, not a problem.

settings.common.saving.context: Replaces the Save caption while a settings panel's write to the server is in flight. Saving means writing to storage, never the financial sense of putting money aside, and it must fit the same button as the resting caption.

settings.common.save.context: Resting caption of the primary button that writes a settings panel's changes to the server. Imperative, in the sense of storing the values, never of economising or setting aside; it is swapped for the in-flight variant during the write, so keep the two about the same width.

settings.common.saveChanges.context: Primary button that commits the edits made in the side panel of an existing rule, webhook or integration. Imperative store, not economise; changes means the edits just made in the form. Also swapped for the in-flight saving caption.

settings.common.add.context: Small button beside the area text box that appends what was typed to the list above it. Imperative; it only adds the entry on screen, nothing reaches the server until the primary save button is pressed.

settings.common.cancel.context: Secondary button that closes an editing side panel and discards what was typed. Imperative; it abandons the edit rather than stopping a running operation.

settings.common.done.context: Closes the dialog that reveals a newly generated webhook secret, once the reader has copied it. Acknowledges that the reader has finished; not a report that the product completed something.

settings.common.refresh.context: Row in the More actions menu above the rules, webhooks and integrations lists, and the caption of a small button above the current-periods table; it re-reads the data from the server. Imperative; it reloads what is displayed and changes nothing.

settings.common.moreActions.context: Announced by screen readers for the icon-only button above a list that opens a short menu of extra commands. Names what the button does; never abbreviated and never shown on screen.

settings.common.actions.context: Accessible name of the narrow, visually empty table column that holds each row's command menu. Plural noun; announced by screen readers only.

settings.common.edit.context: Row in a table row's command menu that opens the selected record in a side panel for changing. Imperative verb, in the sense of modifying an existing record.

settings.common.delete.context: Row in a table row's command menu that permanently removes the record, after a confirmation prompt. Imperative; keep it the destructive, unambiguous word for removing something for good.

settings.common.enable.context: Row in a table row's command menu that switches a currently inactive rule, webhook or integration back on. Imperative command, not an infinitive; it alternates in the same menu slot with the disable caption, so the two should read as a matched pair.

settings.common.disable.context: Row in a table row's command menu that switches an active rule, webhook or integration off without deleting it. Imperative command, not an infinitive; it alternates in the same menu slot with the enable caption.

settings.common.enabled.context: Pill in the Status column of the rules, webhooks and integrations tables, and the label of the on/off switch inside their editing panels. An adjective describing the record's current state, never a command; one or two words, because the badge does not wrap.

settings.common.disabled.context: Pill in the Status column marking a record that exists but is switched off. Adjective describing the state, the counterpart of the enabled badge; one or two words, badges do not wrap.

settings.common.configured.context: Pill after the introductory text of the mail-server and Teams-connection panels, saying that the credentials have already been filled in. Adjective describing the state of the setup; keep it to one or two words.

settings.common.notConfigured.context: Pill after the introductory text of the mail-server and Teams-connection panels, saying that the credentials are still missing. Adjective, the counterpart of the configured badge; it is a warning about setup, not an error.

settings.common.label.context: Header of the first column of the rules and integrations tables, and the label of the optional-name box in their editing panels. Noun for the short display name an administrator gives a record; not the verb, and not a physical tag.

settings.common.status.context: Header of the narrow column holding the enabled or disabled pill of each row. Very short noun; the column is only wide enough for one badge.

settings.common.services.context: Header of the column listing which services a rule or integration applies to, and the label of the same field in the editing panel. A service is an organisational unit that submits data, not a background process and not a commercial offering.

settings.common.schemas.context: Header of the column listing which schemas a rule or integration applies to, and the label of the same field in the editing panel. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition that services fill in for each period.

settings.common.allServices.context: Label of the checkbox meaning the rule or integration is not restricted to particular services; it also names the unrestricted choice in the webhook service dropdown, and stands in a table cell where no restriction is set. Short noun phrase covering every service, no period.

settings.common.allSchemas.context: Label of the checkbox meaning the rule or integration is not restricted to particular schemas, and the summary shown in a table cell where no restriction is set. Short noun phrase covering every schema, no period.

settings.common.selectServices.context: Ghost text in the empty multi-select dropdown for choosing individual services; once names are chosen they replace it. Short imperative prompt, not a repeat of the field label above it.

settings.common.selectSchemas.context: Ghost text in the empty multi-select dropdown for choosing individual schemas; once names are chosen they replace it. Short imperative prompt, not a repeat of the field label above it.

settings.common.removed.context: Stands in for a service or schema that a rule or integration still points at but which no longer exists. Past participle describing the missing record; keep it as short as the English, because it sits in a truncated table cell.

joins.after: Nothing fixed: it takes the place of one name inside a comma-separated list of service or schema names in a table cell
joins.note: Keep the parentheses, which mark it as a stand-in rather than a real name. The comma and space between entries are added by the code, so do not include a separator.

settings.common.unset.context: Stands in for the Teams recipient of an integration when neither a display name nor an identifier has been entered yet. Past participle meaning no value has been given; not an error, and not the same as removed.

joins.after: The recipient kind and a colon, in the target summary of the Teams integrations table
joins.note: Keep the parentheses, which mark it as a stand-in rather than a real name. Nothing follows it.

settings.common.optionalListName.en: Optional name shown only in this list.
settings.common.optionalListName.context: Sits under the optional name box in the editing panel of a rule or integration: filling it in only changes how the record is shown in the administrator's table behind the panel, and never affects behaviour. Full sentence; list refers to that table.

settings.common.serviceRequired.en: Pick at least one service, or choose “All services”.
settings.common.serviceRequired.context: Appears in a bar at the top of the editing panel when someone tries to save without naming a service. Second person; the quoted phrase is the caption of the neighbouring checkbox, so it must match that translation word for word, and the curly quotation marks should be kept.

settings.common.schemaRequired.en: Pick at least one schema, or choose “All schemas”.
settings.common.schemaRequired.context: Appears in a bar at the top of the editing panel when someone tries to save without naming a schema. Second person; the quoted phrase is the caption of the neighbouring checkbox, so it must match that translation word for word, and the curly quotation marks should be kept.

settings.common.cadence.context: Header of the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables, whose rows are the reporting frequencies from daily to yearly. Cadence is the product's word for how often a submission is expected; keep it very short, the column is narrow.

settings.common.cadences.Daily.context: Names the once-a-day reporting frequency: a first-column cell of the submission-window and current-period tables, and a choice in the reminder-frequency dropdown. Adverbial form describing how often, as in 'every day'; keep it short, the column is narrow.

settings.common.cadences.Weekly.context: Names the once-a-week reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. Adverbial form describing how often; the week's own start day is configured separately.

settings.common.cadences.Fortnightly.context: Names the every-two-weeks reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. Use the target language's ordinary way of saying 'every two weeks' if it has no single word; keep it short.

settings.common.cadences.Monthly.context: Names the once-a-month reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. Adverbial form describing how often; the day the month starts on is configured separately.

settings.common.cadences.Quarterly.context: Names the every-three-months reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. The quarters are counted from the configured start of the fiscal year, not necessarily from January.

settings.common.cadences.SemiAnnually.context: Names the twice-a-year reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. Every six months, counted from the configured start of the fiscal year; keep it short enough for a narrow column.

settings.common.cadences.Yearly.context: Names the once-a-year reporting frequency, in the first column of the submission-window and current-period tables and in the reminder-frequency dropdown. The year runs from the configured start of the fiscal year, which need not be January.

settings.common.months.january.context: Month name offered in the dropdowns that choose the first month of the fiscal year and the anchor month of a reminder schedule; the same wording is also dropped into a sentence describing a schedule. Use the plain standalone form of the month name, the one that also reads correctly after a preposition.

settings.common.months.february.context: Month name offered in the dropdowns that choose the first month of the fiscal year and the anchor month of a reminder schedule; the same wording is also dropped into a sentence describing a schedule. settings.common.weekDays.tuesday.context: Day name offered in the dropdown that sets which day a reporting week starts on, and in the multi-select that picks the days a reminder is sent. Full day name in its plain standalone form; the abbreviated forms live under their own keys.

settings.approval.title.context: Heading of the card holding the deployment-wide fallback rule for signing off submissions. Default here means the rule applied when a schema does not state its own, not a factory setting; policy is the configured combination of whether approval is needed and who gives it.

settings.approval.description.en: Schemas set to “Use the global default” fall back to this policy. Changing it affects only new submissions; in-flight ones keep the approvers they were created with.
settings.approval.description.context: Explains under the heading which schemas this fallback governs and that editing it is not retroactive: submissions already awaiting sign-off keep the approvers chosen when they were created. The quoted phrase is a choice offered in the schema editor, so it must match that translation exactly, curly quotation marks included.

settings.approval.saved.context: Green bar confirming that the fallback approval rule has been written to the server. Past tense, reporting a completed action; saved means stored, not economised.

settings.approval.defaultBehavior.en: When a schema defers to the default
settings.approval.defaultBehavior.context: Labels the pair of radio buttons that set what happens when a schema does not state its own approval rule. A clause rather than a noun phrase, so keep it grammatical without a period; 'defers to the default' means falls back to the rule configured here.

settings.approval.dontRequire.context: One of two mutually exclusive radio choices: submissions of such schemas count immediately, with nobody having to sign them off. Negated verb phrase describing the policy, not a command to the reader; keep it parallel with the opposite choice.

settings.approval.require.context: One of two mutually exclusive radio choices: submissions of such schemas must be signed off before they count. Verb phrase describing the policy, not a command to the reader; keep it parallel with the negated choice above it.

settings.approval.appliesTo.context: Labels the dropdown that limits which submissions the sign-off requirement covers, according to how they arrived. Third-person verb phrase about the policy, not an instruction; no period.

settings.approval.approvers.context: Labels the multi-select listing the people who may sign off a submission. An approver is an account entitled to accept or reject a submission; plural noun, no period.

settings.approval.approversHint.en: Approver/Admin accounts who may review, and/or the service owner (the account that sent the submission). Mark at least one as Required.
settings.approval.approversHint.context: Guidance under the approvers field: eligible entries are accounts holding the approver or administrator role, plus the owner of the service that filed the submission, and at least one entry must be marked as mandatory. Approver and Admin name account roles, and Required is the caption of the radio button beside each chosen approver, so match those translations.

settings.approval.requiredApproverValida.en: Add at least one Required approver.
settings.approval.requiredApproverValida.context: Warns that sign-off is demanded but every chosen approver is currently marked as merely optional, so nothing would ever be signed off. Second person imperative; Required is the caption of the radio button beside each approver and must match that translation.

settings.approval.selectApprovers.context: Ghost text in the empty approvers dropdown, replaced by the chosen names once any are picked. Short imperative prompt, not a repeat of the field label.

settings.approval.serviceOwner.context: Choice in the approvers dropdown, and the name shown for that choice in the list of chosen approvers: whoever owns the service that filed the submission signs it off, rather than a named person. The parenthetical explains which service is meant, so keep it; a service is an organisational unit that submits data.

settings.approval.required.context: One of two radio choices beside each chosen approver: this approver's sign-off is mandatory before the submission counts. Adjective describing the approver's obligation, not a demand made of the reader; keep it parallel with the optional choice.

settings.approval.optional.context: One of two radio choices beside each chosen approver: this approver may sign off but the submission does not wait for them. Adjective describing the approver's obligation; keep it parallel with the mandatory choice.

settings.approval.sources.both.context: Choice in the dropdown limiting which submissions need sign-off: those typed in by a person and those sent programmatically alike. Manual means filed by hand in this web console; API means sent by a service over the interface.

settings.approval.sources.manualOnly.context: Choice in the dropdown limiting which submissions need sign-off: only those a person filed by hand in this web console; programmatically sent ones count without review. Web console is this administration interface.

settings.approval.sources.apiOnly.context: Choice in the dropdown limiting which submissions need sign-off: only those sent programmatically by a service; ones filed by hand count without review. API stays in English.

settings.areas.title.context: Heading of the card managing the optional grouping tags that can be attached to accounts. An area is an organisational or geographic unit, such as a region or a site; never a surface, a subject field, or a region of the screen.

settings.areas.description.en: Optional grouping tags offered when editing an account. With one or more areas defined the account editor shows a dropdown; leave the list empty to let editors type a free-text area. Areas are informative only — changing them never affects existing accounts.
settings.areas.description.context: Explains that these tags are offered when someone edits an account: define one or more and the account editor presents them as a dropdown, leave the list empty and whoever edits an account types the area by hand. Also says the tags carry no behaviour, so editing them cannot break accounts that already use them.

settings.areas.saved.context: Green bar confirming the list of grouping tags has been written to the server. Past tense, reporting a completed action; saved means stored.

settings.areas.empty.en: No areas defined — the account editor uses a free-text field.
settings.areas.empty.context: Stands where the list of grouping tags would be when none have been defined, and says what happens instead: whoever edits an account types the area into a plain text box. Not an error; the dash separates the state from its consequence.

settings.areas.moveUp.context: Announced by screen readers for the arrow button that moves one tag one place earlier in the list, which is the order the account editor will show them in. Names the action; nothing appears on screen.

placeholders.name: The tag's own text, exactly as an administrator typed it and therefore untranslated, e.g. North region

settings.areas.moveDown.context: Announced by screen readers for the arrow button that moves one tag one place later in the list, which is the order the account editor will show them in. Names the action; nothing appears on screen.

placeholders.name: The tag's own text, exactly as an administrator typed it and therefore untranslated, e.g. North region

settings.areas.remove.context: Announced by screen readers for the button that takes one tag out of the list. It only changes the list on screen until the panel is saved, and accounts already carrying that tag keep it.

placeholders.name: The tag's own text, exactly as an administrator typed it and therefore untranslated, e.g. North region

settings.areas.addLabel.context: Labels the text box where a new grouping tag is typed; the button beside it appends what was typed to the list. Phrased as an instruction in English but it labels the box, so use whatever a label naturally is in the target language, without a period.

settings.areas.placeholder.context: Ghost text in the empty box for a new grouping tag, showing the kind of value expected. Replace the example itself with a plausible region or site name for the target locale, and keep the 'for example' abbreviation the locale conventionally uses.

settings.submissionPeriods.title.context: Heading of the card that aligns reporting periods to the organisation's calendar. A period is the reporting window a submission belongs to, such as a week or a quarter; plural because every frequency is aligned here at once.

settings.submissionPeriods.description.en: Where each reporting period starts and ends. Changing these takes effect immediately for new submissions and open-period checks; periods already recorded keep the boundaries they were written with.
settings.submissionPeriods.description.context: Explains under the heading that these anchors decide where each reporting period begins and ends, that a change is effective at once for newly filed submissions and for the checks on whether a period is still open, and that periods already recorded keep the boundaries in force when they were written.

settings.submissionPeriods.saved.context: Green bar confirming the period boundaries have been written to the server. Past tense, reporting a completed action; saved means stored.

settings.submissionPeriods.fiscalYearSta.context: Labels the dropdown of month names that sets which month the financial year begins in. Ends in a preposition in English; restructure it naturally, without a period. Fiscal year means the organisation's accounting year, which need not start in January.

settings.submissionPeriods.fiscalYearHin.en: Also anchors quarterly and half-yearly periods.
settings.submissionPeriods.fiscalYearHin.context: Guidance under that dropdown: the same month also fixes where quarters and half-years fall, not just the yearly period. Anchors means aligns or pins; half-yearly corresponds to the twice-a-year frequency named elsewhere.

settings.submissionPeriods.weekStart.context: Labels the dropdown of day names that sets which weekday a reporting week begins on. Ends in a preposition in English; restructure it naturally, without a period.

settings.submissionPeriods.monthStart.context: Labels the number box that sets which day of the month a reporting month begins on, so a month can run for example from the 15th to the 14th. Whole numbers only; the range is stated in the hint beneath.

settings.submissionPeriods.monthStartHin.context: States the accepted range of the day-of-month box above it: any whole number from 1 to 28, the cap being 28 so that every month, February included, actually has that day. Keep the digits and the dash; translate nothing but the punctuation conventions.

settings.submissionPeriods.fortnightAnch.context: Labels the date picker that fixes where the two-week periods fall, since a fortnight has no natural calendar boundary. Anchor is a reference point, not a nautical object; fortnight means a span of two weeks. Noun phrase, no period.

settings.submissionPeriods.fortnightAnch.en: Any date on a fortnight boundary; only the date matters.
settings.submissionPeriods.fortnightAnch.context: Guidance under that date picker: pick any date on which a two-week period is known to begin, and note that only the calendar date counts because any time of day entered is ignored. Boundary here means the start of one such period.

settings.submissionWindows.title.context: Heading of the card that widens or narrows the span of time in which a submission may actually be filed for a period. A window is that span, which by default coincides exactly with the period itself; plural because each reporting frequency has its own.

settings.submissionWindows.description.en: How long before/after each cadence's period a service may actually create or edit a submission for it. Open offset delays when the window opens after the period starts; Grace period extends how long it stays open after the period ends. Both default to 0 hours — the window is exactly the period — until set here. “Missed submission” reporting and reminders also wait for the grace period to elapse.
settings.submissionWindows.description.context: Explains the two numbers configured in the table below: the open offset holds the window shut for a while after the period has begun, and the grace period keeps it open for a while after the period has ended; both are zero unless changed here, meaning the window equals the period. Also warns that a submission is only reported as missed, and reminders only sent, once the grace period has run out. Open offset, Grace period and the quoted phrase are captions and states used elsewhere, so keep those translations consistent.

settings.submissionWindows.saved.context: Green bar confirming the per-frequency window offsets have been written to the server. Past tense, reporting a completed action; saved means stored.

settings.submissionWindows.openOffset.context: Header of the column of number boxes holding how long after a period begins its window becomes available for filing. Open describes the window's availability, not an instruction to open something; the unit in brackets is hours, whole or fractional, from 0 up to about a year, and it must stay in the caption because nothing else states it. Keep it very short, the column is narrow.

settings.submissionWindows.gracePeriod.context: Header of the column of number boxes holding how much extra time is allowed after a period ends before its window shuts. Grace means indulgence, the extra time granted for late filing; the unit in brackets is hours, from 0 up to about a year, and must stay in the caption. Note this use of 'period' means a span of leeway, unlike the reporting period named elsewhere.

settings.currentPeriods.title.context: Heading of the read-only card showing what the settings above work out to at this moment, one row per reporting frequency. Current means present or in force right now, never electrical current.

settings.currentPeriods.description.en: What the settings above resolve to right now — a live snapshot, not something that updates on its own.
settings.currentPeriods.description.context: Warns under the heading that the table is a reading taken when the panel was opened rather than a live display, so it will not advance by itself and has to be refreshed by hand. Second sentence continues the first after a dash; keep it a single flowing sentence if the target language prefers that.

settings.currentPeriods.period.context: Header of the column showing the start and end of the reporting period in force right now for that frequency. Period means the reporting window a submission belongs to; the cell holds two formatted dates and times separated by a dash, so keep the header to one short word.

settings.currentPeriods.window.context: Header of the column showing the start and end of the span in which a submission may actually be filed for that period, which is the period stretched by the offsets configured above. Window means that span of time, not a screen or a pane; keep it to one short word.

settings.ingestion.title.context: Heading of the card that can stop the product accepting incoming data. Ingest is the product's word for taking data in, so use the same term chosen for it elsewhere; noun, no period.

settings.ingestion.description.en: A global kill switch for disaster recovery. Closing submissions blocks service-facing ingestion — service accounts, bulk import and the Teams integration — while everything else (reads, OData, admin create/edit for remediation, schemas, settings) stays available. A banner with the message below is shown to everyone while closed.
settings.ingestion.description.context: Explains that the switch below is an emergency measure covering the whole deployment: while it is on, everything that feeds data in from services is refused, while reading, the OData feed, schemas, settings and administrators' own corrective edits keep working, and everyone sees a banner carrying the message typed underneath. Kill switch is a vivid English idiom, so use whatever plain phrase for an emergency stop reads naturally; the named subsystems are product features.

settings.ingestion.saved.context: Green bar confirming the open-or-closed state and its banner text have been written to the server. Past tense, reporting a completed action; saved means stored.

settings.ingestion.closeAll.context: Label of the on/off switch that stops services filing anything at all; turning it on is the shutdown, turning it off resumes normal operation. Close means stop accepting, the opposite of a window being open, not closing a dialog or completing a period; keep it short enough to sit on one line beside the switch.

settings.ingestion.bannerLabel.context: Labels the multi-line box for the explanation shown to every user while filing is stopped. Banner is the strip of text across the top of the screen; keep the parenthetical marking the box as not compulsory.

settings.ingestion.bannerHint.en: Shown to everyone while submissions are closed.
settings.ingestion.bannerHint.context: Guidance under that box: whatever is typed reaches every user of the product, administrators and services alike, and only for as long as filing stays stopped. Full sentence.

settings.ingestion.bannerPlaceholder.en: e.g. Submissions are paused while we investigate a data issue. Expected back up by 5pm UTC.
settings.ingestion.bannerPlaceholder.context: Ghost text in the empty banner box, modelling the tone expected: say why filing has stopped and when it should resume. Rewrite the example itself idiomatically for the target locale, using its own clock and time-zone conventions, and stay well under the 500 characters the box accepts.

settings.email.title.context: Heading of the card where an administrator configures the outgoing mail server used for every notification email. "SMTP" is a protocol name and stays in Latin letters in every locale.

settings.email.description.en: Where outgoing mail is sent from. Stored in the database; the password is encrypted at rest and never shown again.
settings.email.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading; a small "Configured" or "Not configured" badge is appended to the end of the same paragraph, so the last sentence must be able to end before it. "Stored in the database" reassures the administrator that no configuration file has to be edited; "encrypted at rest" describes the stored copy of the password.

settings.email.saved.context: Green confirmation bar shown above the form once the mail-server settings have been written to storage. "Saved" means stored, never the sense of saving money or saving time.

settings.email.host.context: Label of the text box for the mail server's network address. "Host" is the machine that runs the SMTP server (a DNS name or IP address), not a person who hosts anything; the value carries no scheme and no port.

settings.email.hostPlaceholder.context: Ghost text showing the shape of a valid mail-server address. Leave it exactly as it is: "smtp" is a protocol name and example.org is a reserved documentation domain.

settings.email.port.context: Label of a narrow numeric box for the TCP port the mail server listens on; the form starts at 587. Keep it to one short word — the box is only about 110 pixels wide.

settings.email.useTls.context: Label of an on/off toggle that makes the connection upgrade to encryption with the STARTTLS command on the port above, rather than opening an implicitly encrypted connection. "TLS" and "STARTTLS" are protocol names and are never translated or transliterated.

settings.email.fromAddress.context: Label of the box holding the sender address that recipients will see on every notification email. "From" is the name of the email header, so use the wording your locale's mail clients use for that header rather than a literal preposition.

settings.email.fromAddressPlaceholder.context: Ghost text showing the shape of a valid sender address. Leave it untranslated: "ingest" is the product name used as a mailbox name and example.org is a reserved documentation domain.

settings.email.fromName.context: Label of the box holding the display name shown beside the sender address in a recipient's mail client. "From" refers to the same email header as the address field above it.

settings.email.fromNamePlaceholder.context: Ghost text suggesting the product's own name as the sender display name. "Ingest" is the product name and is never translated.

settings.email.username.context: Label of the box for the account name used to authenticate against the mail server. It is optional; servers that accept unauthenticated relay need no value here.

settings.email.usernamePlaceholder.context: Ghost text telling the administrator what an empty box means: mail is handed to the server without authenticating. "Blank" means the box is left empty, and "anonymous relay" is the mail-server term for accepting unauthenticated mail. Keep the parentheses and the equals sign, and keep it short — it must fit inside the box.

settings.email.changePassword.context: Label of a checkbox shown when a password is already stored; ticking it reveals an empty password box so a new value can be entered. Nothing is changed until the administrator saves the form.

settings.email.setPassword.context: Label of the same checkbox as the change variant, used when no password has been stored yet. "Set" here means supply a value for the first time.

settings.email.password.context: Label of the masked box for the mail server's authentication password. The stored value is never displayed again, so the box is always empty when the form opens.

settings.email.passwordHint.en: Leave blank to clear the stored password.
settings.email.passwordHint.context: Guidance under the password box: submitting an empty box deletes the stored password, after which mail is relayed without authentication. Addressed to the administrator as an instruction, and "blank" means an empty box rather than a space character.

settings.emailTemplates.title.context: Heading of the card listing the message templates used to build notification emails. A template here is an editable subject line plus body text with placeholders, not a document or a stationery design.

settings.emailTemplates.description.en: Liquid templates used to build notification emails. Select one to edit its subject and body.
settings.emailTemplates.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading, telling the administrator that clicking a row in the table below opens that template for editing. "Liquid" is the proper name of the templating language used in the bodies and must stay as it is.

settings.emailTemplates.empty.context: Shown as an informational bar where the template table would be when no templates exist at all. It reports an absence, not a failure.

settings.emailTemplates.template.context: Header of the first, widest column, which holds each template's human-readable name. Keep it to a single noun.

settings.emailTemplates.subject.context: Header of the column that previews each template's subject line, and also the label of the corresponding box in the editing panel. "Subject" is the email header line shown in a recipient's inbox, not a topic of study or a person under authority.

settings.emailTemplates.format.context: Header of a narrow column that says whether a template carries both an HTML and a plain-text body or plain text only. Very tight on space — use the shortest available noun.

settings.emailTemplates.editAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for a clickable table row; activating the row opens that template for editing. "Edit" is the action being offered, so use the verb form your locale uses for a control that opens something for modification.

placeholders.name: Human-readable name of the email template, e.g. Upcoming submission reminder

settings.emailTemplates.htmlAndText.context: Compact badge in the narrow Format column, marking a template that carries both an HTML body and a plain-text body. "HTML" stays in Latin letters and the plus sign is kept; badges do not wrap, so keep this to two short words.

settings.emailTemplates.text.context: Compact badge in the narrow Format column, marking a template that has a plain-text body only. One short word; badges do not wrap.

settings.emailTemplates.editNamed.context: Heading of the side panel that opens over the page for editing one template. Keep the em dash that separates the action from the template's name.

placeholders.name: Human-readable name of the template being edited, e.g. Submission rejected notice

settings.emailTemplates.edit.context: Heading of the same editing panel in the rare case where no template name is available. Word it consistently with the variant that includes the name.

settings.emailTemplates.saved.context: Green confirmation bar inside the editing panel after the template's subject and bodies have been written to storage. "Saved" means stored.

settings.emailTemplates.textBody.context: Label of the large multi-line box holding the plain-text version of the message. "Body" is the main text of an email as opposed to its subject line.

settings.emailTemplates.textBodyHint.context: Guidance under the plain-text box: this version is what recipients see when their mail client cannot display HTML, and placeholder syntax works here too. "Liquid" is the name of the templating language and is never translated.

settings.emailTemplates.htmlBody.context: Label of the large multi-line box holding the rich version of the message. "HTML" stays in Latin letters; "body" is the main text of the email.

settings.emailTemplates.htmlBodyHint.en: Optional. Leave blank to send text only.
settings.emailTemplates.htmlBodyHint.context: Guidance under the HTML box: the field may be left empty, in which case recipients get only the plain-text version. "Blank" means an empty box.

settings.emailTemplates.save.context: Caption of the primary button that writes the edited subject and bodies to storage. "Save" means store, never economise; use the imperative and keep it short enough not to widen the button.

settings.notifications.title.context: Heading of the card where an administrator chooses which events send email and to whom. Use the same word for notifications as the rest of the console.

settings.notifications.description.en: Choose which events generate emails and who receives them. Each trigger can notify the service's own contact email, the recipient list below, or both.
settings.notifications.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading. A trigger is one of the named events listed below, each with its own on/off toggle; a service is an organisational unit that submits data, and its "contact email" is the address stored on that service's own account. The recipient list is the administrator and operator list configured lower on the same card.

settings.notifications.saved.context: Green confirmation bar shown after the notification configuration has been written to storage. "Saved" means stored.

settings.notifications.runResult.context: Green bar reporting the outcome after an administrator triggers an immediate notification pass. "Queued" means the emails were placed in the outgoing mail queue, not that they have already been delivered; "upcoming", "missed" and "warnings" name the three triggers the pass evaluates, so keep them consistent with those toggle labels. The "(s)" is an English plural shortcut — use whatever plural form your locale needs for a variable count.

placeholders.total: Whole number of emails queued by the pass in total, e.g. 12
placeholders.upcoming: Whole number of those emails that were reminders about a window that is about to close, e.g. 7
placeholders.missed: Whole number of those emails that were alerts about a window that closed with no submission, e.g. 3
placeholders.warnings: Whole number of those emails that were notices about a submission accepted with warnings, e.g. 2

settings.notifications.upcoming.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails a reminder shortly before a reporting window closes, while a submission can still be filed. "Upcoming" describes the deadline that is approaching, not the reminder itself.

settings.notifications.leadTime.en: Lead time (hours before the window closes)
settings.notifications.leadTime.context: Label of a narrow numeric box, shown only while the reminder above is switched on, holding how far ahead of the window's closing time the reminder is sent. The unit is whole hours (the backend accepts 1 to 720, and the default is 24); keep the unit visible in the parentheses. "Window" is the reporting period during which data may be submitted.

settings.notifications.missed.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails an alert after a reporting window has closed without the required submission arriving. "Missed" qualifies the submission that never came.

settings.notifications.warnings.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails a notice when a submission was accepted but raised non-blocking warnings. "Notice" here is an informational message, not a legal notification or a warning of rejection.

settings.notifications.draftSaved.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails colleagues whenever a partially filled submission is stored as a draft. "Nudge" is a deliberately light, friendly word for a gentle reminder — avoid anything as formal as "alert" or "warning".

settings.notifications.draftSavedHint.en: Sent on every draft save (no dedupe) to nudge collaborators. The email shows a relative path you paste after your console's address — it isn't a clickable link.
settings.notifications.draftSavedHint.context: Guidance shown under the draft toggle once it is on. "No dedupe" means the email is repeated on every single save instead of being sent once per event, and the second sentence warns that the email contains only a path fragment that the reader must append to their own console address by hand.

settings.notifications.pendingApproval.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails when a submission has been accepted but is being held until an approver signs it off. "Pending approval" is the waiting state of the submission.

settings.notifications.pendingApprovalHi.en: The submission's designated approvers are always emailed; these switches add the submitter and/or admin list.
settings.notifications.pendingApprovalHi.context: Guidance under the pending-approval toggle: the people named as approvers on that submission always receive the email, and the two checkboxes below only add the person who filed the submission and the administrator list. "Switches" refers to those checkboxes, and 'admin list' is the recipient list configured lower on this card.

settings.notifications.approved.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails when an approver signs off a held submission and its data goes live. "Notice" is an informational message.

settings.notifications.rejected.context: Label of the on/off toggle for the trigger that emails when an approver turns down a held submission so its data will not go live. "Notice" is an informational message.

settings.notifications.recipientList.context: Label of a multi-select box naming the people who receive the administrative copy of notification emails. "Admin" and "Operator" are the console's role names — use exactly the same words as the role names elsewhere in the product, and keep the slash.

settings.notifications.recipientListHint.en: Accounts (with an email) that receive the copy when a trigger has 'admin list' on.
settings.notifications.recipientListHint.context: Guidance under that box: only accounts holding the administrator or operator role and having an email address can be picked. 'Admin list' quotes the wording of the per-trigger checkbox "Notify the admin/operator list", so translate the quoted phrase the same way you translate that checkbox.

settings.notifications.noEligibleAccount.en: No eligible accounts (operators/admins need an email)
settings.notifications.noEligibleAccount.context: Ghost text inside the recipient box when no account qualifies, explaining why the list is empty rather than reporting an error. "Operators" and "admins" are role names; keep the parentheses and keep the whole thing short enough to fit inside the closed box.

settings.notifications.selectRecipients.context: Ghost text inside the recipient box, prompting the administrator to open it and tick people. Keep the trailing ellipsis character.

settings.notifications.running.context: Replaces the caption of the immediate-pass button while that pass is being executed on the server. Present progressive, ends with an ellipsis, and must fit the same button as the resting caption.

settings.notifications.runNow.context: Caption of the secondary button that executes the notification pass immediately instead of waiting for the scheduler. "Run" means execute, and "now" means without delay; imperative and short.

settings.notifications.notifyService.context: Label of a checkbox, shown under each enabled trigger, that sends the email to the contact address stored on the submitting service's own account. A service is an organisational unit that submits data, and "service account" is that unit's login account — not a background process.

settings.notifications.notifyAdminList.context: Label of a checkbox, shown under each enabled trigger, that also sends the email to the administrator and operator recipient list configured lower on this card. "Admin" and "operator" are role names; keep the slash and match the wording of the recipient-list label.

settings.approvalRules.title.context: Heading of the card listing cross-cutting rules; today every rule is an approval rule. "Rules" here are administrator-defined conditions the system applies automatically, not regulations or house rules.

settings.approvalRules.description.en: Require approval for specific services and schemas, on top of each schema's own policy. Leave a side set to “All” to cover every service or every schema. A rule scoped to API submissions can force a person to review and fill in partially-automated feeds before they go live.
settings.approvalRules.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition and a service is an organisational unit that submits data; "All" is quoted because it is the wording of the two checkboxes in the rule editor, and "sign-off" means a person formally approving. "API submissions" are those posted by machine rather than typed in by a person, and "go live" means the data becomes visible in reporting.

settings.approvalRules.add.context: Caption of the primary button above the table that opens an empty rule editor, and reused as the heading of that editor panel. Imperative and short; "add" means create a new one.

settings.approvalRules.edit.context: Heading of the side panel that opens over the page when an existing rule is opened for changes. Noun phrase or infinitive according to your locale's convention for panel headings, with no final period.

settings.approvalRules.create.context: Caption of the primary button at the bottom of the editor panel that saves a brand-new rule; when an existing rule is being edited the button says "Save changes" instead. Imperative and short.

settings.approvalRules.created.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after a new rule has been stored. Past tense, reporting a completed action.

settings.approvalRules.saved.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after changes to an existing rule have been stored. "Saved" means stored, never economised.

settings.approvalRules.deleted.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after a rule has been removed. Past tense, reporting a completed action.

settings.approvalRules.disabledMessage.context: Green confirmation bar after a rule has been switched off; it stays in the list but stops being applied. Past tense, describing the rule's new state.

settings.approvalRules.enabledMessage.context: Green confirmation bar after a rule has been switched back on so it is applied again. Past tense, describing the rule's new state.

settings.approvalRules.deleteType.context: Names the kind of object in the browser's delete confirmation prompt; the rule's own label is quoted after it. Lower case, singular, and in whatever grammatical form your locale needs directly after the verb "delete".

joins.after: the delete verb of shell.confirm.delete; supplied as the {{noun}} of shell.confirm.namedSubject, followed by the rule's label in quotes
joins.example:
Delete approval rule "Finance feeds need sign-off"?

This cannot be undone.
