joins.note: Rendered by the browser's own confirmation dialog, so no markup is possible and the surrounding sentence is assembled from other strings.

settings.approvalRules.approval.context: Header of a 180-pixel column summarising what each rule requires, and reused as the small heading above the approval settings inside the rule editor. "Approval" is a person signing off a submission; keep it to one short noun.

settings.approvalRules.useGlobalDefault.context: Value shown in that narrow Approval column when the rule defers to the console-wide default approval setting instead of deciding for itself. "Global" means applying across the whole installation; the text truncates with an ellipsis, so keep it brief.

settings.approvalRules.noApproval.context: Value shown in the narrow Approval column when the rule explicitly requires no sign-off, so matching submissions go live immediately. Keep it brief — the column truncates.

settings.approvalRules.requiredSummary.context: Value shown in the narrow Approval column when the rule demands a sign-off, with the kind of submission it applies to in parentheses. "Required" describes the approval, not the submission; keep the parentheses and stay brief because the column truncates.

placeholders.source: One of the three lower-case source scopes from settings.approvalRules.sources, e.g. manual only

settings.approvalRules.emptyManage.en: No rules yet — click “Add rule” to create one.
settings.approvalRules.emptyManage.context: Single row spanning the table when no rules exist and the signed-in user may create them; it points at the button above the table. The quoted phrase is that button's caption, so translate it exactly as you translated the button, and keep the typographic quotation marks.

settings.approvalRules.emptyReadOnly.context: Single row spanning the table when no rules exist and the signed-in user is not allowed to create any, so no next step is offered. It reports an absence, not an error.

settings.approvalRules.editAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for a clickable table row; activating the row opens that rule for changes. "Edit" is the action offered.

placeholders.name: The rule's own label, or, when it has none, the list of services it covers, e.g. Finance feeds need sign-off

settings.approvalRules.actionsAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for the icon-only button at the end of a row that opens a menu of operations on that rule. "Actions" are the menu's operations such as edit, disable and delete.

placeholders.name: The rule's own label, or, when it has none, the list of services it covers, e.g. Finance feeds need sign-off

settings.approvalRules.labelPlaceholder.context: Ghost text in the optional label box, illustrating the sort of short description an administrator might give a rule. Invent an equally natural example in your language; "sign-off" means formal approval and "feeds" are automated streams of incoming data.

settings.approvalRules.sources.both.context: Says that the rule applies to submissions typed in by a person and to those posted through the API alike. Lower case because it is dropped inside parentheses mid-phrase; "API" stays in Latin letters and the plus sign is kept.

joins.after: the word "Required", inside the parentheses of settings.approvalRules.requiredSummary

settings.approvalRules.sources.manualOnl.context: Says that the rule applies only to submissions a person filled in by hand in the console, leaving machine-posted ones alone. Lower case, because it is dropped inside parentheses mid-phrase.

joins.after: the word "Required", inside the parentheses of settings.approvalRules.requiredSummary

settings.approvalRules.sources.apiOnly.context: Says that the rule applies only to submissions posted programmatically through the API, leaving hand-filled ones alone. "API" stays in Latin letters, and the rest is lower case because it is dropped inside parentheses mid-phrase.

joins.after: the word "Required", inside the parentheses of settings.approvalRules.requiredSummary

settings.teamsConnection.title.context: Heading of the card holding the credentials that let the product post messages into Microsoft Teams. "Microsoft Teams" is a product name and is never translated; "connection" means the configured link to that service, not a network connection being opened.

settings.teamsConnection.description.en: The bot app registration used to send prompts to Teams. Stored in the database; the bot secret is encrypted at rest and never shown again. See the setup guide for how to register the bot in Azure.
settings.teamsConnection.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading; a "Configured" or "Not configured" badge is appended to the end of the same paragraph. "Bot" and "app registration" are the Microsoft Entra terms for the identity the product signs in as — use the wording Microsoft's own localised documentation uses — and "prompts" are the messages the bot sends asking someone to supply data. "Azure" is a product name.

settings.teamsConnection.saved.context: Green confirmation bar after the bot credentials have been written to storage. "Saved" means stored.

settings.teamsConnection.testSucceeded.context: Green bar shown after the test button has signed in with the stored credentials and been accepted. It confirms only that the credentials work, not that any message was sent; keep the em dash.

settings.teamsConnection.testFailed.context: Red bar shown after a failed credential test when the server returned no more specific reason; when it does return one, that detail is shown instead of this sentence.

settings.teamsConnection.appId.context: Label of the box holding the identifier of the bot's Microsoft Entra app registration, a 36-character GUID. "App (client) ID" is Microsoft's own field name in the Azure portal, so use the wording that portal uses in your language and keep the parenthesised alternative.

settings.teamsConnection.appIdPlaceholde.context: Ghost text showing that a GUID in the standard hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form is expected. Leave the zeros and hyphens exactly as they are.

settings.teamsConnection.tenantId.context: Label of the box holding the GUID of the Microsoft Entra directory the bot belongs to. "Tenant" is Microsoft's term for one organisation's directory — use the wording the Azure portal uses in your language.

settings.teamsConnection.tenantHint.en: Leave blank for a multi-tenant bot.
settings.teamsConnection.tenantHint.context: Guidance under the tenant box: an empty box means the bot is registered to accept sign-ins from any organisation. "Multi-tenant" is the Microsoft term for exactly that; "blank" means an empty box.

settings.teamsConnection.tenantPlacehold.context: Ghost text repeating what an empty tenant box means, using the Microsoft term for an app that serves any organisation. Keep the parentheses and the equals sign, and keep it short enough to fit inside the box.

settings.teamsConnection.singleTenant.context: Label of an on/off toggle stating that the app registration is restricted to one Microsoft Entra directory rather than open to any organisation. "Single-tenant" is the Microsoft term and pairs with the multi-tenant wording used in the hint above.

settings.teamsConnection.changeSecret.context: Label of a checkbox shown when a bot secret is already stored; ticking it reveals an empty box for a replacement value. "Secret" is a stored credential — a noun, not an adjective — and nothing changes until the form is saved.

settings.teamsConnection.setSecret.context: Label of the same checkbox when no bot secret has been stored yet, so a value is being supplied for the first time. "Secret" is a stored credential, used as a noun.

settings.teamsConnection.secret.context: Label of the masked box for the bot app registration's password-equivalent credential. "Client secret" is Microsoft's own field name in the Azure portal; keep the parenthesised form and treat "secret" as a noun. The stored value is never shown again, so the box always opens empty.

settings.teamsConnection.secretHint.en: Leave blank to clear the stored secret.
settings.teamsConnection.secretHint.context: Guidance under that box: saving with the box empty deletes the stored credential, after which the bot cannot sign in. Addressed to the administrator as an instruction; "blank" means an empty box.

settings.teamsConnection.testing.context: Replaces the caption of the test button while the credentials are being verified against Microsoft Entra. Present progressive, ends with an ellipsis, and must fit the same button as the resting caption.

settings.teamsConnection.test.context: Caption of the secondary button that tries the stored credentials against Microsoft Entra and reports whether they work; it stays disabled until credentials have been saved. "Test" is the imperative verb "try out", not the noun for an examination, and "connection" is the configured link to Teams.

settings.integrations.title.context: Heading of the card listing the configured outbound integrations; today each one sends prompts into Microsoft Teams. Use the same word the sidebar uses for this subpage.

settings.integrations.description.en: Each integration prompts a Teams user or channel for the samples that are still outstanding across the services and schemas it covers. Prompts run on a daily schedule, or on demand with “Run now”. Disabled and hidden fields are omitted; warnings are surfaced inline.
settings.integrations.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition, a service is an organisational unit that submits data, and "samples that are still outstanding" are the individual required values a service has not yet supplied for the current reporting period. "Run now" is quoted because it is the wording of a menu command, and "disabled and hidden fields" are values a schema's own conditions have switched off, so nobody is asked for them.

settings.integrations.connectionWarning.en: The Microsoft Teams connection isn’t configured yet — set the bot credentials on the “Teams connection” subpage before integrations can send prompts.
settings.integrations.connectionWarning.context: Amber warning bar that stays on the page while no Teams bot credentials have been stored, so no prompt can be sent. It describes a standing condition rather than the outcome of an action; the quoted phrase is the name of another settings subpage and must match that navigation label exactly.

settings.integrations.add.context: Caption of the primary button above the table that opens an empty integration editor, and reused as the heading of that editor panel. Imperative and short.

settings.integrations.edit.context: Heading of the side panel that opens over the page when an existing integration is opened for changes. No final period.

settings.integrations.create.context: Caption of the primary button at the bottom of the editor panel that stores a brand-new integration; when an existing one is being edited the button says "Save changes" instead. Imperative and short.

settings.integrations.created.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after a new integration has been stored. Past tense, reporting a completed action.

settings.integrations.saved.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after changes to an existing integration have been stored. "Saved" means stored, never economised.

settings.integrations.deleted.context: Green confirmation bar above the table after an integration has been removed. Past tense, reporting a completed action.

settings.integrations.disabledMessage.context: Green confirmation bar after an integration has been switched off; it stays in the list but sends no more prompts. Past tense, describing its new state.

settings.integrations.enabledMessage.context: Green confirmation bar after an integration has been switched back on so its schedule resumes. Past tense, describing its new state.

settings.integrations.deleteType.context: Names the kind of object in the browser's delete confirmation prompt; the integration's own label is quoted after it. Lower case, singular, and in whatever grammatical form your locale needs directly after the verb "delete".

joins.after: the delete verb of shell.confirm.delete; supplied as the {{noun}} of shell.confirm.namedSubject, followed by the integration's label in quotes
joins.example:
Delete integration "Daily nudge for the ops channel"?

This cannot be undone.
joins.note: Rendered by the browser's own confirmation dialog, so no markup is possible and the surrounding sentence is assembled from other strings.

settings.integrations.runComplete.context: Green bar reporting the outcome after an administrator has executed one integration immediately from the row menu. "Prompted" counts the Teams messages queued — one for each service and schema pair that still owes values — and "skipped" counts the pairs that had nothing outstanding, so skipping is a normal result and not a failure. Keep the em dash.

placeholders.prompted: Whole number of prompt messages queued by this run, e.g. 4
placeholders.skipped: Whole number of service-and-schema pairs passed over because nothing was outstanding, e.g. 11

settings.integrations.testEnqueued.context: Green bar confirming that a single sample prompt has been placed in the outgoing queue to check the Teams target; delivery happens a moment later. "Test" is a trial message, not an examination.

settings.integrations.target.context: Header of a 200-pixel column showing who each integration sends its prompts to. "Target" is the recipient — a Teams user or channel — not an objective or a goal; keep it to one short noun.

settings.integrations.scheduleLabel.context: Header of a 150-pixel column showing when each integration runs. "Schedule" is the recurring timetable; keep it to one short noun.

settings.integrations.emptyManage.en: No integrations yet — click “Add integration” to create one.
settings.integrations.emptyManage.context: Single row spanning the table when nothing is configured yet and the signed-in user may create integrations; it points at the button above the table. The quoted phrase is that button's caption, so translate it exactly as you translated the button, and keep the typographic quotation marks.

settings.integrations.emptyReadOnly.context: Single row spanning the table when nothing is configured yet and the signed-in user may not create integrations, so no next step is offered. It reports an absence, not an error.

settings.integrations.editAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for a clickable table row; activating the row opens that integration for changes. "Edit" is the action offered.

placeholders.name: The integration's own label, or, when it has none, its target summary, e.g. Daily nudge for the ops channel

settings.integrations.actionsAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for the icon-only button at the end of a row that opens a menu of operations on that integration. "Actions" are the menu's commands such as edit, run, send test, disable and delete.

placeholders.name: The integration's own label, or, when it has none, its target summary, e.g. Daily nudge for the ops channel

settings.integrations.runNow.context: Command in a row's action menu that executes this integration's prompt pass immediately instead of waiting for its schedule. "Run" means execute; imperative and short enough for a menu row.

settings.integrations.sendTest.context: Command in a row's action menu that sends one trial message to check that the target is reachable, without waiting for real outstanding data. The same wording is reused for webhook endpoints, so choose a phrasing that suits both a chat prompt and an HTTP call; "test" is a trial, not an examination.

settings.integrations.targetSummary.context: Value shown in the 200-pixel Target column, naming the kind of recipient and then the recipient itself; the full text is repeated in a tooltip on hover. Keep the colon and stay brief, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.kind: The recipient type, one of the two lower-level labels settings.integrations.channel or settings.integrations.user, e.g. Channel
placeholders.target: The friendly display name if one was given, otherwise the raw Teams identifier, e.g. Ops team channel

settings.integrations.channel.context: Names the recipient type when prompts go to a Teams channel rather than one person. It is dropped in before a colon and the recipient's name, so no final punctuation.

joins.after: nothing; it is the {{kind}} of settings.integrations.targetSummary, followed by a colon and the recipient's name

settings.integrations.user.context: Names the recipient type when prompts go to one Teams person rather than a channel. It is dropped in before a colon and the recipient's name, so no final punctuation.

joins.after: nothing; it is the {{kind}} of settings.integrations.targetSummary, followed by a colon and the recipient's name

settings.integrations.targetRequired.en: Enter the target user or channel id.
settings.integrations.targetRequired.context: Red bar at the top of the editor panel when the recipient box was left empty. "Id" is short for identifier — the Teams channel or user identifier — and stays a technical term; address the administrator directly.

settings.integrations.hourValidation.context: Red bar at the top of the editor panel when the hour box holds something outside the 24-hour clock. Keep the numbers as digits and the range inclusive; the backend enforces the same limits.

settings.integrations.minuteValidation.context: Red bar at the top of the editor panel when the minute box holds something outside a valid minute of the hour. Keep the numbers as digits and the range inclusive.

settings.integrations.labelPlaceholder.en: e.g. Daily nudge for the ops channel
settings.integrations.labelPlaceholder.context: Ghost text in the optional label box, illustrating the sort of short name an administrator might give an integration. Invent an equally natural example in your language; "nudge" is a gentle reminder and "ops" is the shorthand for an operations team.

settings.integrations.sendTo.context: Label above a pair of radio buttons choosing whether prompts go to one person or to a channel. Noun phrase or short question according to your locale's form for a choice label, with no final colon.

settings.integrations.aUser.context: Label of the radio button that sends prompts to a single Teams person as a private chat. Keep it as short as the other option beside it, since the two sit on one line.

settings.integrations.aChannel.context: Label of the radio button that sends prompts to a Teams channel where everyone in it can see them. Keep it as short as the other option beside it, since the two sit on one line.

settings.integrations.channelId.context: Label of the required box for the recipient identifier, shown when the channel option is chosen. "Id" is short for identifier — an opaque code copied out of Teams, not a name a person would recognise.

settings.integrations.userId.en: User id (Entra object id, UPN, or email)
settings.integrations.userId.context: Label of the required box for the recipient identifier, shown when the single-person option is chosen; any of three forms is accepted. "Entra object id", "UPN" (user principal name) and "email" are Microsoft identity terms and stay in Latin letters.

settings.integrations.targetIdHint.en: See the setup guide for how to find this id.
settings.integrations.targetIdHint.context: Guidance under the identifier box, pointing the administrator at the product's written setup instructions. "This id" means the identifier the box above is asking for; use the same word for the setup guide as the rest of the console.

settings.integrations.channelIdPlacehold.context: Ghost text showing the shape of a Teams channel identifier. Leave it exactly as it is: every character, including the "19:" prefix and the "@thread.tacv2" suffix, is literal Teams syntax.

settings.integrations.userIdPlaceholder.context: Ghost text showing that a person may be identified by their email address. Leave it untranslated; example.org is a reserved documentation domain.

settings.integrations.displayName.context: Label of the optional box for a readable name to show instead of the raw identifier in this admin table. "Display name" is what appears on screen, not the recipient's real name in Teams.

settings.integrations.displayNameHint.en: Optional friendly label for this target.
settings.integrations.displayNameHint.context: Guidance under that box: the value is only a convenience for administrators reading the list and has no effect on delivery. "Target" is the recipient of the prompts.

settings.integrations.displayNamePlaceho.context: Ghost text illustrating a readable name for a recipient. Invent an equally natural example in your language; "ops" is the shorthand for an operations team.

settings.integrations.frequency.context: Label of the dropdown choosing how often the integration runs, from daily to yearly. One short noun.

settings.integrations.frequencyHint.en: How often the pass looks for outstanding values. It also runs on demand with “Run now”.
settings.integrations.frequencyHint.context: Guidance under that dropdown. "The pass" is one scheduled sweep that looks for values still missing, and the quoted phrase is the wording of the run command in each row's action menu — translate it exactly as you translated that menu command and keep the typographic quotation marks.

settings.integrations.daysOfWeek.context: Label of a multi-select dropdown, shown only for a weekly frequency, restricting which weekdays the pass runs on. Noun phrase, no final colon.

settings.integrations.daysOfWeekHint.en: Leave empty to run every day.
settings.integrations.daysOfWeekHint.context: Guidance under that dropdown: selecting nothing means no restriction, so the pass runs on all seven days. Addressed to the administrator as an instruction.

settings.integrations.everyDay.context: Shown inside the weekday dropdown while no day is ticked, standing for all seven days. It is both the ghost text and the collapsed value of the closed dropdown, so keep it short; "every day" means daily, not "everyday" in the sense of ordinary.

settings.integrations.anchorMonth.context: Label of a dropdown, shown for quarterly, half-yearly and yearly frequencies, choosing the month the repeating cycle is counted from. "Anchor" means the fixed starting point of the cycle.

settings.integrations.anchorMonthHint.en: The period repeats from this month (e.g. quarterly from February = Feb, May, Aug, Nov).
settings.integrations.anchorMonthHint.context: Guidance under that dropdown, explaining the cycle with a worked example. "Period" is the recurring interval set by the frequency above; translate the month names and abbreviate them the way your locale does, keeping the parentheses and the equals sign.

settings.integrations.dayOfMonth.context: Label of a dropdown, shown for monthly and longer frequencies, choosing which calendar day inside the interval the pass runs on. Noun phrase, no final colon.

settings.integrations.dayOfMonthHint.en: Runs on (or after) this day within the period; “Last day” runs on the final day of the month.
settings.integrations.dayOfMonthHint.context: Guidance under that dropdown: "on (or after)" allows for a month too short to contain the chosen day, and the quoted phrase is that dropdown's own final option, so translate it exactly as you translated the option. "Period" is the recurring interval set by the frequency above.

settings.integrations.lastDay.context: Final option in the day-of-month dropdown, after the numbers 1 to 31, meaning whichever day ends the month — the 28th, 29th, 30th or 31st as the calendar dictates. Short noun phrase; it is also shown as the closed dropdown's value.

settings.integrations.theLastDay.context: Substituted into a schedule summary in place of an ordinal number when the pass is set to run on whichever day ends the month. Lower case and carrying its article because it lands mid-sentence in a narrow table cell.

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value
joins.example: Monthly on the last day, 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.hourUtc.context: Label of a narrow numeric box for the hour of day the pass starts, on a 24-hour clock from 0 to 23. The time is always in Coordinated Universal Time and never adjusted for local time or daylight saving; "UTC" stays in Latin letters, and the box is only about 110 pixels wide.

settings.integrations.minuteUtc.context: Label of a narrow numeric box for the minute past the hour the pass starts, from 0 to 59, alongside the hour box. "UTC" stays in Latin letters; keep it as short as the hour label because both boxes sit on one line.

settings.integrations.ordinal.zero.context: Turns a day number into an ordinal (English "5th") for the day-of-month dropdown and for the schedule summary in the table. This entry covers the ordinal category your language calls "zero"; English never selects it, so if your language has no such form give it the same text as the general form. Keep the placeholder, add a space before your suffix only if your language needs one, and expect values from 1 to 31.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 15

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.ordinal.one.context: Ordinal form for numbers your language treats as the "one" category — in English 1, 21 and 31, giving "1st". Keep the placeholder and use the suffix your language attaches to those numbers; if your language has a single ordinal form for every number, repeat that form in all six entries.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 1

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.ordinal.two.context: Ordinal form for numbers your language treats as the "two" category — in English 2 and 22, giving "2nd". Keep the placeholder and use the suffix your language attaches to those numbers.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 2

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.ordinal.few.context: Ordinal form for numbers your language treats as the "few" category — in English 3 and 23, giving "3rd". Keep the placeholder and use the suffix your language attaches to those numbers.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 3

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.ordinal.many.context: Ordinal form for numbers your language treats as the "many" category. English never selects it, so if your language has no such form give it the same text as the general form. Keep the placeholder and expect values from 1 to 31.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 11

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.ordinal.other.context: The general ordinal form, used for every day number the other categories do not claim — in English 4 through 20 and beyond, giving "4th". This is the one form that is always used, so if your language has a single ordinal ending put it here and repeat it in the other five entries.

placeholders.count: Day of the month as a plain number from 1 to 31, e.g. 4

joins.after: the preposition of a settings.integrations.schedule summary, as its {{day}} value; also used on its own as an option in the day-of-month dropdown

settings.integrations.schedule.weeklyEve.context: Value shown in the 150-pixel Schedule column when an integration runs every day of the week at a fixed time. "Weekly" is the chosen frequency and the parenthesised phrase says no weekday restriction was set; keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.weeklyDay.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when specific weekdays were chosen, listing them and then the time. Only the punctuation between the two parts is yours to adapt; keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.days: Already-localised short weekday names joined with commas, e.g. Mon, Wed, Fri
placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.monthly.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when an integration runs once a month. Reorder the parts to suit your language, but keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.day: Either an ordinal day such as 15th or the phrase "the last day", already localised, e.g. the last day
placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.quarterly.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when an integration runs every three months, counted from the chosen starting month. "From" marks that starting month, not a range; keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.month: Already-localised full month name that the cycle is counted from, e.g. February
placeholders.day: Either an ordinal day such as 15th or the phrase "the last day", already localised, e.g. 15th
placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.semiAnnua.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when an integration runs every six months, counted from the chosen starting month. "Semi-annually" means twice a year; keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.month: Already-localised full month name that the cycle is counted from, e.g. February
placeholders.day: Either an ordinal day such as 15th or the phrase "the last day", already localised, e.g. 15th
placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.yearly.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when an integration runs once a year in the chosen month. Reorder the parts to suit your language, but keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.month: Already-localised full month name in which the run happens, e.g. February
placeholders.day: Either an ordinal day such as 15th or the phrase "the last day", already localised, e.g. 15th
placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.integrations.schedule.daily.context: Value shown in the narrow Schedule column when an integration runs once every day at a fixed time. "Daily" is the chosen frequency; keep it very short, because the cell truncates with an ellipsis.

placeholders.time: Fixed clock time built in code as two-digit hours and minutes followed by the literal word UTC, e.g. 08:00 UTC

settings.webhooks.title.context: Heading of the card listing the external addresses the product calls when something happens. "Webhook" is the established technical term for such a callback and "endpoint" is one registered destination address; keep both as the developer audience knows them, untranslated where your locale's technical writing leaves them in English.

settings.webhooks.description.en: Send a signed HTTP POST to an external URL (Teams, Power Automate, your own service) when a subscribed event happens — no polling required.
settings.webhooks.description.context: Explanatory paragraph under the heading. "Signed" means each request carries a cryptographic signature the receiver can check, "POST" is the HTTP method and stays in capitals, and "no polling required" contrasts this with the receiver having to ask repeatedly for changes. "Teams" and "Power Automate" are Microsoft product names and are never translated.

settings.webhooks.add.context: Caption of the primary button above the table that opens an empty endpoint form. Imperative and short; "endpoint" is one destination address.

settings.webhooks.addTitle.context: Heading of the side panel that opens over the page for registering a new destination. No final period; keep the same word for endpoint as the rest of this card.

settings.webhooks.editTitle.context: Heading of the same side panel when an existing destination is opened for changes. Keep the em dash that separates the action from the endpoint's name.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.editAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for a clickable table row; activating the row opens that endpoint for changes. "Edit" is the action offered.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.actionsAria.context: Announced by a screen reader for the icon-only button at the end of a row that opens a menu of operations on that endpoint. Name the operations generally, as in "actions for", since the menu holds several commands.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.deleteConfirm.en:
Delete the webhook endpoint “{{name}}”?

Its past deliveries are kept for audit.
settings.webhooks.deleteConfirm.context: Text of the browser's own confirmation prompt before an endpoint is removed; the second sentence reassures the administrator that the record of past attempts survives for auditing. Keep the blank line between the two parts and the typographic quotation marks around the name; "deliveries" are the individual attempts to call the address.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint about to be deleted, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.deleted.context: Green confirmation bar above the table naming the endpoint that has just been removed. Past tense; keep the typographic quotation marks around the name.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint that was deleted, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.rotateConfirm.en:
Generate a new signing secret for “{{name}}”?

The old secret stops working immediately.
settings.webhooks.rotateConfirm.context: Text of the browser's own confirmation prompt before a fresh signing secret replaces the current one. Say plainly that the change takes effect at once, so whoever receives the calls must be given the new secret immediately or their signature checks will fail; "secret" is a stored credential, used as a noun. Keep the blank line and the typographic quotation marks.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint whose secret is being replaced, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.testQueued.en: Test delivery queued for “{{name}}”. Check the delivery log below.
settings.webhooks.testQueued.context: Green bar confirming that a trial call has been placed in the outgoing queue, so its result appears a moment later rather than immediately. The delivery log is the record of attempts reached from the link under the table; keep the typographic quotation marks around the name.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint the test was queued for, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.name.context: Header of the first column, holding the administrator's own name for each endpoint, and also the label of the required box for that name in the form. One short noun.

settings.webhooks.url.context: Header of the column showing each endpoint's destination address in a monospace font, truncated with the full value on hover. "URL" stays in Latin capitals.

settings.webhooks.eventsLabel.context: Header of a 120-pixel column showing how many events an endpoint is subscribed to, and also the label above the list of event checkboxes in the form. An event is one thing that happened in the product and can be reported outward; keep it to one short plural noun.

settings.webhooks.empty.en: No endpoints yet. Add one to start receiving events.
settings.webhooks.empty.context: Single row spanning the table when no destination has been registered yet, with the next step in the second sentence. "Add one" refers to the button above the table; it reports an absence, not an error.

settings.webhooks.unsignedHint.en: No signing secret set — deliveries are sent unsigned.
settings.webhooks.unsignedHint.context: Revealed on hover over the warning marker beside an endpoint's name, explaining that without a stored secret the outgoing calls carry no signature, so the receiver cannot verify they came from this product. "Secret" is a stored credential, used as a noun.

settings.webhooks.unsigned.context: Compact amber marker shown under an endpoint's name when it has no signing secret, in the same cell as the name and truncated if it does not fit. Keep it to one lower-case word; it describes the calls, meaning they carry no cryptographic signature.

settings.webhooks.noEvents.context: Shown on hover in place of the list of subscribed events when an endpoint is subscribed to none. Two words at most; it reports an absence, not an error.

settings.webhooks.eventCount_one.context: Singular form of the value in the 120-pixel Events column, counting how many event types the endpoint is subscribed to. Extremely tight on space, so keep it to the number plus one short noun; add whichever further plural forms your language needs by copying this entry with the matching suffix.

placeholders.count: Whole number of subscribed event types, here always 1

settings.webhooks.eventCount_other.context: General plural form of the value in the 120-pixel Events column, counting how many event types the endpoint is subscribed to. Extremely tight on space, so keep it to the number plus one short noun; the maximum is seven.

placeholders.count: Whole number of subscribed event types, from 0 to 7, e.g. 3

settings.webhooks.rotateSecret.context: Command in a row's action menu, shown when a secret already exists, that replaces it with a newly generated one. "Rotate" is the security term for periodically replacing a credential, not physical turning; "secret" is a stored credential, used as a noun.

settings.webhooks.generateSecret.context: The same menu command, worded for an endpoint that has no secret yet, so one is being created for the first time. "Generate" means the system produces the value itself rather than the administrator choosing it.

settings.webhooks.deliveryHistory.en: Delivery history — status, retries, and manual redelivery — lives on the <auditLink>Audit page</auditLink> under <sectionName>Webhook deliveries</sectionName>.
settings.webhooks.deliveryHistory.context: Hint under the webhook endpoint list, telling the reader that this screen configures endpoints while the record of individual deliveries lives elsewhere. Delivery here means one attempt to POST an event to a subscriber's URL. Translate the two wrapped labels to match exactly what the Audit page and its tab are called in your locale — the reader is being told what to look for. Order the clause however your language prefers; the link and the section name may move.

settings.webhooks.nameRequired.context: Red bar at the top of the form when the name box was left empty. States the problem impersonally; the administrator simply has to type a name.

settings.webhooks.urlValidation.context: Red bar at the top of the form when the destination address is not a complete address beginning with http:// or https://. "Absolute" means the whole address including the scheme, not a path on its own; "http(s)" stays exactly as written, parentheses included.

settings.webhooks.eventRequired.en: Select at least one event to subscribe to.
settings.webhooks.eventRequired.context: Red bar at the top of the form when no event checkbox was ticked, so the endpoint would never be called. "Subscribe to" means asking to be notified of that event.

settings.webhooks.namePlaceholder.context: Ghost text in the name box, illustrating the sort of label an administrator might use to recognise a destination. Invent an equally natural example in your language; "Teams" is a Microsoft product name and the punctuation between the two parts may follow your locale's habits.

settings.webhooks.destinationUrl.context: Label of the required box for the address the product will call. "Destination" is where the call is sent and "URL" stays in Latin capitals.

settings.webhooks.destinationUrlHint.en: The signed POST is sent here. Must be an absolute http(s) URL.
settings.webhooks.destinationUrlHint.context: Guidance under that box: the signed request is sent to exactly this address, which must be complete and begin with http:// or https://. "POST" is the HTTP method and stays in capitals; "http(s)" stays exactly as written.

settings.webhooks.urlPlaceholder.context: Ghost text showing the shape of a complete destination address. Leave it untranslated: example.org is a reserved documentation domain and the path is illustrative literal text.

settings.webhooks.onlyForService.context: Label of a dropdown that narrows this endpoint to the events of a single service, a service being an organisational unit that submits data. "Only for" restricts rather than requires.

settings.webhooks.onlyForServiceHint.en: Limit deliveries to one service account. Leave blank to fire for every service.
settings.webhooks.onlyForServiceHint.context: Guidance under that dropdown: choosing nothing means the endpoint is called for events of every service. "Service account" is the login account belonging to one such organisational unit, not a background process, and "fire" means the call is made.

settings.webhooks.descriptionLabel.context: Label of an optional multi-line box for the administrator's own remarks about this endpoint. One short noun.

settings.webhooks.descriptionHint.en: Optional note shown only in this admin list.
settings.webhooks.descriptionHint.context: Guidance under that box: the text is for administrators reading this table only and is never sent anywhere or shown to the people who receive the calls.

settings.webhooks.generateOnCreate.en: Generate a signing secret (HMAC-SHA256). Shown once after saving.
settings.webhooks.generateOnCreate.context: Label of a checkbox, shown only when registering a new endpoint, asking the system to produce a credential for signing the outgoing calls. "HMAC-SHA256" is the name of the signing algorithm and stays exactly as written; the second sentence warns that the value is revealed a single time and cannot be looked up afterwards.

settings.webhooks.create.context: Caption of the primary button that registers the new destination; when an existing one is being edited the button says "Save changes" instead. Imperative and short.

settings.webhooks.secretTitle.context: Heading of the modal that reveals the freshly generated credential once. "Signing secret" is the credential used to sign outgoing calls — a noun, not an adjective; keep the typographic quotation marks around the name.

placeholders.name: The administrator's own name for the endpoint the secret belongs to, e.g. Teams – submissions channel

settings.webhooks.secretInstructions.en: Copy this now — it is shown once and cannot be retrieved later. Use it to verify the X-Ingest-Signature header on each delivery.
settings.webhooks.secretInstructions.context: Body of that modal, urging the administrator to store the value now because it is never displayed again. "Verify" means checking that the signature matches; "X-Ingest-Signature" is the exact name of an HTTP header and must be reproduced character for character, never translated.

settings.webhooks.copied.context: Briefly replaces the copy button's caption, for about two seconds, once the value has been placed on the clipboard. It confirms a completed action, so past participle rather than progressive, and it must fit the same button as the resting caption.

settings.webhooks.copySecret.context: Resting caption of the button that puts the revealed credential on the clipboard. "Copy" is the imperative verb and "secret" is the credential, used as a noun; keep it short.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAccep.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a reporting period, and "accepted" means it passed validation and was stored. The event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAccep.en: A service submitted data and it was accepted.
settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAccep.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires. A service is an organisational unit that submits data; "accepted" means the data passed validation and was stored.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionWarni.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a submission that was stored but raised remarks worth looking at. The event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionWarni.en: An accepted submission carried non-blocking warnings.
settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionWarni.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires. "Non-blocking" means the warnings did not stop the submission from being stored, so this is not a rejection.

settings.webhooks.events.WindowUpcoming..context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a reporting window whose deadline is near. "Window" is the period during which data may be submitted; the event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.WindowUpcoming..en: A submission window is approaching its close.
settings.webhooks.events.WindowUpcoming..context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires. "Its close" is the moment the window stops accepting data, and the event fires while there is still time to submit.

settings.webhooks.events.WindowMissed.la.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a reporting window that ended with nothing submitted. "Missed" describes the deadline that passed unmet; the event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.WindowMissed.de.en: A window closed without the required submission.
settings.webhooks.events.WindowMissed.de.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires: the window stopped accepting data and the expected submission never arrived.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionPendi.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a submission waiting for a person to sign it off. "Pending approval" is the waiting state; the event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionPendi.en: A submission was accepted but is held awaiting approval.
settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionPendi.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires. "Held" means the data was stored but is deliberately kept back from reporting until an approver decides.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAppro.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a submission an approver has signed off. The event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAppro.en: A pending submission was approved and is now live.
settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionAppro.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires. "Go live" means the submission's data is now counted in reporting; "pending" was its previous waiting state.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionRejec.context: Label of a checkbox in the list of subscribable events, for a submission an approver has turned down. The event's dotted code name is appended in parentheses automatically and must never be translated.

settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionRejec.en: A pending submission was rejected and will not go live.
settings.webhooks.events.SubmissionRejec.context: Small grey line under that checkbox explaining when the event fires: an approver refused the held submission, so its data will never be counted in reporting.

shell.common.close.context: Shared caption for dismissing whatever is on screen: the primary button on a finished wizard's confirmation view, and the accessible name of the icon-only X in drawer headers. Means dismiss this panel — never finishing or closing a reporting period. One short imperative word.

shell.common.cancel.context: Leaves a multi-step dialog without saving anything, sitting beside Back and Next in the dialog footer. Imperative, and deliberately different from Close: work in progress is discarded.

shell.skipToContent.context: A link that is the first focusable element on every screen, invisible until it receives keyboard focus, and that jumps past the sidebar straight to the page body. Use the wording your language conventionally uses for this accessibility shortcut rather than a word-for-word rendering.

shell.primaryAriaLabel.context: Names the left-hand sidebar region so screen-reader users can jump to it. 'Primary' identifies the page's main landmark region; it does not mean most important. Never seen on screen.

shell.mainNavigationAriaLabel.context: Names the block of sidebar links for screen-reader users, telling them apart from the breadcrumb trail in the header. Never seen on screen.

shell.serviceConsole.context: Subtitle under the product name at the top of the sidebar, shown when the signed-in account can only reach the dashboard and its own submissions — that is, an account acting as a service, the organisational unit that submits data. Two or three words at most: the sidebar is a fixed narrow column.

shell.adminConsole.context: Subtitle under the product name at the top of the sidebar, shown when the signed-in account has back-office screens available to it. Two or three words at most: the sidebar is a fixed narrow column.

shell.navigation.dashboard.context: Sidebar link to the landing screen that summarises current reporting activity. Short noun phrase, no punctuation; users navigate by muscle memory, so the wording should stay stable across releases.

shell.navigation.submissions.context: Sidebar link to the list of submissions, and the matching crumb in the header trail; a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for one reporting period. Plural noun phrase, and the same word must be used wherever the term appears.

shell.navigation.missing.context: Sidebar link to the screen listing reporting periods where an expected submission never arrived. Describes absent submissions, not a mislaid object; keep it to one short word so it fits beside its icon.

shell.navigation.explore.context: Sidebar link to the interactive analysis screen where operators chart and compare reported values. It names a destination rather than issuing an instruction, so use whatever noun or verb your language uses for a data-exploration area.

shell.navigation.reports.context: Sidebar link to the saved reports, and the crumb above a single one; a report is a stored selection of values and periods that can be rendered or exported. Plural noun phrase.

shell.navigation.accounts.context: Sidebar link to the list of every account — people who sign in, automated credentials, and the services that submit data. Deliberately broader than 'services', so avoid narrowing it to users.

shell.navigation.schemas.context: Sidebar link to the list of schemas; a schema is an admin-defined definition of which values a service must report and how often. Use one consistent word for this concept throughout the product.

shell.navigation.events.context: Sidebar link to the timeline of occurrences an administrator has recorded, such as maintenance windows, incidents or deployments. Plural noun phrase.

shell.navigation.audit.context: Sidebar link to the permanent log of who changed what and when. A noun naming that log, not an instruction to audit something.

shell.navigation.tools.context: Sidebar link, pinned near the bottom, to operational utilities such as backup and restore. Plural noun phrase.

shell.navigation.settings.context: Sidebar link, pinned at the bottom, to the configuration area covering email, notifications, webhooks and the default approval policy. Plural noun naming the area, not an imperative.

shell.submissionsClosed.title.context: Headline of a warning strip that stays pinned under the header while an administrator has suspended data entry. Closed means not currently accepting anything; it does not describe a reporting period that has ended.

shell.submissionsClosed.message.en: New submissions and edits from service accounts are temporarily paused.
shell.submissionsClosed.message.context: Body of that warning strip, explaining that accounts acting as services cannot create or change submissions until an administrator lifts the block. Keep the sense that the block is temporary.

shell.login.hint.en: Paste your API key. Only User-kind credentials can sign in here (any role); Application-kind keys are API-only.
shell.login.hint.context: Small grey guidance on the sign-in card telling the reader what to paste into the credential box below. User-kind credentials belong to a person and may sign in whatever their role, while Application-kind keys belong to programs and work only against the API; keep both terms recognisable as the two account kinds. Key here means an access credential.

shell.login.applicationKeyError.en: This API key is for application (non-interactive) use only. Ask an administrator for a User-kind credential to access the admin UI.
shell.login.applicationKeyError.context: Appears after someone tries to sign in with a credential meant for programs, which is deliberately barred from the console. Address the reader directly and keep the instruction to obtain a person-type credential from an administrator.

shell.login.continueWith.context: Caption of one button per configured single-sign-on provider on the sign-in card. Keep the translated part short: the provider's own name is inserted and can be long.

placeholders.provider: Display name of the identity provider, as configured by an administrator, e.g. Contoso Entra ID

shell.login.orUseApiKey.context: Caption sitting on the horizontal rule that separates the single-sign-on buttons from the manual credential form. A lower-case connective phrase offering the alternative underneath; a few words at most, since it has to fit inside the rule.

shell.login.apiKey.context: Label of the masked box where the reader pastes their credential string. Key means an access credential here, never a keyboard key or a database key.

shell.login.couldNotSignIn.context: Headline of the red strip above the sign-in button; the specific reason returned by the server is printed under it. Reports a failed attempt without blaming the reader.

shell.login.verifying.context: Replaces the sign-in caption while the pasted credential is being checked against the server. Present progressive, and it must fit the same button as the resting caption.

shell.login.signIn.context: Submits the credential typed on the sign-in card. Imperative, and the counterpart of the sign-out wording in the account menu.

shell.login.sso.title.context: Headline of the red strip shown when an attempt to sign in through an identity provider did not succeed; the reason follows underneath. Use the established term in your language for signing in once across systems.

shell.login.sso.errors.notLinked.en: That account is not set up for single sign-on here. Ask an administrator to link your identity, or sign in with an API key.
shell.login.sso.errors.notLinked.context: Reason shown when the identity returned by the provider matches no account here. Tell the reader that an administrator has to connect their identity, or that they can fall back to pasting a credential string.

shell.login.sso.errors.noEmail.en: Your identity provider didn't share a verified email, which is required to sign in.
shell.login.sso.errors.noEmail.context: Reason shown when the provider completed the handshake but released no verified email address, which the console needs in order to match the identity to an account. Second person, one sentence.

shell.login.sso.errors.remote.en: Single sign-on was canceled or failed. Please try again.
shell.login.sso.errors.remote.context: Reason shown when the flow at the provider's end was abandoned by the reader or failed there. Neutral wording — nothing is wrong with the account — and it invites another attempt.

shell.login.sso.errors.default.en: Single sign-on did not complete. Please try again.
shell.login.sso.errors.default.context: Fallback reason for a sign-in attempt through a provider that ended without success for a cause the console does not recognise. Stay deliberately vague and invite another attempt.

shell.breadcrumbs.home.context: First crumb of the trail in the header, always pointing back to the landing screen. Short noun; it must read identically on every screen.

shell.breadcrumbs.new.context: Final crumb while a create form is open, following Schemas or Submissions in the trail. Names an item that does not exist yet rather than instructing the reader to create one.

shell.breadcrumbs.edit.context: Final crumb while an existing schema or submission is open for changes. Names the activity under way, so a verbal noun usually reads better here than a bare imperative.

shell.breadcrumbs.view.context: Final crumb while a submission is open read-only, as opposed to the editing trail. Means looking at it without changing anything.

shell.breadcrumbs.status.context: Final crumb of the trail for one service's reporting-status screen, which shows whether the submissions expected from it have arrived. Refers to reporting state, not to an account being enabled or disabled.

shell.breadcrumbs.historicalData.context: Final crumb for the screen showing the values previously reported under a schema, period by period. Noun phrase; short, because a schema name sits in front of it and the trail is shortened when space runs out.

shell.breadcrumbs.submission.context: Stands in for one submission in the middle of the trail and links back to that submission's own screen; submissions have no name of their own to display here. Singular noun.

shell.breadcrumbs.missingSubmissions.context: Crumb for the screen listing reporting periods where an expected submission never arrived. Missing qualifies the submissions themselves.

shell.topBar.pageLocation.context: Names the breadcrumb trail in the header for screen-reader users, so they know the links that follow describe where in the console they currently are. Never seen on screen.

shell.topBar.searchPlaceholder.context: Ghost text inside the empty global search box in the header. A very short prompt; the trailing ellipsis signals that the reader types on.

shell.topBar.searchAriaLabel.context: Accessible name of the header search box, which also advertises the keyboard combination that jumps to it from anywhere. Translate only the word for searching and leave the key combination exactly as written.

shell.topBar.role.context: Hover text on the account button in the header, naming the role the signed-in account holds. Role means the permission template the account was set up with; the role names themselves arrive already translated.

placeholders.role: Already-translated role name of the signed-in account, e.g. Operator

shell.topBar.accountMenu.context: Accessible name of the header button that opens the account menu, used when the account has no display name to include. Never seen on screen.

shell.topBar.accountMenuFor.context: Accessible name of the same header button once a display name is known, so screen-reader users hear whose menu will open. Never seen on screen.

placeholders.name: Friendly label of the signed-in account, or its machine name when no label is set, e.g. A. Rossi

shell.topBar.signOut.context: The single entry in the account menu; it ends the session and returns the reader to the sign-in screen. Imperative, and the counterpart of the sign-in wording.

shell.topBar.scope.names.context: Hover text on the badge that marks a session confined to particular services, listing them by name. 'Can only see' means the data visible in the console, not eyesight.

placeholders.names: Comma-separated names of the services this session may see, e.g. North depot, South depot

shell.topBar.scope.count_one.en: This session is limited to {{count}} service.
shell.topBar.scope.count_one.context: Hover text on the same badge when the services cannot be named, stating only how many there are. Singular form.

placeholders.count: How many services the session may see; in this form always 1

shell.topBar.scope.count_other.en: This session is limited to {{count}} services.
shell.topBar.scope.count_other.context: Hover text on the same badge when the services cannot be named, stating only how many there are. Plural form.

placeholders.count: How many services the session may see, e.g. 4

shell.topBar.scope.badge_one.context: Badge in the header warning that the session shows only part of the estate, so a partial list is never mistaken for the whole. Must stay very short — the badge does not wrap — and the middle dot separates the warning from the count. Singular form.

placeholders.count: How many services the session may see; in this form always 1

shell.topBar.scope.badge_other.context: Badge in the header warning that the session shows only part of the estate, so a partial list is never mistaken for the whole. Must stay very short — the badge does not wrap — and the middle dot separates the warning from the count. Plural form.

placeholders.count: How many services the session may see, e.g. 4

shell.account.label.context: Fallback on the header account button when the signed-in account has neither a display name nor a role: it becomes the hover text and the source of the initials in the round avatar, so the opening letters do appear on screen. Refers to the reader's own account, not to accounting.

shell.account.kinds.User.context: One of the two kinds an account can have: it belongs to a person and can sign in to the console. Shown as a compact label in search results and spoken as part of an avatar's accessible name, so keep it to a single word.

shell.account.kinds.Application.context: The other account kind: a credential used by a program or script, able to call the API but barred from signing in to the console. A single compact word, contrasting with the person-type kind.

shell.account.roles.Service.context: Role of an account that stands for an organisational unit reporting data — the origin of submissions rather than a back-office user. Appears under the account name in the header, in search results and inside accessible names, so keep it to one word.

shell.account.roles.Operator.context: Role of a back-office user who works with submissions, reports and schemas day to day without administering the system. One word, shown in the same tight places as the other roles.

shell.account.roles.Admin.context: Role of a user with full administrative reach over configuration and accounts. An established short form is welcome here, since the space beside the account name is narrow.

shell.account.roles.Approver.context: Role of a user who signs off submissions so they count as final. Use the same term as elsewhere for the person who approves a submission, and keep it to one word.

shell.search.title.context: Heading of the global search screen, and the trailing breadcrumb segment while that screen is open. Here the word is a noun naming the feature, not the imperative verb on the button beside the input box, so use the noun form even where the language distinguishes them.

shell.search.placeholder.en: Search actions, schemas, values, events, accounts…
shell.search.placeholder.context: Ghost text in the global search box. It enumerates what the box finds: task shortcuts, schemas (admin-defined definitions of what a service reports), the individual values a schema defines, timeline events, accounts and report definitions. Keep the trailing ellipsis, and keep the list short enough to fit one line — drop an item rather than let it wrap.

shell.search.button.context: Caption of the primary button that runs the search. Imperative — an instruction to search now — unlike the identically worded screen heading, which is a noun.

shell.search.hint.en: Type what you want to do (for example “add user”, “submit”, “scorecard”) or the name of a schema, value, event, account or report.
shell.search.hint.context: Guidance shown under the search box before anything has been typed, explaining that the box accepts either an intent or the name of an object. The three quoted examples are phrases a user would actually type, so replace them with natural equivalents in the target language and keep them consistent with the search keyword lists for the same shortcuts; use the quotation marks the language normally uses.

shell.search.searching.context: Sits beside a small spinner inside a result-block heading while that category's results are still being fetched. Present progressive, keeping the trailing ellipsis; a heading leaves little room, so one or two words.

shell.search.viewAll.context: Caption of the link at the foot of a result block that leaves the search screen and opens the full list for that category. This is the generic fallback used when no counted variant applies. Imperative.

shell.search.valueCount_one.context: Secondary line under a schema in the search results, used when that schema has no display label: it counts the values the schema defines. A value here is one data field a service reports for the schema, never a monetary amount. One line only, truncated with an ellipsis if it does not fit.

placeholders.count: Number of values defined by the schema, e.g. 1

shell.search.valueCount_other.context: Plural form of the secondary line under a schema in the search results, counting the values the schema defines. A value is one data field a service reports for that schema, never a monetary amount. One line only, truncated with an ellipsis if it does not fit.

placeholders.count: Number of values defined by the schema, e.g. 12

shell.search.viewAllSchemas_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the schema results that opens the full schema catalogue. The count is the total number of schemas that matched, which is larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching schemas, e.g. 1

shell.search.viewAllSchemas_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the schema results that opens the full schema catalogue. The count is the total number of schemas that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching schemas, e.g. 23

shell.search.inSchema.context: Secondary line under a matched schema value in the search results, naming the schema that defines it. The preposition is locative — it says which schema the value belongs to, not a time or a manner. One truncated line.

placeholders.schema: Display label of the schema, falling back to its technical name, e.g. Monthly service KPIs

shell.search.matchingValues_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the schema-values results, which opens the schema that defines the best match. 'Matching' means matching the term the user typed; a value is one data field defined by a schema. Reads as a link, so keep it terse.

placeholders.count: Total number of schema values that matched the search term, e.g. 1

shell.search.matchingValues_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the schema-values results, which opens the schema that defines the best match. 'Matching' means matching the term the user typed; a value is one data field defined by a schema.

placeholders.count: Total number of schema values that matched the search term, e.g. 14

shell.search.accountKindRole.context: Secondary line under an account in the search results, pairing what kind of account it is with the role it holds. Both parts arrive already translated, so only the order and the separator are yours; the spaces on either side of the middle dot are load-bearing and the dot itself is not a full stop.

placeholders.kind: Account kind, already translated from its own list, e.g. Person
placeholders.role: Account role, already translated from its own list, e.g. Approver

joins.note: Both halves are substituted in; keep a space before and after the middle dot. CJK may use a full-width separator instead, but must not run the two halves together.

shell.search.viewAllAccounts_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the account results that opens the full account list. The count is the total number of accounts that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching accounts, e.g. 1

shell.search.viewAllAccounts_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the account results that opens the full account list. The count is the total number of accounts that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching accounts, e.g. 42

shell.search.eventSummaryRich.context: Secondary line under a timeline event in the search results: what kind of event it was, then when it happened. Keep the tag exactly as written, including the slash and the spacing inside it, and do not translate it — it is replaced at display time by the date and time formatted for the reader's locale. The two parts may be reordered if that reads better.

placeholders.kind: Event kind, already translated from its own list, e.g. Incident

joins.after: The event kind, followed by a rendered timestamp element in place of the tag
joins.note: The spaces around the middle dot are load-bearing; the dot is a separator, not a full stop, so the line takes no final punctuation.

shell.search.viewAllEvents_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the event results that opens the full events timeline. The count is the total number of events that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching events, e.g. 1

shell.search.viewAllEvents_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the event results that opens the full events timeline. The count is the total number of events that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching events, e.g. 37

shell.search.viewAllReports_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the report results that opens the full report catalogue. The count is the total number of report definitions that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching report definitions, e.g. 1

shell.search.viewAllReports_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the report results that opens the full report catalogue. The count is the total number of report definitions that matched, larger than the handful listed above it. Imperative.

placeholders.count: Total number of matching report definitions, e.g. 9

shell.search.submissionSummaryRich.context: Secondary line under a submission in the search results: which schemas the submitted data covers, then when it was sent in. Keep the tag exactly as written, including the slash, and do not translate it — it is replaced at display time by the submission date and time formatted for the reader's locale.

placeholders.schemas: Comma-separated list of the schema names the submission covers, or the 'no schemas' wording when it covers none, e.g. Monthly service KPIs, Safety

joins.after: The schema list, followed by a rendered timestamp element in place of the tag
joins.note: The spaces around the middle dot are load-bearing; the whole line is truncated with an ellipsis when it does not fit, so keep it lean.

shell.search.noSchemas.context: Takes the place of the schema list in the submission summary line when a submission references no schema at all. It reports an absence rather than an error, and it shares one truncated line with the submission's date, so keep it to two or three words.

joins.before: The middle-dot separator and the rendered submission timestamp supplied by the summary line
joins.note: Substituted into the surrounding string, which supplies the separator and its spacing; add no punctuation of your own.

shell.search.recentMatches_one.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the submission results that opens the full submission list. Only recently submitted data is scanned, which is what 'recent' qualifies — the count is how many of those matched, not how many exist in total.

placeholders.count: Number of recent submissions that matched the search term, e.g. 1

shell.search.recentMatches_other.context: Plural form of the link at the foot of the submission results that opens the full submission list. Only recently submitted data is scanned, which is what 'recent' qualifies — the count is how many of those matched, not how many exist in total.

placeholders.count: Number of recent submissions that matched the search term, e.g. 18

shell.search.noResults.en: No results for “{{query}}”. Try a different term.
shell.search.noResults.context: Replaces every result block when the typed term matched nothing at all, not even a task shortcut. It is not an error: the second sentence invites the reader to rephrase, so keep it as friendly advice in the second person. Keep the typographic quotation marks the language uses around the term.

placeholders.query: The search term exactly as the user typed it, including any typing mistakes, e.g. montly kpi

shell.search.sections.actions.context: Heading of the result block listing task shortcuts — rows that jump to a screen or open a create form directly. 'Actions' means things the user can go and do, never actions that already happened; a count badge follows the heading, and it is also the block's accessible name.

shell.search.sections.schemas.context: Heading of the result block listing matching schemas. A schema is an admin-defined definition of what a service has to report, so use the same term as everywhere else in the console; a count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.sections.schemaValues.context: Heading of the result block listing individual values matched inside schemas, as opposed to the schemas themselves in the block above. A value is one data field a schema defines; a count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.sections.accounts.context: Heading of the result block listing matching accounts — the people, applications and services that can sign in or send data in. A count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.sections.events.context: Heading of the result block listing matching timeline events, such as incidents, maintenance or deployments recorded against the data. A count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.sections.reports.context: Heading of the result block listing matching report definitions, i.e. the templates that can be rendered, not rendered output. A count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.sections.submissions.context: Heading of the result block listing matching submissions. A submission is one filled-in set of data a service has sent in for a reporting period; a count badge follows the heading.

shell.search.reportType.single.context: Secondary line under a report in the search results, saying that this report definition renders one chosen submission. Keep it clearly distinct from the aggregate type that appears in the same list; 'single' counts submissions, not schemas. One truncated line, no final period.

shell.search.reportType.aggregate.context: Secondary line under a report in the search results, saying that this report definition combines many submissions rather than rendering one. Keep it clearly distinct from the single-submission type that appears in the same list. One truncated line, no final period.

shell.search.actions.submission-new.titl.context: Row in the task-shortcut list that opens the form for entering a submission — one filled-in set of data for a service and a reporting period. A noun phrase naming what gets created, and it should match how the same action is worded elsewhere in the console.

shell.search.actions.submission-new.desc.en: Submit KPI data for a service
shell.search.actions.submission-new.desc.context: One-line hint under that shortcut. 'Submit' means sending the reported figures in for a period, and 'service' is the organisational unit the figures belong to. Single line, no final period.

shell.search.actions.submission-new.keyw.context: Never displayed: a list of extra terms the search matches against, alongside the visible title, so that typing an intent finds this shortcut. Replace each entry with what someone would really type in the target language for entering data — including short forms and near synonyms — rather than translating word for word; you may add or remove entries, but keep the vertical bars as separators and keep everything lowercase.

shell.search.actions.schema-new.title.context: Row in the task-shortcut list that opens the form for creating a schema, i.e. a new definition of what services must report. Imperative in the same register as a button, matching the wording used for the same action on the schema screens.

shell.search.actions.schema-new.descript.context: One-line hint under that shortcut. 'Create' is the act of defining a new schema from scratch, as distinct from filling one in. Single line, no final period.

shell.search.actions.schema-new.keywords.context: Never displayed: extra terms the search matches against so that typing an intent finds this shortcut for defining a new schema. Use the words someone would really type in the target language, including the local term for a KPI definition, rather than a word-for-word translation; keep the vertical bars as separators and keep everything lowercase.

shell.search.actions.account-new-user.ti.context: Row in the task-shortcut list that opens the account list ready to create a person's account. 'User' means a human who signs in to the console, in contrast to the service account shortcut listed next to it. Imperative, matching the wording on the accounts screen.

shell.search.actions.account-new-user.de.context: One-line hint under that shortcut. An account is a sign-in identity in the console; this one is for a person rather than for a service that sends data. Single line, no final period.
