placeholders.error: Raw technical reason the file could not be read or parsed, in English, e.g. Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0

tools.accountsBackup.confirmImport.en:
Import accounts from this file?

Accounts are matched by name: existing ones are updated and new names are created. Accounts not in the file are left untouched.

API keys are NOT included in the file, so any account created by this import starts with no key — generate one for each afterwards.
tools.accountsBackup.confirmImport.context: Confirmation asked in a plain browser dialog before an accounts file is imported: accounts are matched by their identifier, so existing ones are updated and unknown identifiers create new accounts, while accounts absent from the file are left alone. The last paragraph warns that no API key comes with the file, so every account the import creates has no credential until one is issued for it. Keep the emphasis on NOT and the blank lines between paragraphs.

tools.accountsBackup.keysNeverExported.context: Emphasised opening of the standing warning on the accounts card: no secret credential ever leaves the system in an exported file. A key here is an API credential, never a keyboard or database key.

joins.before: The rest of the paragraph, starting 'They aren't stored in a recoverable form …'
joins.example: API keys are never exported. They aren't stored in a recoverable form, so an imported account starts with no key and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate. Import is non-destructive — accounts missing from the file are left as they are.
joins.note: Rendered bold and it keeps its own full stop; one space is inserted before the next piece, which refers back to the keys named here.

tools.accountsBackup.warningBeforeNoKey.en: They aren't stored in a recoverable form, so an imported account starts with
tools.accountsBackup.warningBeforeNoKey.context: Explains why: keys are held only in a form that cannot be turned back into the original secret, so there is nothing to export. It breaks off before an emphasised phrase.

joins.after: The emphasised sentence stating that API keys are never exported
joins.before: The emphasised phrase meaning that the account has no credential at all
joins.example: API keys are never exported. They aren't stored in a recoverable form, so an imported account starts with no key and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate.
joins.note: The pronoun at the start refers to the keys named in the previous piece, so use whatever agreement your language needs. Leave the sentence open so the bold phrase can complete it.

tools.accountsBackup.noKey.context: The emphasised phrase describing the state of an account created by an import: it holds no credential whatsoever and therefore cannot authenticate yet.

joins.after: The words '… an imported account starts with'
joins.before: The clause 'and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate.'
joins.example: … so an imported account starts with no key and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate.
joins.note: Rendered bold with a space on each side; keep it to two or three words.

tools.accountsBackup.warningAfterNoKey.en: and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate. Import is non-destructive — accounts missing from the file are left as they are.
tools.accountsBackup.warningAfterNoKey.context: Ends the warning: someone must issue a fresh key for each imported account before it can prove who it is, and the import itself destroys nothing — accounts the file does not mention stay exactly as they were. 'Non-destructive' is the reassurance that nothing is deleted.

joins.after: The emphasised phrase meaning that the account has no credential
joins.example: … an imported account starts with no key and must have one re-generated before it can authenticate. Import is non-destructive — accounts missing from the file are left as they are.
joins.note: A space is inserted before it and it supplies the closing full stop; nothing follows.

tools.accountsBackup.importCompleteBefor.context: Opens the green bar reporting the outcome of an accounts import; the figures follow immediately after the colon. Keep it short, and keep the colon that introduces them.

joins.before: The number of accounts created, in bold, then the word for created
joins.note: One space is inserted after it, before the first figure.

tools.accountsBackup.created.context: Follows the first figure in that summary, saying those accounts did not exist before and were added. Past participle agreeing with the counted accounts, and it must work for any number including zero and one.

joins.after: The number of accounts created, rendered in bold
joins.before: A comma, then the number of accounts updated and the word for updated
joins.note: The comma is supplied by the surrounding text, so do not add punctuation.

tools.accountsBackup.updated.context: Follows the second figure in that summary, saying those accounts already existed and were changed to match the file. Past participle agreeing with the counted accounts, and it must work for any number including zero and one.

joins.after: The number of accounts updated, rendered in bold
joins.note: The closing full stop is supplied by the surrounding text, so do not add punctuation. Any rejected entries are listed underneath as a separate bulleted list.

tools.accountsBackup.download.context: Primary button that produces the accounts file and saves it to the administrator's machine; no secret credential is ever included. Imperative and short.

reports.title.context: Heading of the screen listing every report definition. A report is an administrator-uploaded template that turns collected submission data into a formatted document; plural noun, not the act of reporting.

reports.singular.context: Stand-in heading on the single-report viewer, shown only until that report's own name has loaded. Singular noun naming one report definition.

reports.actions.more.context: Announced for the three-dot toolbar button above the report list, which opens a menu holding Refresh and Upload report. Name the menu, not the icon.

reports.actions.refresh.context: Menu entry that re-fetches the list of reports from the server. Imperative, as a command the user gives.

reports.actions.upload.context: Menu entry that opens a file picker so an administrator can add a new report template. Upload means sending a file to the server; visible only to administrators.

reports.actions.view.context: Row-level menu entry that opens the chosen report in the viewer. Imperative.

reports.actions.delete.context: Row-level menu entry that permanently removes a report definition; shown in red and confirmed first. Imperative.

reports.messages.loadFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when the list of reports could not be fetched; the server's own error text is printed underneath it, so keep this to a short summary.

reports.messages.actionFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when an upload or a delete did not go through; the underlying error detail is printed underneath it.

reports.messages.loading.context: Fills the whole width of the otherwise empty report table while the list is being fetched. Progress, not an error.

reports.messages.empty.context: Fills the report table when no report has been uploaded yet, for users who are not allowed to add one, so it offers no next step.

reports.messages.emptyAdmin.en: No reports yet — click “Upload report” to add one.
reports.messages.emptyAdmin.context: Fills the report table when nothing has been uploaded yet, for administrators who may add one. The quoted part names the Upload report menu entry and must match that translation word for word; keep the curly quotation marks.

reports.fields.name.context: Column holding each report's display name, with its description underneath. Long names are cut off with an ellipsis, so keep the header itself very short.

reports.fields.type.context: Column showing whether a report is Single or Aggregate. The column is fixed at roughly 120 pixels.

reports.fields.targets.context: Column listing the schemas a report is allowed to run against, as small chips; reports with no restriction show Global instead. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition.

reports.fields.created.context: Column with the date the report was uploaded. Narrow, roughly 110 pixels, and it holds a date, so keep the header to one short word.

reports.fields.createdBy.context: Column naming the account that uploaded the report. Roughly 140 pixels wide.

reports.fields.actions.context: Right-aligned header above the narrow column that holds each row's three-dot menu. Roughly 80 pixels, so one short word.

reports.types.single.context: Badge marking a report that renders exactly one submission, which the user picks before rendering. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a period. Contrasts with Aggregate; one word, badges do not wrap.

reports.types.aggregate.context: Badge marking a report that combines many submissions across a chosen span of time rather than showing a single one. Contrasts with Single; one word, badges do not wrap.

reports.targets.global.context: Badge shown in the Targets column when a report is tied to no particular schema and can therefore be run against any of them. Global means unrestricted in scope, not worldwide.

reports.validation.emptyFile.context: Appears in the error bar after an administrator picks a file for upload whose contents are blank; the upload is abandoned and nothing is saved.

reports.aria.open.context: Announced for a clickable row in the report list; activating the row opens that report in the viewer.

placeholders.name: Display name of the report, e.g. Quarterly availability

reports.aria.actionsFor.context: Announced for the three-dot button at the end of a report row, which opens that row's own menu.

placeholders.name: Internal name of the report, e.g. quarterly-availability

reports.confirmDelete.en:
Delete report "{{target}}"?

This cannot be undone.
reports.confirmDelete.context: Whole text of the browser's own confirmation box before a report definition is removed. Plain text with no formatting: keep both line breaks so the warning stays on its own paragraph, and state plainly that the removal is permanent.

placeholders.target: Display name of the report about to be deleted, e.g. Quarterly availability

reports.view.back.context: Returns from a single report to the list of all reports. Imperative navigation, paired with a left arrow.

reports.view.loadFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when the report definition itself could not be fetched, so nothing can be rendered; the server's error text follows underneath.

reports.view.loading.context: Sits beside a spinner while the report definition is being fetched. Short progress text on one line, in the same present progressive as other in-flight messages.

reports.view.schema.context: Labels the filter that chooses which schema's data the report is run against. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition; the filter is hidden when the report allows only one.

reports.view.pickGlobalSchema.context: Ghost text in the empty schema dropdown when the report is not restricted to particular schemas, so every schema in the system is on offer. The parenthesis explains why the list is so long.

reports.view.pickSchema.context: Ghost text in the empty schema dropdown when the report names several allowed schemas and the user must choose one of them. The ellipsis marks it as a prompt to act.

reports.view.period.context: Labels the dropdown choosing the span of time whose data the report covers. Period here is a reporting window, never a punctuation mark.

reports.view.periods.thisMonth.context: Time-span choice covering the first day of the current calendar month up to now. Noun phrase naming a choice.

reports.view.periods.lastWeek.context: Time-span choice covering the seven days ending now. It is a rolling count of days, not the previous calendar week, so keep the number.

reports.view.periods.lastMonth.context: Time-span choice covering the thirty days ending now. A rolling count of days, not the previous calendar month, so keep the number.

reports.view.periods.lastYear.context: Time-span choice covering the three hundred and sixty-five days ending now. A rolling count of days, not the previous calendar year, so keep the number.

reports.view.periods.custom.context: Time-span choice that reveals the From and To inputs so the user can name the two ends of the window themselves. Range means a span between two moments in time.

reports.view.from.context: Labels the date-and-time input that sets the earlier end of a custom reporting window. Paired with To.

reports.view.to.context: Labels the date-and-time input that sets the later end of a custom reporting window. Paired with From.

reports.view.submission.context: Labels the dropdown choosing the one submission a Single report is rendered from. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema, sent in by a service for a reporting window.

reports.view.submissionOption.context: One row of the submission dropdown, and the collapsed text shown once a row is chosen, identifying a submission by who sent it, when, and how big it is. A sample is one recorded data point inside the submission; the count has no separate plural form, so word it to read correctly for any number.

placeholders.service: Name of the service that sent the submission, e.g. Payments API
placeholders.date: Already-formatted date and time the submission was received, e.g. 11 Aug 2026, 14:32
placeholders.count: How many samples the submission contains, e.g. 24

reports.view.submissionOptionRich.context: The same submission row, rendered with the timestamp as a live element instead of pre-formatted text. Keep the self-closing submittedAt tag exactly as written, and move it if the target language needs a different word order; the date it produces is formatted for the reader's locale. A sample is one recorded data point inside the submission, and the count has no separate plural form.

placeholders.service: Name of the service that sent the submission, e.g. Payments API
placeholders.count: How many samples the submission contains, e.g. 24

reports.view.noMatchingSubmissions.context: Ghost text in the submission dropdown when nothing sent in falls inside the chosen window or uses the chosen schema, so there is nothing to pick until the filters above are loosened. States an absence, not a failure.

reports.view.pickSubmission.context: Ghost text in the submission dropdown while submissions are available but none has been chosen yet. The ellipsis marks it as a prompt to act.

reports.view.rendering.context: Takes the place of the Render caption while the server is producing the document. Must fit the same button as the resting caption.

reports.view.render.context: Produces the finished document from the report template and the data selected by the filters above. Imperative; render means generating a formatted result, not artistic depiction. Stays disabled until the required filters are set.

reports.view.renderFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when the server could not produce the document from the chosen data; the underlying error text follows underneath.

reports.view.frameTitle.context: Accessible name of the frame holding the produced document; never visible on screen, only announced by screen readers. The leading word identifies what the frame contains.

placeholders.name: Display name of the report that was rendered, e.g. Quarterly availability

reports.view.collapse.context: Leaves the full-window view of the produced document and returns it to its place in the page. Imperative; the opposite of Expand.

reports.view.expand.context: Enlarges the produced document to fill the whole browser window. Imperative; the opposite of Collapse.

reports.view.openNewTab.context: Opens the produced document in a separate browser tab, which is how users print or share it. Imperative; tab here is a browser tab, not a tab strip in the console.

reports.view.download.context: Saves the produced document to the reader's own computer as a self-contained file. Imperative; appears in both the inline and the full-window toolbar, so it must read the same in each.

schemasSubmissions.approval.appliesTo.context: Labels the dropdown narrowing an approval policy to submissions that arrived a particular way — typed into the web console by a person, or sent programmatically through the API. Reads as the start of the sentence completed by the chosen option.

schemasSubmissions.approval.appliesToHin.en: You can require approval for only manual entries, only API submissions, or both.
schemasSubmissions.approval.appliesToHin.context: Explains the three choices in the dropdown above. A manual entry is one a person typed into the web console; an API submission is one a script or integration sent in. Addresses the administrator directly.

schemasSubmissions.approval.approvers.context: Labels the multi-select listing the accounts allowed to sign off submissions governed by this policy. An approver is a person or account that reviews a submission and decides whether it may go live.

schemasSubmissions.approval.approversHin.en: Pick who may review: the Approver/Admin accounts below, and/or the service owner (the account that sent the submission, so a service can sign off on its own data). Mark at least one as Required; the submission goes live once every Required approver has approved.
schemasSubmissions.approval.approversHin.context: The main explanation of how sign-off works: who may be chosen, that the service owner is the account that sent the submission in, and that a submission only becomes live once every approver marked Required has approved. Approver, Admin, Required and the going-live rule must match the wording used for those terms elsewhere in this area. Several sentences, so it is not tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.approval.globalDefaul.en: This follows the global default approval policy, configured in Settings — Approval.
schemasSubmissions.approval.globalDefaul.context: Blue information bar shown once the mode is set to defer to the server-wide default, telling the administrator that the rules now come from elsewhere and where to change them. The trailing path names a settings screen and its Approval section, so use the same translations those screens use.

schemasSubmissions.approval.heading.context: Bold heading above the block of controls that decide whether submissions must be signed off before they count. Noun naming the feature, not a command to approve anything.

schemasSubmissions.approval.mode.globalD.context: Mode choice leaving this schema without an opinion of its own: whatever the server-wide default policy says at the time applies. Imperative phrasing that names a choice.

schemasSubmissions.approval.mode.none.context: Mode choice meaning submissions go live the moment they are accepted, with nobody signing off. The default for existing schemas.

schemasSubmissions.approval.mode.require.context: Mode choice meaning submissions are held back until the approvers named just below have signed off. Required here describes the approval step, not a mandatory form field.

schemasSubmissions.approval.modeHint.en: Submissions in scope are held as Pending until approved, and excluded from the OData feed and Explore until then. Defaults to no approval for backwards compatibility.
schemasSubmissions.approval.modeHint.context: Explains the consequence of turning approval on: an affected submission sits in the Pending state, and its figures stay out of the machine-readable data feed and the data-exploration screen until somebody approves it. Pending, the feed name and Explore are all named elsewhere in the console and must match.

schemasSubmissions.approval.modeLabel.context: Labels the dropdown choosing whether submissions for this schema need signing off at all. Mode here means which of three fixed policies applies.

schemasSubmissions.approval.modifiableHe.en: Re-submitting data for a window that already has a submission replaces it and resets its approval status to Pending — even if it was previously approved. While it waits for re-approval it drops out of the OData feed and Explore. If you don't want re-submissions to disturb approved data, mark the schema as not modifiable.
schemasSubmissions.approval.modifiableHe.context: Body of an orange caution shown when a schema both requires approval and allows its submissions to be replaced. Explains that sending data again for a reporting window that already has a submission overwrites it and puts it back into the Pending state, so previously approved figures temporarily disappear from the data feed and the exploration screen. Modifiable is the name of a schema setting shown elsewhere; keep it recognisable.

schemasSubmissions.approval.modifiableTi.en: Heads up: this schema is modifiable
schemasSubmissions.approval.modifiableTi.context: Headline of that orange caution. An informal attention-getter followed by the fact that triggered it; keep it short and use whatever natural equivalent of a friendly warning the target language has rather than translating word for word.

schemasSubmissions.approval.requiredVali.en: Add at least one Required approver.
schemasSubmissions.approval.requiredVali.context: Warning under the approver picker while every chosen approver is only optional, which the server refuses to save. Required is the name of the setting on each approver row; keep it recognisable as that same word.

schemasSubmissions.approval.requirement..context: One of two radio buttons on an approver's row: this person may sign off, but the submission can go live without them. Paired with Required; both sit side by side on a narrow row, so keep them short.

One of two radio buttons on an approver's row: the submission stays held until this person has approved it. Paired with Optional; describes the approver, not a mandatory form field, and both sit side by side on a narrow row.

schemasSubmissions.approval.selectApprov.context: Ghost text in the empty approver picker before anybody has been chosen. Once choices are made it is replaced by their names, joined with commas.

schemasSubmissions.approval.serviceOwner.context: Entry at the top of the approver picker standing for no fixed person: whichever service sent a given submission signs off on its own data. A service is an organisational unit that submits data; the parenthesis explains which account that resolves to. Also reused as the row label once chosen.

schemasSubmissions.approval.source.apiOn.context: Scope choice applying the policy only to submissions sent programmatically through the API, leaving anything typed into the web console to go live unchecked.

schemasSubmissions.approval.source.both.context: Scope choice applying the policy to every submission however it arrived. The default.

schemasSubmissions.approval.source.manua.context: Scope choice applying the policy only to submissions a person typed into the web console, leaving programmatic ones to go live unchecked. The parenthesis says where manual entry happens.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.chooseServ.context: Ghost text in the empty service dropdown of the import dialog. Every submission in one imported file is credited to this one service, an organisational unit that submits data.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.failed.context: Last of up to three sentences making up the result bar after an import, counting the submissions that were rejected and are listed individually underneath. It is appended after the sentences before it with a single space, so it must stand as a complete sentence on its own.

placeholders.count: How many submissions in the file were rejected, e.g. 2

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.file.context: Labels the file-picker row where the administrator chooses the JSON or CSV file to import. Names the thing being chosen.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.format.context: Labels the dropdown stating how the chosen file is laid out, JSON or CSV. Format means the file's structure, not visual formatting.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.formatHint.en: Auto-detected from the file extension; override if needed.
schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.formatHint.context: Explains that the dropdown above fills itself in from the file's extension and that the administrator may change it. Second person, addressed to the administrator.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.formats.cs.context: File-layout choice for a comma-separated table of rows. A recognised file-format name: leave it exactly as it is in every language.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.formats.js.context: File-layout choice for a structured JSON document. A recognised file-format name: leave it exactly as it is in every language.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.group.context: Bold first part of a line in the per-submission report, identifying one imported submission by the label its own rows carried in the file. Group is a column in the imported file whose value buckets rows together into one submission; the quoted value is written by whoever made the file and is never translated. A failure note may be appended to the same line.

placeholders.name: The group value taken verbatim from the imported file, e.g. north-depot

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.help.en: Import historical submissions for a single service from a JSON or CSV file. Parsing must succeed for the whole file; each submission is then validated and saved independently, so a rejected one won't block the rest. Submissions that already exist are skipped, so re-running the same file is safe.
schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.help.context: Paragraph at the top of the import dialog explaining how a run behaves: the file must be readable from end to end before anything is written, after which each submission stands or falls on its own, and anything already recorded for the same reporting window is passed over so running the same file twice changes nothing. Not tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.import.context: Confirming button of the dialog; reads the chosen file and writes its submissions. Imperative; import means bringing outside data into the product.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.importing.context: Takes the place of the Import caption while the file is being processed. Must fit the same button as the resting caption.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.itemFailed.context: Tail of a line in the per-submission report, marking that submission as rejected and saying how big it was; the reasons are listed underneath. A sample is one recorded data point. The bracketed plural marker is the English way of covering one and many at once — drop it and use whatever reads correctly for any number in the target language.

placeholders.count: How many samples that rejected submission contained, e.g. 3

joins.after: The bold group name or submission number that starts the same line, plus one space
joins.note: Keeps its leading bracket and the spaced dash before the final word; both are part of the visual pattern.

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.skipped.context: Middle of up to three sentences making up the result bar after an import, counting the submissions passed over because the same reporting window had already been recorded. Skipped means deliberately left alone, not lost or failed. Appended after the sentence before it with a single space, so it must stand as a complete sentence on its own.

placeholders.count: How many submissions were passed over as already present, e.g. 4

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.submission.context: Bold first part of a line in the per-submission report, used instead of a group name when the file gave the submission no label; the number is its position in the file counting from one. Keep the hash sign or the target language's usual ordinal marker. A failure note may be appended to the same line.

placeholders.number: Position of the submission within the imported file, counting from one, e.g. 3

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.summary.context: Opening sentence of the result bar after an import, reporting how many of the file's submissions were written. Two further sentences about skipped and rejected ones may be appended after it, so it must end cleanly. The bracketed plural marker is the English way of covering one and many at once; use whatever reads correctly for any number instead.

placeholders.succeeded: How many submissions were written successfully, e.g. 8
placeholders.total: How many submissions the file contained in all, e.g. 10

schemasSubmissions.bulkImport.title.context: Heading of the administrator-only dialog that loads past submissions for one service from a file. Import means bringing outside data into the product; a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a reporting window.

schemasSubmissions.comments.comment.context: Names what is about to be deleted inside the browser's own confirmation box; it is dropped into a ready-made sentence after the verb. Capitalised in English only because it starts the source string — it lands mid-sentence, so use the casing, article and grammatical case your language needs after the verb for deleting. A comment is one message a reviewer wrote in a discussion thread.

joins.after: The verb of the delete-confirmation sentence, which supplies the question mark and the consequence line
joins.example:
Delete Comment?

This cannot be undone.
joins.note: Only this noun is translated here; the surrounding sentence comes from a separate string.

schemasSubmissions.comments.deleteThread.context: Entry in a thread's own menu that removes the whole discussion and every message in it, after a confirmation. Imperative; a thread is one discussion about a schema or one of its values.

schemasSubmissions.comments.deleteThread.en: This deletes every comment in the thread. This cannot be undone.
schemasSubmissions.comments.deleteThread.context: Consequence line of the confirmation box shown before a whole discussion is removed, replacing the usual generic warning. Says plainly that every message goes, not only the one being looked at.

schemasSubmissions.comments.edited.context: Quiet marker in the small grey line above a message, saying its author changed the text after posting it. Past participle describing the message, not an instruction; keep the brackets and keep it very short.

joins.after: The author's name and the message's timestamp, laid out in the same row with a small gap
joins.note: Spacing comes from the layout, so the string itself needs no leading space.

schemasSubmissions.comments.empty.context: Centred grey line in the comments panel when the schema has no discussions at all. The composer above it already offers the next step, so this only states the absence.

schemasSubmissions.comments.general.context: Top choice in the picker deciding what a new discussion is about: the schema as a whole rather than one particular value in it. All the other choices are the schema's own value names. Also shown as the collapsed text once chosen, and echoed on a narrow badge, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.comments.loading.context: Sits beside a spinner while the discussions on this schema are being fetched. Short progress text on one line.

schemasSubmissions.comments.newThread.context: Bold heading of the card at the top of the panel where a new discussion is started. Noun phrase naming what the card creates, not a command.

schemasSubmissions.comments.open.context: Amber badge on a discussion that is still live and accepting replies. An adjective describing the state, never the verb for opening something; the opposite state is Resolved. One word, badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.comments.post.context: Confirming button of the new-discussion card; publishes the typed text as the first message of a new thread. Imperative verb meaning to publish a message, not the noun for mail or a job position.

schemasSubmissions.comments.reopen.context: Entry in a resolved discussion's menu that moves it from Resolved back to Open so people can reply again. Imperative. This concerns a discussion only; reopening a submission is a separate action with its own wording.

schemasSubmissions.comments.reply.context: Confirming button under an open discussion; adds the typed text as another message in that same thread. Imperative verb, not the noun for an answer.

schemasSubmissions.comments.replyPlaceho.context: Ghost text in the empty box for adding another message to an existing discussion. The ellipsis marks it as a prompt to start typing.

schemasSubmissions.comments.required.context: Red line under a message box when the user tries to post, reply or save an edit with nothing typed in. Required here means the box must not be left empty.

schemasSubmissions.comments.resolve.context: Entry in an open discussion's menu that moves it from Open to Resolved, closing it to further replies until somebody reopens it. Imperative; resolve means settling the matter under discussion, not computing or looking something up.

schemasSubmissions.comments.resolved.context: Green badge on a discussion that has been settled and is no longer accepting replies. Past participle describing the state; the opposite state is Open. One word, badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.comments.resolvedCanR.en: This thread is resolved — reopen it to add another comment.
schemasSubmissions.comments.resolvedCanR.context: Italic line with a padlock at the foot of a settled discussion, shown to people who are allowed to reopen it and telling them that is what they must do first. Reopen must match the wording of the menu entry that performs it.

schemasSubmissions.comments.resolvedRead.context: Italic line with a padlock at the foot of a settled discussion, shown to people who cannot reopen it and therefore offered no next step. States the fact only.

schemasSubmissions.comments.scope.context: Labels the picker choosing what a new discussion is attached to: the whole schema, or one named value inside it. Scope here means the subject a discussion is filed under.

schemasSubmissions.comments.thread.context: Names what is about to be deleted inside the browser's own confirmation box; it is dropped into a ready-made sentence after the verb. Capitalised in English only because it starts the source string — it lands mid-sentence, so use the casing, article and grammatical case your language needs after the verb for deleting. A thread is one whole discussion, made up of an opening message and its replies.

joins.after: The verb of the delete-confirmation sentence, which supplies the question mark and the consequence line
joins.example:
Delete Thread?

This deletes every comment in the thread. This cannot be undone.
joins.note: Only this noun is translated here; the surrounding sentence comes from a separate string.

schemasSubmissions.comments.threadAction.context: Announced for the small three-dot button on a discussion's header, which opens that discussion's own menu of resolve, reopen and delete. Name the menu, not the icon.

schemasSubmissions.comments.title.context: Heading of the side panel holding every discussion on a schema. The same word also captions the toolbar button that opens the panel and heads a narrow table column counting open discussions, so keep it to one short plural noun that works in all three.

schemasSubmissions.comments.unknown.context: Stands in for a message's author when the account that wrote it can no longer be identified, for instance because it was removed. Also feeds the initials on the round avatar beside the message, so keep it short and starting with a letter.

schemasSubmissions.comments.writeComment.context: Ghost text in the empty box for the opening message of a new discussion. The ellipsis marks it as a prompt to start typing.

schemasSubmissions.common.actionFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when a delete or export did not go through; the underlying error text is printed underneath it, so keep this to a short summary.

schemasSubmissions.common.actions.context: Right-aligned header above the last column of a table, which holds each row's three-dot menu. Very narrow, and on some tables it is only announced to screen readers rather than shown, so keep it to one short plural noun.

schemasSubmissions.common.actionsFor.context: Announced for the three-dot button at the end of a table row, which opens that row's own menu. Used for schema rows and for the value rows inside the schema editor.

placeholders.name: Display name of the schema or of the value on that row, e.g. waste_monthly

schemasSubmissions.common.approvalStatus.context: Green badge meaning every reviewer who had to sign off has done so, and the submission's figures are now live: they appear in the data feed and the exploration screens. The state a submission reaches from Pending when it is approved. Also captions one reviewer's recorded decision, and appears as a choice in the status filter. One word, badges do not wrap.

State of a submission that never had to be signed off at all, because the schema does not ask for approval; it was live from the moment it was accepted. Distinct from Approved, which was held and then cleared. Appears mainly as a choice in the status filter, since rows in this state show only a dash. Keep it short; badges do not wrap.

Amber badge meaning the submission has arrived but is being held until its reviewers sign off, so its figures are deliberately kept out of the data feed and the exploration screens. The state a submission enters on arrival and leaves for Approved or Rejected. Pending means awaiting a decision, not unfinished work. One word, badges do not wrap.

Red badge meaning a reviewer turned the submission down; it moves out of Pending, stays out of the data feed, but remains visible together with the reason given. The submitter has to send corrected data rather than reopen this one. Also captions one reviewer's recorded decision. One word, badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.common.approve.context: Records the reader's sign-off on a submission that is waiting for it, moving it from Pending towards Approved; once the last required reviewer has approved, the figures go live. Imperative. Sits on a small green-outlined button in a table row and on a toolbar button in the side panel, so it must stay short.

schemasSubmissions.common.audit.context: Bold heading over the block of read-only facts recording who created or last changed a schema or submission and when. Noun naming that record-keeping block, not a command to audit anything.

schemasSubmissions.common.back.context: Returns from a detail screen to the list it was opened from. Imperative navigation, paired with a left arrow, used on every schema and submission detail screen so it must read identically in all of them.

schemasSubmissions.common.by.context: Attributes a creation or a change to the account that made it. Means performed by that person, so use the preposition your language needs after a date rather than a literal rendering.

placeholders.name: Display name of the account that acted, e.g. A. Rossi

joins.after: A rendered date and time, followed by a space, a middle dot and another space
joins.note: The separator is supplied by the layout, so this string needs no leading space or punctuation of its own.

schemasSubmissions.common.cadenceLabel.context: Heads the narrow column stating how often each value has to be reported, and labels the same picker in the value editor. Cadence here means the length of one reporting window, such as monthly or quarterly; if the target language has no equivalent noun, a short word for reporting frequency is better than a borrowed term.

schemasSubmissions.common.cancel.context: Abandons the dialog or form the reader is in without saving anything. Imperative; means backing out, never cancelling a subscription or an order.

schemasSubmissions.common.clone.context: Makes an independent copy of a schema, which then opens for editing under a new name; the original is untouched. Imperative; clone means duplicate.

schemasSubmissions.common.close.context: Dismisses a dialog without doing anything further. Imperative; here it means shutting a window, never closing a reporting window or completing a period.

schemasSubmissions.common.continue.context: Confirms a warning and goes ahead with what the reader was doing. Imperative verb, not the noun for a continuation.

schemasSubmissions.common.created.context: Heads the narrow column with the date a schema or submission was first recorded, and labels the same fact in the detail panels, where it is followed by the account that did it. Past participle used as a noun label; the column holds a date, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.createdBy.context: Heads the column naming the account that first recorded a schema or submission. Roughly 140 pixels wide, so keep it short.

schemasSubmissions.common.delete.context: Permanently removes a schema, a submission or a comment after a confirmation; always shown in red as a destructive action. Imperative, and stronger than Remove, which only takes something out of a list being edited.

schemasSubmissions.common.deleted.context: Red badge on a submission that has been removed but is still on screen because the reader asked to see removed records. Past participle describing the state, not an action. One word, badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.common.description.context: Labels the free-text box explaining what a schema is for, shown to the people who fill it in. Noun.

schemasSubmissions.common.disabled.context: Grey badge on a schema or one of its values that has been switched off, so no new data can be submitted against it. Past participle describing the state, never a command; the opposite state is Enabled. One word, badges do not wrap, and it is also written into exported spreadsheets.

schemasSubmissions.common.dismiss.context: Small transparent button inside an error bar that hides that bar; it clears only the message, never the underlying problem or any data. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.common.download.context: Saves the schema definition to the reader's own computer as a file. Imperative; the arrow beside it opens further download choices.

schemasSubmissions.common.draft.context: Blue badge with two related meanings. On a submission it means work in progress that has been saved but not sent: it is kept out of the data feed and the exploration screens and no sign-off runs until it is published, and it cannot go back to this state afterwards. On a row of a schema's version history it means that version of the schema was not switched on, the opposite of Published. Noun, not the verb for drafting; one word, badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.common.edit.context: Opens a schema, submission or comment for changing. Imperative verb, never the noun for an edit that was made.

schemasSubmissions.common.enabled.context: Green badge on a schema or one of its values that is switched on and accepting data. Past participle describing the state, never the command Enable; the opposite state is Disabled. The same word also heads a very narrow column and labels a tick box, and is written into exported spreadsheets, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.exportList.context: Menu entry that saves everything currently listed, across all pages and honouring the filters above, as a spreadsheet file on the reader's computer. Imperative; list means the table on screen.

schemasSubmissions.common.exporting.context: Takes the place of an export menu entry while the file is being assembled and downloaded. Present progressive with an ellipsis, and it must fit the same row as the resting caption.

schemasSubmissions.common.false.context: How a recorded yes-or-no data point is shown when it was answered in the negative, in the read-only view of a submission. Deliberately lower case, matching the way the value is stored; the editable pickers use the friendlier No instead. Fills a table cell, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.from.context: Labels the date-and-time input that sets the earlier end of a custom filter window on the submission list. Paired with To.

schemasSubmissions.common.global.context: Fills the audience cell of a schema that every service can submit against, rather than a named few. Global means unrestricted in reach, not worldwide. It is the whole content of a narrow table cell and is also written into exported spreadsheets, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.history.context: Tab beside the details of one submission, listing every recorded change to it and who made it. Short noun; readers switch to it by habit, so keep the wording stable.

schemasSubmissions.common.id.context: Labels the machine-generated identifier of a submission, shown in a fixed-width font beneath it. An abbreviation of identifier; keep whatever short form your language uses for that on technical screens.

schemasSubmissions.common.label.context: Labels the friendly, human-readable name given to a schema or one of its values, as opposed to Name, which is the fixed machine identifier. Also heads a table column and appears in exported spreadsheets, so keep it to one short noun and keep it clearly different from Name.

schemasSubmissions.common.loadFailed.context: Headline of the red bar shown when a list could not be fetched from the server; the server's own error text follows underneath, so keep this to a short summary.

schemasSubmissions.common.loading.context: Fills the whole width of an otherwise empty table, or stands alone on a detail screen, while data is being fetched. Progress, not an error.

schemasSubmissions.common.modifiable.context: Names the setting that decides whether data already recorded for a reporting window may be sent again and overwritten. When it is off, the first submission for a window is final. Labels a tick box, heads a narrow column, appears on a badge and is written into exported spreadsheets, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.modified.context: Labels the date a schema or submission was last changed, followed by the account that changed it. Past participle used as a noun label, sitting beside Created in the same block.

schemasSubmissions.common.moreActions.context: Announced for the three-dot button in a screen's toolbar, which opens a menu of whole-page actions such as refreshing and exporting. Name the menu, not the icon.

schemasSubmissions.common.name.context: Labels the fixed machine identifier of a schema or one of its values — the text that scripts and imported files must match, which is why it cannot be changed after creation. Distinct from Label, the friendly display name; keep the two clearly different. Also heads table columns and appears in exported spreadsheets.

schemasSubmissions.common.no.context: The negative answer for a yes-or-no data point, offered in a picker and shown in narrow table cells for settings such as whether a value is required. One word; pairs with Yes and both must be visibly different at a glance.

schemasSubmissions.common.note.context: Heads the column holding the free-text remark a submitter attached to one recorded data point, explaining an unusual figure. Singular noun; most cells are empty.

schemasSubmissions.common.notes.context: Labels the free-text box for internal remarks about a schema, kept for administrators rather than shown to the people filling the schema in. Plural noun; distinct from the singular Note attached to a single data point.

schemasSubmissions.common.preview.context: Opens a dialog showing what the submission form built from this schema will look like, without saving anything or recording any data. Imperative verb.

schemasSubmissions.common.publish.context: Turns a saved draft submission into a real one: it is fully checked, enters the sign-off workflow if the schema asks for it, and its figures count from then on. Imperative; the move is one-way, as a published submission can never go back to being a draft.

schemasSubmissions.common.published.context: Green badge on a row of a schema's version history meaning that version of the schema was switched on and live. Past participle describing the state; the opposite state is Draft. One word, badges do not wrap, and it is also written into exported spreadsheets.

schemasSubmissions.common.refresh.context: Menu entry that fetches the current list again from the server, discarding what was cached. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.common.reject.context: Turns a submission that is awaiting sign-off down, moving it from Pending to Rejected: its figures stay out of the data feed, and the reviewer is asked for a reason first. Imperative. Distinct from deleting, which removes the record altogether, and from reopening, which puts work back in the submitter's hands. The wording also has to work as the caption of a narrow icon-only button announced to screen readers.

schemasSubmissions.common.remove.context: Takes a value out of the schema being edited, or out of a layout. Milder than Delete: nothing is written until the schema itself is saved, so it can still be abandoned. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.common.replacedAt.context: Labels the moment a submission was superseded by newer data for the same reporting window; blank while it is still the current one. Past participle plus a preposition of time, so word it as when it was replaced.

schemasSubmissions.common.requiresApprov.context: Explains the shield marker beside a schema's name: submissions against this schema are held until a reviewer signs them off. Also used as the marker's spoken name and as a badge in the schema panel, so it must stay to about two words and read as a statement about the schema.

schemasSubmissions.common.retry.context: Attempts the failed request again; offered inside the error bar itself. Imperative verb, not a noun.

schemasSubmissions.common.sample.context: Heads the column holding the figure actually recorded for one value. A sample is a single measured data point inside a submission, never a specimen or an example. Singular; keep it short.

schemasSubmissions.common.samples.context: Heads the narrow column counting how many data points a submission contains, and labels the same count in the detail panels. A sample is a single measured data point inside a submission; the cells hold numbers, so keep the header short.

schemasSubmissions.common.save.context: Confirms an edit to a comment and writes it. Imperative; save means storing, never the financial sense of putting money aside.

schemasSubmissions.common.saveChanges.context: Writes the edits made to an existing schema or submission. Imperative; save means storing, never the financial sense. Appears on a toolbar button and at the foot of the form, so keep it short enough for both.

schemasSubmissions.common.schema.context: Names the administrator-defined form definition that says which values a service must report and how often. Labels a picker, heads a table column, stands in as a panel heading, and is also folded into the sentence of a delete confirmation, where the interface lower-cases it automatically — so if your language never lower-cases this noun, choose a form that still reads correctly when it is.

schemasSubmissions.common.service.context: Names the organisational unit that submits data — a department, site or system with its own account. Labels a picker and heads a table column, so keep it to one short noun; never the sense of customer service or a background process.

schemasSubmissions.common.status.context: Heads the narrow column showing where a submission stands in the sign-off workflow, or whether a version of a schema was live; it also labels the matching filter. Singular noun, kept short because the cells hold badges.

schemasSubmissions.common.submission.context: Names one filled-in instance of a schema, sent in by a service for a reporting window. Heads the detail screen and the quick-look side panel, and is also folded into the sentence of a delete confirmation, where the interface lower-cases it automatically — so if your language never lower-cases this noun, choose a form that still reads correctly when it is. Singular noun, never the act of submitting.

schemasSubmissions.common.submissions.context: Heads the screen listing every submission, and also heads a narrow column counting how many submissions were recorded against one version of a schema. Plural noun for the filled-in instances themselves, never the act of submitting; keep it short enough for the column.

schemasSubmissions.common.submittedAt.context: Heads the column with the moment a submission was sent in, which for imported historical data is the date of the data itself rather than the day of the import. Past participle plus a preposition of time; keep the header short because the cells hold dates.

schemasSubmissions.common.timestamp.context: Heads the column with the exact moment attached to one recorded data point, or to one entry in the change history. Keep it short; the cells hold a date and a time.

schemasSubmissions.common.to.context: Labels the date-and-time input that sets the later end of a custom filter window on the submission list. Paired with From; a preposition marking the end of a span of time, never the recipient of anything.

schemasSubmissions.common.true.context: How a recorded yes-or-no data point is shown when it was answered in the affirmative, in the read-only view of a submission. Deliberately lower case, matching the way the value is stored; the editable pickers use the friendlier Yes instead. Fills a table cell, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.type.context: Heads the narrow column saying what kind of figure a value holds — text, a number, a date or a yes-or-no answer — and labels the same picker in the value editor. Type here means data type; keep it to one short word.

schemasSubmissions.common.untitledSchema.context: Stands in for a schema's name in a dialog heading when the schema being previewed has neither a display name nor a machine name yet, which happens while a brand-new one is still being built. Reads as a description of the missing name rather than as a real title.

joins.after: The fixed part of a dialog heading, such as the one naming the dependency view or the form preview
joins.note: Lands inside another heading, so keep it short and use the casing that reads naturally in mid-sentence.

schemasSubmissions.common.value.context: Heads the column holding the figure recorded for each value of a submission. A value is one data point a schema defines, such as tonnes collected; here the column shows what was actually entered for it. Keep it to one short word.

schemasSubmissions.common.valueType.Bool.context: The data type for a value that can only be answered one way or the other. Deliberately worded for non-technical readers instead of using the programming term; the two halves are the same words used on the Yes and No choices, joined by a slash. Shown in a picker and in a narrow column, so keep it very short.

schemasSubmissions.common.valueType.Date.context: The data type for a value that holds a point in time, entered with a date-and-time picker. Shown in a picker and in a narrow column, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.valueType.Inte.context: The data type for a count with no decimal part, such as a number of incidents. Worded for non-technical readers rather than using the programming term; contrast it clearly with the plain Number type, which does allow decimals. Shown in a picker and in a narrow column.

schemasSubmissions.common.valueType.Numb.context: The data type for a figure that may have a decimal part, such as tonnes or a percentage. Must read as clearly different from the whole-number type beside it in the same picker. Keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.valueType.Stri.context: The data type for a free-text value. Worded for non-technical readers rather than using the programming term for a string. Shown in a picker and in a narrow column, so keep it to one word.

schemasSubmissions.common.values.context: Names the data points a schema defines — the individual figures a service has to report, such as tonnes collected or hours lost. Captions a tab in the schema editor, heads a block in the read-only view and a narrow column counting them, and appears in exported spreadsheets. Readers switch to the tab by habit, so keep the wording stable and short.

schemasSubmissions.common.version.context: Labels the whole number an administrator raises when a schema changes in a way worth marking, so past submissions can be told apart from later ones. Noun.

schemasSubmissions.common.view.context: Opens a submission in the same layout as the editor but with everything locked, for reading only. Imperative verb, never the noun for a view or a screen; distinct from View details, which shows the raw list of recorded figures instead.

schemasSubmissions.common.viewDetails.context: Opens the plain table of every figure recorded in a submission, useful for comparing or copying values. Imperative; the alternative to View, which shows the same data laid out as the form.

schemasSubmissions.common.warnings.context: Names the non-blocking remarks raised while a submission was checked: the data was accepted, but something is worth a second look. Appears on an amber badge, heads a narrow counting column, and labels the same count in the detail panels, so keep it to one plural noun. Not errors.

schemasSubmissions.common.yes.context: The affirmative answer for a yes-or-no data point, offered in a picker and shown in narrow table cells for settings such as whether a value is required. One word; pairs with No and both must be visibly different at a glance.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.calculat.context: Legend entry naming the dashed shape used in the diagram for a value the system works out from other values by a formula, instead of one a service types in. Very tight on space, in a column about 220 pixels wide.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.connecto.en: A connector points from a referenced value to the one whose rule depends on it.
schemasSubmissions.dependencies.connecto.context: Short guidance beside the diagram explaining how to read the arrows: the arrow starts at the value that is referred to and ends at the value whose rule refers to it. A connector is one drawn line between two values. Sits in a narrow column, so keep it to one sentence.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.cal.context: Names the kind of link where the value at the arrow's head is worked out by a formula from the value at its tail. Reads as the start of a phrase completed by the other value's name, so it should still make sense when a name follows it. Appears in the legend and in the tooltip on the line itself; very tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.ena.context: Names the kind of link where a rule decides whether a value can be filled in at all, based on another value; when the rule does not hold, anything sent for it is dropped with a warning rather than saved. Reads as the start of a phrase completed by a condition. Appears in the legend and in the tooltip on the line; very tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.sub.context: Names the kind of link that comes from a rule declared on the schema as a whole rather than on any single value, so it compares several values against each other and has no owner. The bracketed part says where the rule lives. Longest entry in the legend and still tight on space, so abbreviate rather than let it wrap.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.val.context: Names the kind of link where a value is only accepted while a condition involving another value holds; failing it stops the whole submission. Reads as the start of a phrase completed by a condition. Appears in the legend and in the tooltip on the line; very tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.vis.context: Names the kind of link where a rule decides whether a value is shown on the form at all, based on another value; when the rule does not hold, the input is hidden and anything sent for it is dropped with a warning. Reads as the start of a phrase completed by a condition; very tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.edge.war.context: Names the kind of link where a condition involving another value raises a remark without stopping anything: the submission is still accepted. Reads as the start of a phrase completed by a condition, and the verb must not sound like a refusal. Very tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.failed.context: Opens the red bar shown when the diagram could not be worked out, usually because the server could not be reached. The colon introduces the underlying reason, and a Retry button follows on the same line.

joins.before: The server's own error text, then a Retry button, all on one line
joins.example: Couldn't build the dependency graph: The request timed out.
joins.note: Keep the trailing colon and the space after it; they separate this from the reason that follows.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.legend.context: Bold heading of the narrow column beside the diagram that explains what each shape and each style of line means. Noun.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.loading.en: Walking this schema's rules for dependencies…
schemasSubmissions.dependencies.loading.context: Sits beside a spinner while every rule in the schema is being read to work out which values refer to which. The opening verb conveys going through the rules one by one; a plain progress wording is fine if the target language has no natural equivalent.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.noValues.en: This schema has no usable values yet — add one to see its dependencies.
schemasSubmissions.dependencies.noValues.context: Amber bar shown when the schema has no usable values yet, so there is nothing to draw a diagram from; the second half tells the administrator what to do about it. Not an error.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.none.en: No dependencies detected among these values yet.
schemasSubmissions.dependencies.none.context: Quiet line in the legend column when the schema has values but no rule connects any of them, so the diagram shows shapes and no lines. States the absence; not an error.

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.title.context: Heading of the dialog showing how a schema's values refer to one another through its rules. The word before the colon names what is being shown; the schema's own name follows and is not translated.

placeholders.name: Display name of the schema, or a stand-in when it has none yet, e.g. Monthly waste KPIs

schemasSubmissions.dependencies.value.context: Legend entry naming the plain shape used in the diagram for an ordinary value that a service fills in by hand, as opposed to one worked out by a formula. Very tight on space; one word.

schemasSubmissions.layout.addSection.context: Adds a new empty group at the top level of the form layout, into which values can then be dragged. Imperative; a section is a named group of values that becomes a heading on the submission form.

schemasSubmissions.layout.addSubsection.context: Announced for the small plus button on a section's row, which nests a further group inside that section. Describe the action, not the icon.

schemasSubmissions.layout.addSubsectionI.context: Shown on hovering the small plus button on a section's row; the last word makes clear that the new group is nested within this section rather than placed beside it.

schemasSubmissions.layout.allPlaced.en: Every value is placed in the layout.
schemasSubmissions.layout.allPlaced.context: Replaces the tray of loose value chips once every value in the schema has been dragged into the arrangement, so there is nothing left to place. A statement of completeness, not an instruction.

schemasSubmissions.layout.duplicateValue.en: Value "{{name}}" appears more than once in the layout.
schemasSubmissions.layout.duplicateValue.context: Red issue listed under the layout editor when the same value has been dropped into the arrangement in two places, which is not allowed; one of the two must be taken out before the schema can be saved. The quoted name comes from the schema and is never translated.

placeholders.name: Machine name of the value placed twice, e.g. tonnes_collected

schemasSubmissions.layout.emptyHelp.en: Drag values from above to place them, or add a section. Values that aren't placed here will still render first in submission forms (under no heading).
schemasSubmissions.layout.emptyHelp.context: Fills the empty arrangement area, offering both ways to begin and warning what happens if the administrator arranges nothing: values left out are still shown on the submission form, but first and with no heading over them. Second person, addressed to the administrator.

schemasSubmissions.layout.errorPrefix.context: Marks one of the listed problems as serious enough to block saving, as opposed to the milder note marker used beside it. Shown in red.

joins.before: The text of the problem itself, run straight on with no separator of its own
joins.example: Error: A section is missing its caption.
joins.note: Keeps its colon and its trailing space; nothing else supplies the gap before the message.

schemasSubmissions.layout.missingCaption.en: A section is missing its caption.
schemasSubmissions.layout.missingCaption.context: Red issue listed under the layout editor when a group in the arrangement has been left without a heading; the schema cannot be saved until one is typed in. The caption is the heading shown above that group on the submission form.

schemasSubmissions.layout.missingTarget.en: A layout value node is missing its target.
schemasSubmissions.layout.missingTarget.context: Red issue listed under the layout editor when an entry in the arrangement does not say which value it stands for, which normally means the stored arrangement is damaged rather than that the administrator did something wrong. Written impersonally for that reason.

schemasSubmissions.layout.newSection.context: The heading a freshly added group starts out with, filled into its caption box for the administrator to type over. It is real content rather than ghost text, so it is saved as written and would appear on the submission form if left alone; keep it short and obviously provisional.

schemasSubmissions.layout.notePrefix.context: Marks one of the listed problems as advisory: worth knowing, but it does not stop the schema being saved. Shown in orange, in contrast to the red error marker beside it.

joins.before: The text of the remark itself, run straight on with no separator of its own
joins.example: Note: 2 value(s) not placed in the layout — they will render before the sections.
joins.note: Keeps its colon and its trailing space; nothing else supplies the gap before the message.

schemasSubmissions.layout.removeFromLayo.context: Shown on hovering the small bin button on a value's row, and announced for it. Takes that value out of the arrangement only: the value itself stays in the schema and will simply be shown before the groups instead. Milder than deleting.

schemasSubmissions.layout.removeSection.context: Shown on hovering the small bin button on a group's row, and announced for it. Takes the group and everything nested inside it out of the arrangement; the values themselves stay in the schema.

schemasSubmissions.layout.sectionCaption.context: Announced for the single-line box holding a group's heading, which has no visible label of its own. Caption here means the heading shown above that group on the submission form.

schemasSubmissions.layout.sectionDescrip.context: Announced for the multi-line box holding a group's optional explanatory line, which has no visible label of its own.
Ghost text in the empty box for a group's explanatory line, saying both that it may be left blank and where it will appear: below the group's own heading on the submission form.

schemasSubmissions.layout.sectionHeading.context: Ghost text in the empty box where a group's heading is typed. Names what belongs there; it is not saved and never reaches the submission form.

schemasSubmissions.layout.tooDeep.en: Layout is nested too deep (max 32 levels).
schemasSubmissions.layout.tooDeep.context: Red issue listed under the layout editor when groups have been nested inside one another beyond the allowed depth. Keep the numeral; the bracket states the hard limit.

schemasSubmissions.layout.unassignedValu.context: Heads the tray of loose chips for values that have not yet been dragged into the arrangement. The interface renders it in capitals at a very small size, so keep it short and do not add capitals of your own.

placeholders.count: How many values are still unplaced, e.g. 3

schemasSubmissions.layout.unassignedWarn.en: {{count}} value(s) not placed in the layout — they will render before the sections.
schemasSubmissions.layout.unassignedWarn.context: Orange advisory listed under the layout editor: the schema still saves, but values left out of the arrangement appear at the very top of the submission form with no heading over them. The bracketed plural marker is the English way of covering one and many at once; use whatever reads correctly for any number instead.

placeholders.count: How many values were left out of the arrangement, e.g. 2

schemasSubmissions.layout.unknownValue.context: Red issue listed under the layout editor when the arrangement points at a value the schema no longer has, usually because it was renamed or removed; the stale entry must be taken out before saving. The quoted name comes from the stored arrangement and is never translated.

placeholders.name: Machine name the arrangement still refers to, e.g. tonnes_collected

schemasSubmissions.layout.untitledSectio.context: Stands in for a group's heading in the editor's tree while its caption box is still empty; it is never saved and never reaches the submission form. Keep the brackets and the lower case, which mark it as a stand-in rather than a real heading, and keep it short because the row truncates.

schemasSubmissions.preview.bestEffortHea.context: Bold headline of the blue information bar at the top of the window that renders a schema's form the way a submitter would see it. Best-effort means approximate: the checks run in the browser and may disagree with the server. A few words only, so it stays on one line above the explanation.

schemasSubmissions.preview.bestEffortHel.en: This renders the form and evaluates rules in your browser against the unsaved schema. The server stays authoritative — some semantics differ here (regex dialect, and helpers like sampleTimestamp()/serviceName() aren't available client-side), so always confirm with a real submission or the API before relying on a rule.
schemasSubmissions.preview.bestEffortHel.context: Explanation under that headline. The form is built from the definition the administrator is editing, unsaved changes included, while the server remains the authority on whether data is really accepted. Leave sampleTimestamp() and serviceName() exactly as written — they are formula function names that exist only in English — and keep regex as the technical term for a text-matching pattern.

schemasSubmissions.preview.conditionalHe.en: Conditional display (hide/gray) and inline warnings appear on the form to the left.
schemasSubmissions.preview.conditionalHe.context: Small grey line closing the results panel, pointing the reader at the trial form rendered beside it; on a narrow window the form sits above rather than to the left, so wording that does not depend on the direction travels better. Hide and gray describe a data point that a rule written by the administrator removes from the form or shows greyed out and uneditable.

schemasSubmissions.preview.findings.requ.context: One entry in the list of problems found in the trial form: the schema obliges the submitter to supply this data point and nothing has been entered. Required means demanded by the definition, not merely recommended. Lower case and no closing period, because the data point's own label is printed immediately before it.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Tonnes collected: required value is empty
joins.note: Neighbouring entries in the same list are phrased the same way, so keep the register uniform across them.

schemasSubmissions.preview.findings.sche.context: Stands alone in the problem list under the heading for schema-wide rules, and appears only as a fallback when the administrator's rule refused the data without supplying wording of its own. A schema-level rule judges the whole filled-in form at once instead of one data point. Lower case and no closing period, to match the entries around it.

schemasSubmissions.preview.findings.valu.en: value validation rule rejected this value
schemasSubmissions.preview.findings.valu.context: Fallback wording for an entry in the problem list when a rule the administrator attached to one data point refused the entered figure but returned no message of its own; whenever that rule does return a message, the administrator's own text is shown instead and is never translated. Value means one data point inside a submission. Lower case, no closing period.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Tonnes collected: value validation rule rejected this value

schemasSubmissions.preview.loadingServic.context: Ghost text in the closed service picker while the list of services is still being fetched. A service is an organisational unit that submits data. Keep the trailing ellipsis and keep it short — the picker is only about 260 pixels wide.

schemasSubmissions.preview.noFilledValue.en: No filled values yet — fill in the form below first.
schemasSubmissions.preview.noFilledValue.context: Small grey line under the service and timestamp controls, shown while every box in the trial form is still empty so there is nothing to send for checking. Fill in means entering figures into the form below; the dash introduces that instruction.

schemasSubmissions.preview.noProblems.en: No problems with the current values.
schemasSubmissions.preview.noProblems.context: Green line with a tick that takes the place of the problem list when the browser-side checks find nothing wrong with what has been entered. Current values means the figures presently in the trial form. Not a promise of acceptance: the server is asked separately.

schemasSubmissions.preview.noUsableValue.en: This schema has no usable values to preview yet. Add a value first.
schemasSubmissions.preview.noUsableValue.context: Amber information bar shown instead of the trial form when the schema defines no data point that can be rendered — either none at all, or none with a usable machine name. A value is one data point defined by the schema, and the second sentence tells the administrator to define one in the editor. Imperative in the second sentence.

schemasSubmissions.preview.previewTitle.context: Heading of the window that renders a schema's form as a submitter would see it. Preview is a noun here — a trial rendering — and the colon separates it from the schema's own name.

placeholders.name: The schema's display name, or its machine name when it has none. Written by an administrator and never translated, e.g. Monthly waste KPIs

schemasSubmissions.preview.resetValues.context: Empties everything entered into the trial form and puts the sample moment back to now. Imperative; reset means clear back to the starting state, not re-send. The schema itself is untouched and nothing is stored either way.

schemasSubmissions.preview.sampleTimesta.context: Labels the date-and-time box that decides when the trial figures count as having been measured. A sample is one measured figure inside a submission; timestamp is the moment attached to it.

schemasSubmissions.preview.scopes.requir.context: Red pill heading the group of problems where a data point the schema insists on was left empty. Reads as adjective plus noun — the demanded items that are absent — never as an instruction to supply them. Badges do not wrap, so two short words at most.

schemasSubmissions.preview.scopes.schema.context: Red pill heading the group of problems raised by rules that judge the whole filled-in form at once rather than a single data point. A schema is the form definition an administrator writes. Keep it compact; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.preview.scopes.shape.context: Red pill heading the group of problems about the form of an entered figure — its type, its length, its bounds, its pattern — as distinct from rules an administrator wrote. Shape means the structural form of the data, nothing geometric. Two short words; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.preview.scopes.value.context: Red pill heading the group of problems raised by the rule an administrator attached to one individual data point. Value means one data point in a submission, not worth or price. Keep it compact; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.preview.selectService.context: Ghost text in the empty service picker, prompting the reader to choose which service the trial check should run as; who may see the schema, the one-per-period limit and comparisons with earlier data all depend on that choice. A service is an organisational unit that submits data.

schemasSubmissions.preview.server.accept.en: Would be accepted immediately (no approval required).
schemasSubmissions.preview.server.accept.context: Grey line under the server's verdict, saying the figures would count towards reporting at once because nobody has to sign them off. Would be is conditional — nothing was actually filed. Approval is the sign-off a reviewer gives a submission.

schemasSubmissions.preview.server.discar.context: Grey line listing the data points the server set aside before checking, because a rule the administrator wrote says they do not apply to this submission. Discarded means quietly dropped rather than refused; the rest of the submission still counts. EnabledIf and VisibleIf are the names of two rule fields in the editor and stay in English exactly as written.

placeholders.names: Comma-separated machine names of the dropped data points, exactly as the administrator spelled them and never translated, e.g. night_shift_total, weekend_total

schemasSubmissions.preview.server.heldFo.en: Would be held for approval ({{count}} approver(s) required).
schemasSubmissions.preview.server.heldFo.context: Grey line under the server's verdict, saying a real submission of these figures would wait for a reviewer's sign-off before counting towards reporting. Held means kept back pending a decision, not stored away. English fakes the plural with '(s)'; use whatever your language does naturally for a count that may be one.

placeholders.count: How many approvers must sign off, e.g. 2

schemasSubmissions.preview.server.invali.context: Red pill giving the server's verdict on the trial figures: as they stand they would not be accepted. Invalid describes the attempted submission, never the schema. Very tight on space — badges do not wrap — so keep the wording before the dash to a single word if you can.

placeholders.count: How many errors the server reported, e.g. 3. English fakes the plural with '(s)'

schemasSubmissions.preview.server.valid.en: Valid — a real submission would be accepted.
