schemasSubmissions.preview.server.valid.context: Green line with a tick giving the server's verdict: figures like these would be taken. Conditional throughout — this run stored nothing, so nothing was actually submitted.

schemasSubmissions.preview.serverValidat.context: Bold heading of the block inside the results panel that reports what the server said, as opposed to the browser's own findings listed above it. Validation means checking entered data against the schema's rules.

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.aboveMa.context: Entry in the problem list: the figure entered is larger than the upper bound the schema sets for that data point. The bound is inclusive, so a figure exactly equal to it passes. Lower case and no closing period, because the data point's label and a colon come first.

placeholders.value: The upper bound set on that data point, e.g. 100

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Tonnes collected: above the maximum of 100

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.belowMi.context: Entry in the problem list: the figure entered is smaller than the lower bound the schema sets for that data point. The bound is inclusive, so a figure exactly equal to it passes. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The lower bound set on that data point, e.g. 0

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Tonnes collected: below the minimum of 0

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.earlier.context: Entry in the problem list: the moment entered falls before the earliest one the schema allows for that data point. The bound is inclusive, so the earliest allowed moment itself passes. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The earliest allowed moment, printed exactly as the administrator typed it in the editor, e.g. 2026-01-01. Do not reformat or localise it

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.invalid.en: value is not a valid date
schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.invalid.context: Entry in the problem list: what was entered for a data point of the Date type cannot be read as a moment in time at all. Use the same word for the type as the type list in the editor uses. Lower case, no closing period.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Collection date: value is not a valid date

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.later.context: Entry in the problem list: the moment entered falls after the latest one the schema allows for that data point. The bound is inclusive, so the latest allowed moment itself passes. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The latest allowed moment, printed exactly as the administrator typed it in the editor, e.g. 2026-12-31. Do not reformat or localise it

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.longer.en: longer than the maximum length of {{value}}
schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.longer.context: Entry in the problem list: the text entered has more characters than the schema permits for that data point. Length is counted in characters, not words. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The greatest number of characters allowed, e.g. 40

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Site reference: longer than the maximum length of 40

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.notNumb.context: Entry in the problem list: what was entered for a numeric data point cannot be read as a number. Lower case, no closing period, because the data point's label and a colon come first.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Tonnes collected: value is not a number

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.pattern.context: Entry in the problem list: the text entered does not satisfy the character pattern the administrator set for that data point. Pattern here means a regular expression — a technical recipe for permitted characters — and it is printed verbatim after the wording, so never translate, space out or otherwise touch it. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The pattern exactly as the administrator typed it, e.g. ^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$. Never translated or reformatted

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Site reference: does not match the pattern ^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.regexBr.en: regex pattern could not be evaluated in the browser (will be checked on the server)
schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.regexBr.context: Entry in the problem list reporting that the browser could not run the administrator's character pattern, usually because it uses syntax only the server understands; it is a caveat rather than a fault in the entered text. Keep regex as the technical term. Lower case, no closing period.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Site reference: regex pattern could not be evaluated in the browser (will be checked on the server)

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.shorter.en: shorter than the minimum length of {{value}}
schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.shorter.context: Entry in the problem list: the text entered has fewer characters than the schema demands for that data point. Length is counted in characters, not words. Lower case, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The smallest number of characters allowed, e.g. 3

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Site reference: shorter than the minimum length of 3

schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.wholeNu.en: value must be a whole number
schemasSubmissions.preview.shape.wholeNu.context: Entry in the problem list: the data point takes whole numbers only, so anything with a decimal part is refused. Whole number means an integer, negative ones included. Lower case, no closing period, even though the wording is stronger than its neighbours.

joins.after: The label of the data point followed by a colon and a space, in the results panel of the preview window
joins.example: Incidents: value must be a whole number

schemasSubmissions.preview.skipCadence.context: Labels the tick box that tells the trial check to ignore the limit of one figure per reporting window for each data point, so an administrator can rehearse a window that has already been reported. Cadence is how often a data point is expected — daily, weekly, monthly and so on — and the bracketed phrase glosses it. Skip means leave out of the check.

schemasSubmissions.preview.skippedValues.en: Skipped {{count}} value(s) with a blank or duplicate name: {{names}}. Give every value a unique name to preview it.
schemasSubmissions.preview.skippedValues.context: Amber information bar listing the data points left out of the trial form because their machine name is blank or repeats another; rules refer to data points by that name, so duplicates cannot be told apart. The closing sentence is an instruction to the administrator to give each one a distinct name.

placeholders.count: How many data points were left out, e.g. 2. English fakes the plural with '(s)'
placeholders.names: Comma-separated names of those data points — their machine name, or their display label when the name is blank. Author-written and never translated, e.g. tonnes_collected, Downtime

schemasSubmissions.preview.testHeading.context: Bold headline of the blue information bar in the other mode of the same window, where the real server checks run against a saved schema without anything being stored. Test qualifies submission — a rehearsal of filing data — and a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a period.

schemasSubmissions.preview.testHelp.en: Runs the real server validation as the chosen service — including cadence duplicates, history rules, and the would-be approval state — without saving anything. Fill in the form, pick a service, then Validate.
schemasSubmissions.preview.testHelp.context: Explanation under that headline. Cadence duplicates means a second figure inside a reporting window that allows only one; history rules compare the entered figures with what the service filed before; the would-be approval state is whether a reviewer's sign-off would be needed. Validate at the end names the button in the same window, so use exactly the caption you chose there.

schemasSubmissions.preview.testTitle.context: Heading of the same window when it is opened to run the real server checks rather than a browser-side rendering. Test submission is a noun phrase — a rehearsed submission — and the colon separates it from the schema's own name.

placeholders.name: The schema's display name, or its machine name when it has none. Written by an administrator and never translated, e.g. Monthly waste KPIs

schemasSubmissions.preview.timestampPrev.en: Used for the samples and any date-based rules that read a Date value.
schemasSubmissions.preview.timestampPrev.context: Guidance under the date-and-time box in the browser-side rendering: the chosen moment feeds the example figures shown in the form and any rule that reads a moment in time. A Date value is a data point of the Date type, so use the same word for it as the type list in the editor uses.

schemasSubmissions.preview.timestampServ.en: Used for every sample and any date/cadence/history rules.
schemasSubmissions.preview.timestampServ.context: Guidance under the date-and-time box when the real server checks are run: the chosen moment is stamped on every figure sent, which decides which reporting window they fall into and what earlier data they are compared against. Cadence is how often a data point is expected; history rules look back at what the service filed before.

schemasSubmissions.preview.unnamedValue.context: Stands in for a data point that has neither a machine name nor a display label, so that it can still be mentioned in the list of items left out of the trial form. Keep the brackets and the lower case; it is a description, not a name anybody typed.

joins.after: Inside the comma-separated list of names in the amber 'skipped values' information bar
joins.example: Skipped 2 value(s) with a blank or duplicate name: (unnamed value), tonnes_collected. Give every value a unique name to preview it.

schemasSubmissions.preview.validate.context: Primary button that sends the entered figures to the server for a genuine check and reports the verdict; nothing is stored. Imperative verb, not the noun for the check itself. Referred to by name in the explanation at the top of the same window, so keep the two identical.

schemasSubmissions.preview.validateAsSer.context: Labels the compulsory picker choosing which service the check should be run on behalf of; as means in the role of, not in the manner of. A service is an organisational unit that submits data, and the result depends on which one is chosen.

schemasSubmissions.preview.validationCou.en: {{count}} value(s) will be validated. The schema must be saved and visible to the chosen service.
schemasSubmissions.preview.validationCou.context: Small grey line under the controls saying how many of the entered data points would be sent for checking. The second sentence is a precondition: the check runs against the stored definition, so unsaved edits are not covered and the chosen service must be allowed to see the schema.

placeholders.count: How many data points have been filled in, e.g. 4. English fakes the plural with '(s)'

schemasSubmissions.preview.validationRes.context: Bold heading over the panel beside the trial form that lists everything the browser found wrong with the figures entered so far. Results of checking the data, not an outcome of anything being filed.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.addNotes.context: Quiet button in the third column of a data point's row that opens a text box for a free-text remark about that one figure. Notes means the submitter's own comment — an explanation of an unusual figure, say — and whatever they type is stored as typed and never translated. Imperative; plural in English but a singular remark is what is normally written.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.calculat.context: Pill beside a data point in the form marking it as worked out by a formula from the other figures in the same submission instead of being entered by hand; its box is read-only. Use the same word here as for the Calculated choice in the schema editor. One word; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.disabled.context: Pill marking a data point whose box cannot be filled in right now — because the schema or the data point is switched off, because a condition the administrator wrote turns it off, because the page is read-only, or because the figure is calculated. An adjective describing the state, never an instruction to switch something off. One word; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.from.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving the earliest moment the schema accepts for it. The bound is inclusive. Very tight on space, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The earliest allowed moment exactly as the administrator typed it, e.g. 2026-01-01. Never reformatted or localised

joins.after: Nothing, but sibling limits follow, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.max.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving the largest number the schema accepts for it; the bound is inclusive. Abbreviate as English does — the line sits in a narrow column — and use the same abbreviation as the Max box in the editor. No closing period.

placeholders.value: The upper bound the administrator set, e.g. 100

joins.after: The minimum item when one is set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.maxLengt.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving how many characters the text may run to at most. Counted in characters, not words. Keep it abbreviated and short; no closing period.

placeholders.value: The greatest number of characters allowed, e.g. 40

joins.after: The minimum-length item when one is set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.min.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving the smallest number the schema accepts for it; the bound is inclusive. Abbreviate as English does and match the Min box in the editor. No closing period.

placeholders.value: The lower bound the administrator set, e.g. 0

joins.after: Nothing, but the maximum item follows when one is set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.minLengt.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving how many characters the text must run to at least. Counted in characters, not words. Keep it abbreviated and short; no closing period.

placeholders.value: The smallest number of characters allowed, e.g. 3

joins.after: Nothing, but the maximum-length item follows when one is set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.notProvi.context: Third choice in the yes/no picker for a data point, standing for no answer at all — deliberately different from answering no. Keep the brackets, which mark it as a description rather than an answer.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.note.context: Labels the text box holding a free-text remark about one figure in the submission. Singular: one remark per data point. Whatever the submitter writes there is stored as typed and never translated.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.optional.context: Pill marking a data point that may be left empty without the submission being refused; it is the counterpart of the Required pill on the same row. One word; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.regex.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, naming the character pattern the text has to satisfy. Regex is the technical term for such a pattern and stays as it is, and the pattern printed after the colon is shown verbatim — never translate, re-space or otherwise touch it.

placeholders.value: The pattern exactly as the administrator typed it, e.g. ^[A-Z]{3}-[0-9]{4}$

joins.after: The length limits when they are set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.required.context: Marks a data point the submitter must supply: the submission is refused if it is left empty. The same word does three jobs — a pill on the form, a column heading in the editor's list of data points, and the tick box in the value editor that sets the obligation — so it has to work as a bare adjective in all three and stay within a badge. Required means demanded, not merely recommended.

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.to.context: One item in the small grey line of limits under a data point's label, giving the latest moment the schema accepts for it. The bound is inclusive. Very tight on space, no closing period.

placeholders.value: The latest allowed moment exactly as the administrator typed it, e.g. 2026-12-31. Never reformatted or localised

joins.after: The 'from' item when one is set, separated by a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.sampleFields.value.context: Labels the box where the figure for one data point is entered, on both the submission form and the preview. Value means the data point's figure, not worth or price; the unit of measure follows it in brackets when the administrator has set one.

placeholders.unit: The unit of measure in brackets with a leading space, or empty when none is set. Written by the administrator and never translated, e.g. ' (t)' or ' (hours)'

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.addRule.context: Small button under the list of rules that checks a whole submission, adding one more empty rule box. Imperative. The rule itself is a formula the administrator writes, in a syntax that is the same in every language.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.addValue.context: Primary button above the list of data points, adding a new one and opening its editor straight away. Imperative; a value is one data point defined by the schema.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMax.context: Labels the box holding the upper edge of the acceptable range shown on charts for a numeric data point. Amber is the middle of the red/amber/green traffic-light scheme, and the colour word in brackets is what makes the label readable, so keep it. This range is reporting decoration only — nothing is ever refused because of it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMaxHi.en: Above this is red. Outer upper edge.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMaxHi.context: Guidance under that box: anything above this edge is charted as red, the worst band. Outer means this is the outermost of the two upper edges, with the ideal one sitting inside it. Two very short sentences; keep them short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMin.context: Labels the box holding the lower edge of the acceptable range shown on charts for a numeric data point. Amber is the middle of the red/amber/green traffic-light scheme; keep the colour word in brackets. Reporting decoration only — no figure is ever refused for falling outside it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMinHi.en: Below this is red. Outer lower edge.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.amberMinHi.context: Guidance under that box: anything below this edge is charted as red, the worst band. Outer means this is the outermost of the two lower edges, with the ideal one sitting inside it. Keep both sentences short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.calculated.context: One of the two choices for what sort of data point this is, and the word shown in the list of data points once chosen: worked out by a formula from the other figures in the same submission, never sent in by the submitter. Keep it identical to the Calculated pill on the form. A choice in a picker, so it stays a bare adjective.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.cancelEdit.context: Closes the question about how to publish and puts the administrator back in the editor with every edit still in place; nothing is stored and nothing is lost. Cancel refers to the decision being asked for, not to the schema or to the editing session. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.caption.context: Labels the box where the administrator types their own heading to appear above this data point on the submission form. It names a place for the administrator's own wording, which is stored as typed and is not translated, so avoid any suggestion that the console supplies the text.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.captionHin.en: Optional heading rendered above this value in the submission form and view (think section title). Display-only; clients ignore it.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.captionHin.context: Guidance under that box: the heading is optional, appears above the data point both when filling the form in and when reading it back, and behaves like the title of a section. Display-only means it changes nothing about what is accepted; clients here are the programs that talk to the product's interface rather than people.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.checking.context: Grey status line that appears under a formula box for a moment while the server checks whether the formula is well formed. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept. It shares one fixed-height line with the pass and fail wordings, so all three must be about equally short and none may wrap.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.conditiona.context: Small-capitals heading over the two boxes that decide, from the other figures in the same submission, whether this data point can be filled in and whether it is shown at all. Conditional means depending on a condition; display is about visibility on the form, not a screen.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.create.context: Primary button that saves a brand-new schema for the first time; the editor shows a different caption once the schema exists. Imperative verb plus object.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.dateConstr.context: Small-capitals heading over the earliest and latest moments accepted for a data point of the Date type. Constraints are limits that are genuinely enforced when data is filed, unlike the charted target band. Use the same word for the type as the type picker uses.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.deleteType.context: Names the kind of object in the browser's prompt confirming removal of one value from a schema being edited; the value's own caption is quoted after it. A value is a single measure the schema collects — a field — not a quantity or an amount. Lower case, singular, and in whatever grammatical form your locale needs directly after the verb "delete".

joins.after: the delete verb of shell.confirm.delete; supplied as the {{noun}} of shell.confirm.namedSubject, followed by the value's caption in quotes
joins.example:
Delete value "Tonnes recycled"?

Removing a value that submissions already use may break them. Consider disabling it instead.
joins.note: Only appears for values that were already saved; newly added ones are dropped without asking. Rendered by the browser's own confirmation dialog, so no markup is possible.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.dependenci.context: Toolbar button opening a diagram of which data points feed which formulas and rules inside this schema. A noun naming what the diagram shows, not an instruction. Short — it sits in a crowded toolbar.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.discardCha.context: Fourth choice in the list offered when a published schema has been edited: throw the edits away and leave the editor, storing nothing. Discard means abandon and lose, and it cannot be undone — the edits are gone. Same register as the other choices in the list.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.draftUnava.en: Unavailable — {{count}} submission(s) already exist for this schema.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.draftUnava.context: Small grey line explaining why the choice above it is greyed out: data has already been filed against this schema, so it can no longer be taken out of circulation. Submissions are filled-in instances of the schema.

placeholders.count: How many submissions already exist, e.g. 12. English fakes the plural with '(s)'

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.editTitle.context: Heading at the top of the screen where an existing schema is changed. Noun phrase or infinitive as your language prefers for a screen title; it names the screen, so avoid a command.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.editValue.context: Spoken by a screen reader for a row in the list of data points, whose whole surface opens that data point's editor. Describe the action the row performs; never abbreviate.

placeholders.name: The data point's display label, or its machine name when it has none, or a numbered stand-in when it has neither. Author-written and never translated, e.g. Tonnes collected

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.enabledIf.context: Labels the box where the administrator writes a condition deciding whether this data point can be filled in for a given submission. Reads as a label — the enabling condition — not as a sentence about being enabled. Keep it parallel with the visibility label beside it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.enabledIfH.en: When false (or null) the value is disabled in the UI and a submitted sample is dropped with a warning. Empty = always enabled.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.enabledIfH.context: Guidance under that box. When the condition works out to false, or to nothing at all, the box is greyed out on the form and any figure that is nevertheless sent in is dropped with a warning rather than refusing the whole submission. Leaving the box empty means the data point is always available; a sample is one figure inside a submission.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.enabledPub.context: Labels the tick box that decides whether the schema is in circulation: ticked, services can file data against it; unticked, it is a draft nobody can submit against. Published in the sense of released for use, and the bracketed word is a gloss on the first, so keep both. This can be turned back and forth, but only while no data has been filed.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.expression.context: Labels the box holding the formula that works out a calculated data point from the other figures in the same submission. Expression in the mathematical sense — a formula — not a phrase or a look.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.expression.en: NCalc formula referencing sibling values in the same submission only (e.g. average(a, b)). Chaining to other calculated values is allowed.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.expression.context: Guidance under that box. NCalc is the name of the formula language and average(a, b) is one of its functions: leave both exactly as written, since function names are typed in English whatever the console language. It may only read data points of the same schema in the same submission, including other calculated ones.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMax.context: Labels the box holding the upper edge of the ideal range shown on charts for a numeric data point. Green is the best band of the red/amber/green scheme; keep the colour word in brackets. Charting decoration only — nothing is refused for falling outside it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMaxHi.en: Inner upper edge. Needs an amber max.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMaxHi.context: Guidance under that box: this edge sits inside the acceptable range, and it may only be set once the acceptable upper edge has been. Inner means nearer the middle of the band. Two very short sentences.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMin.context: Labels the box holding the lower edge of the ideal range shown on charts for a numeric data point. Green is the best band of the red/amber/green scheme; keep the colour word in brackets. Charting decoration only — nothing is refused for falling outside it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMinHi.en: Inner lower edge. Needs an amber min.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.greenMinHi.context: Guidance under that box: this edge sits inside the acceptable range, and it may only be set once the acceptable lower edge has been. Inner means nearer the middle of the band. Keep both sentences short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.incrementV.context: First and recommended choice offered when a schema already in circulation has been edited: store the edits under the next version number. A version is a numbered revision of the definition; raising the number leaves everything already filed under the old number untouched, and the number can never be lowered again. Increment means raise by one.

placeholders.version: The number the schema would move up to, e.g. 4

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.kind.context: Heads the narrow column, and labels the picker in the value editor, saying which of two sorts a data point is: one the submitter fills in, or one worked out by a formula. Deliberately not the same word as Type, which is the separate column for the sort of data — text, number, date — so the two must stay clearly distinct in your language. Very short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.kindHint.en: Calculated values are computed from sibling values in the same submission and are never submitted.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.kindHint.context: Guidance under that picker: a data point of the calculated sort is worked out from the other figures in the same submission and is never sent in by a submitter. Values means data points of the same schema.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.layoutHint.en: Drag values into sections to group them. This affects the submission form layout only — the server treats submissions as flat lists.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.layoutHint.context: Guidance above the arranging area: data points can be dragged into sections to group them. It changes only how the form looks to whoever fills it in — what is stored and what programs receive stays one flat list — so make clear that this is presentation, not structure.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.loading.context: Line beside a spinner while the schema being opened is fetched. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept; loading means fetching for display, and nothing is being changed.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.max.context: Labels the box holding the largest number accepted for this data point; the bound is inclusive and it is genuinely enforced when data is filed, unlike the charted target band below it. Abbreviate as English does — the box sits in a narrow two-column grid — and use the same abbreviation as the limits line on the form.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.maxDate.context: Labels the box holding the latest moment accepted for a data point of the Date type; the bound is inclusive. ISO names the international way of writing a date, such as 2026-12-31, which the administrator types by hand — leave the abbreviation in English and keep the brackets.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.maxLength.context: Labels the box holding how many characters the text may run to at most; counted in characters, not words. Abbreviate as English does — the box sits in a narrow two-column grid.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.min.context: Labels the box holding the smallest number accepted for this data point; the bound is inclusive and it is genuinely enforced when data is filed, unlike the charted target band below it. Abbreviate as English does and match the limits line shown on the form.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.minDate.context: Labels the box holding the earliest moment accepted for a data point of the Date type; the bound is inclusive. ISO names the international way of writing a date, such as 2026-01-01, typed by hand — leave the abbreviation in English and keep the brackets.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.minLength.context: Labels the box holding how many characters the text must run to at least; counted in characters, not words. Abbreviate as English does — the box sits in a narrow two-column grid.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.moveToDraf.en: Move the schema back to Draft and apply the changes
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.moveToDraf.context: Third choice offered when a schema already in circulation has been edited: store the edits and at the same time take the schema out of circulation, so nobody can file data against it until it is put back. Draft is the state of a definition not yet released for use; the step can be reversed by publishing again, and it is offered only while no data has been filed. Imperative, like the other choices.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.nameFixed.en: The schema name is fixed after creation — changing it could break validation rules and existing submissions.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.nameFixed.context: Guidance under the greyed-out name box on an existing schema: the machine name is settled at creation and cannot be changed afterwards, because rules and data already filed refer to the schema by it. Name here is the identifier, distinct from the display label in the box beside it, which can be changed freely.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.needsValue.en: A schema needs at least one value to be useful.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.needsValue.context: Shown in a blue information bar where the list of data points would be, while the schema still defines none. A value is one data point; useful is the point — a schema without any collects nothing. Not an error, and not a refusal to save.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.noRules.context: Shown where the list of rules that check a whole submission would be, when there are none and the reader cannot add any because they are looking at a stored version rather than editing. Yet implies none so far, without suggesting any are required.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.noRulesAdd.en: No rules yet. Use "Add rule" to create one.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.noRulesAdd.context: Shown where the list of rules that check a whole submission would be, when there are none yet and the reader can add some. The quoted words repeat the caption of the button just below, so use exactly the wording you gave that button, quotation marks included.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.notFound.context: Bold headline of the red bar shown in place of the editor when the schema named in the address cannot be produced. Names the situation, so keep it a short noun-style phrase without a closing period.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.numericCon.context: Small-capitals heading over the smallest and largest numbers accepted for a data point. Constraints are limits genuinely enforced when data is filed, unlike the charted target band that follows. Numeric covers both whole numbers and ones with decimals.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.publishAsI.en: Publish as-is without changing the version
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.publishAsI.context: Second choice offered when a schema already in circulation has been edited: put the edits into circulation while leaving the version number alone. As-is means unchanged, and it refers to the version number, not to the edits; submitters then get no signal that anything about the form has changed. Same register as the other choices in the list.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.publishCha.context: Heading of the small window that opens when a schema already in circulation has been edited without its version number being raised. Publish means putting the edited definition into circulation so services file against it. Names the decision being asked for; no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.publishHel.en: You changed this published schema but didn't update the version number. What would you like to do?
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.publishHel.context: Body of that window, addressing the administrator directly and ending in a genuine question whose answers are the choices listed beneath. Published means in circulation; the version number is the number that marks a revision of the definition, raised by hand.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.readOnlySn.context: Bold headline of the blue bar at the top of the editor when what is on screen is a stored copy of the definition as it stood at one past save, opened only for reading. A snapshot is that stored copy; read-only means nothing on the screen can be changed. Short noun phrase, no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.regexPatte.context: Labels the box where the administrator types a character pattern that text sent for this data point must satisfy. Regex is the accepted technical term for such a pattern and is normally left as it is; whatever the administrator types is not translated.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.removeRule.context: Serves both as the hover text and as the spoken name of the small cross beside one rule box, which takes that rule out of the list. Remove means take away, and it is undone only by not saving. Imperative, and short enough for a hover bubble.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.removeValu.en:
Removing a value can break validation rules and reject or alter existing submissions. Consider disabling it instead (uncheck "Enabled") to keep historical data intact.

Remove it anyway?
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.removeValu.context: Body of the confirmation the browser puts up before a data point that already exists is taken out of the schema: rules that mention it stop working and data already filed may be refused or altered. Keep the blank line and the closing question, which is what the reader answers. The quoted word repeats the caption of the tick box that keeps a data point in circulation, so use exactly the wording you gave it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.schemaMiss.en: No schema named "{{name}}" exists. It may have been deleted.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.schemaMiss.context: Sentence under that red headline: nothing by this name is on file, most likely because it was deleted since the link was made. Cautious about the cause — it says may have been — so keep the hedge.

placeholders.name: The schema's machine name taken from the address, exactly as written and never translated, e.g. waste_monthly

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.sinceVersi.context: Labels the box holding the number of the version in which this data point first appeared. Since means starting from and including; a version is a numbered revision of the schema definition.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.sinceVersi.en: Optional. When set and equal to the schema's current version ({{version}}), the SPA shows a "New" tag next to this value for one cadence period. Leave empty for "always present".
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.sinceVersi.context: Guidance under that box: filling it with the schema's present version number makes the app that submitters use flag the data point as newly added, and only for one reporting period. Leaving it empty means treating the data point as having always been there. The quoted word is a small badge shown to submitters in that other app; keep the quotation marks.

placeholders.version: The schema's present version number, e.g. 3

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.snapshotHe.en: Version {{version}} saved <savedAt /> {{author}}. This is a historical view and cannot be edited — it does not affect the current schema.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.snapshotHe.context: Sentence under the blue headline saying which stored copy is on screen, when it was saved and by whom, and that reading it changes nothing about the definition in use. Keep <savedAt /> exactly as it is — the date and time are rendered in its place, formatted for the reader's language — and move it if your word order needs it.

placeholders.version: The version number the schema had at that save, e.g. 3
placeholders.author: An already-translated attribution of the form 'by <name>', or empty when the account is unknown, e.g. by A. Rossi

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.snapshotMi.en: This version snapshot no longer exists. It may have been deleted from the history.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.snapshotMi.context: Sentence under the red headline when the stored copy that was asked for is no longer on file, most likely because an administrator cleared it out of the history. Hedged — it says may have been — and note that deleting stored copies never touches the definition in use.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.stringCons.context: Small-capitals heading over the length limits and the character pattern for a data point that holds text. String is the product's word for a text data point, so use the same word as the type picker uses; constraints are limits genuinely enforced when data is filed.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.syntaxErro.context: Red status line under a formula box saying the formula is not well formed; the server's own explanation is printed immediately after it. Syntax means the grammar of the formula, not whether it gives a sensible answer. Keep the colon, and keep it short — it shares one fixed-height line with the checking and pass wordings.

joins.before: The explanation returned by the server, which arrives in English only and is never translated
joins.example: Syntax error: Parse error at line 1: unexpected token ')'

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.tabs.appro.context: Tab holding the rules for who has to sign a submission off before it counts, hidden altogether when that workflow is switched off for the deployment. Plural noun naming the sign-offs, not an instruction to approve. Short and stable — administrators navigate here by habit.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.tabs.gener.context: First tab of the schema editor, holding the schema's own particulars: names, whether it is in circulation, its version number, and who may see it. General in the sense of overall, as opposed to the tabs about individual data points. Short and stable.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.tabs.layou.context: Tab where the data points are dragged into sections to decide how the submission form reads. Layout means visual arrangement; it changes nothing about what is stored. Short and stable.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.tabs.valid.context: Tab holding the rules that judge a whole filled-in submission at once. Plural noun naming the checks themselves; keep it distinct from the per-data-point rule labelled inside the value editor. Short and stable.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.targetBand.context: Small-capitals heading over the four edges that shade a numeric data point's charts. A target band is the range a figure is supposed to fall in; RAG stands for red, amber and green and is best kept recognisable, since the boxes beneath it name those colours. Optional in brackets means none of it need be filled in.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.targetBand.en: Reporting-only Red/Amber/Green ranges shown as shaded bands on charts — never enforced. The acceptable (amber) range is the outer band; the ideal (green) range sits inside it. Outside the amber range is red. Each edge is optional, but a green edge needs the matching amber edge on the same side, and edges must read low-to-high: amber min ≤ green min ≤ green max ≤ amber max.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.targetBand.context: Grey paragraph explaining the four edges: they are drawn as shaded bands on charts and nothing is ever refused for falling outside them. Acceptable is the outer range and ideal the inner one, anything beyond the outer range counts as red, and every edge is optional so long as an inner edge is paired with the outer edge on its own side. Keep the ≤ signs and the ordering they express exactly as they are.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.unit.context: Labels the box where the administrator types the unit of measure for this data point — tonnes, hours, per cent. Unit of measurement only; nothing to do with an organisational unit. What is typed is shown beside the figure and is never translated or checked.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.userDefine.context: The ordinary of the two sorts of data point, and the word shown in the list once chosen: one whose figure is sent in by whoever submits, rather than worked out by a formula. It says where the figure comes from, not that anybody invented the data point; keep it clearly opposed to the calculated sort.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validSynta.context: Green status line under a formula box: the formula is well formed and the server could read it. It says nothing about whether the formula gives the answer the administrator intended. Shares one fixed-height line with the checking and failure wordings, so keep it about as short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validation.context: Small-capitals heading over the two rule boxes belonging to a single data point: the one that can refuse a figure and the one that only cautions. Validation means checking submitted data against rules.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validation.en: e.g. if(expenses > revenue, 'expenses cannot exceed revenue', null)
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validation.context: Ghost text in an empty rule box, showing by example how a rule is written: test something, give back a message when it is wrong, and give back nothing when it is fine. Leave the formula itself alone — the function name, the names of the data points and the word for nothing are typed in English whatever the console language — though the message inside the quotes may be put into your language, since it stands for wording the administrator would write.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validation.en: Each rule runs once per submission against every value in the schema. Add several to enforce multiple cross-value invariants.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.validation.context: Guidance above the list of rules that judge a whole submission: each one is evaluated once per submission and can look at every data point in the schema at the same time. Cross-value invariants are conditions that must hold between several data points, such as one figure never exceeding another.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueDetai.context: Heading of the side panel where a single data point is defined, used only until the data point has a name of its own to show there instead. Details means its particulars; value is one data point of the schema.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameF.en: The name is fixed after creation — it is referenced by validation rules and existing submissions. Add a new value if you need a different name.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameF.context: Guidance under the greyed-out name box of a data point that already exists: the machine name is settled once saved, because rules and data already filed refer to it by that name. The closing sentence tells the administrator that defining an additional data point is the way round it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameH.en: Used as the identifier in validation rules. Must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, digits, and underscores.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameH.context: Guidance under the name box of a new data point: this is the name formulas and rules use to refer to it, and it is spelled with unaccented letters, digits and underscores only, never starting with a digit. Identifier means a machine-readable name; it is not shown to submitters, who see the display label instead.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameV.en: Must be a valid identifier: letters, digits and underscores only; cannot start with a digit.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNameV.context: Red message under the name box when what has been typed cannot serve as a machine-readable name. States the rule rather than addressing the reader, so keep it impersonal; letters here means unaccented Latin letters.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueNumbe.context: Stands in for the name of a data point that has neither a machine name nor a display label yet, so a freshly added row can still be pointed at. Keep the brackets, and replace the number sign with whatever your language uses before an ordinal figure. Appears in the row, in its hover bubble, and inside the row's spoken name.

placeholders.number: The data point's position in the list, counting from one, e.g. 3

joins.after: Nothing on its own, but it is also substituted into the spoken name of the row

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueValid.context: Labels the box holding the rule that judges the figure sent for this one data point and can refuse it. Value means the figure for this data point; keep it distinct from the schema-wide rules on the Validations tab.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueValid.en: Runs against the submitted sample. Vars include value, minimum, maximum. Whitespace and line breaks are ignored.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.valueValid.context: Guidance under that box: the rule is applied to each figure sent in, and inside the formula the words value, minimum and maximum stand for that figure and the bounds set above — leave those three exactly as they are, since they are typed in English. Spaces and line breaks in the formula make no difference, so it may be laid out over several lines.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.versionHin.en: Bump when introducing new values. Cannot decrease. Each value's 'Since version' must be ≤ this.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.versionHin.context: Guidance under the version number box: raise it when data points are added, it can never be lowered, and no data point may claim to have appeared in a later version than this. Bump means raise by one; the quoted words repeat the label of a box in the value editor, so use exactly the wording you gave it, and keep the ≤ sign.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.viewVersio.context: Heading of the screen showing a stored copy of a schema as it stood at one past save, for reading only. View is a verb here — look at, without changing; a version is a numbered revision of the definition.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.visibleIf.context: Labels the box where the administrator writes a condition deciding whether this data point appears on the form at all. Reads as a label — the visibility condition — not as a sentence. Keep it parallel with the enabling label above it.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.visibleIfH.en: When false (or null) the value is hidden in the UI. Server-side behaves like Enabled if. Empty = always visible.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.visibleIfH.context: Guidance under that box. When the condition works out to false, or to nothing at all, the data point is left off the form entirely, and anything nevertheless sent in for it is dropped with a warning exactly as with the enabling condition. Leaving the box empty means it is always shown; the reference to the other box must use the wording you gave that label.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.visibleSer.context: Labels the picker naming which services may see this schema and file data against it; it appears only when the schema is not open to all of them. A service is an organisational unit that submits data. Visible to means available to, not merely displayed.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.warning.context: Labels the box holding the rule that flags a figure as worth a second look without refusing it. A noun naming what the rule produces, not a caution addressed to the administrator reading the label.

schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.warningHin.en: Optional rule that produces a non-blocking warning when true or when it returns a non-empty string.
schemasSubmissions.schemaEdit.warningHin.context: Guidance under that box: the rule is optional, and it raises a caution — never a refusal — either when it works out to true or when it gives back some text. That text is then shown to the submitter word for word as the administrator wrote it, so it is not translated. Non-blocking means the submission still goes through.

schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.bucketD.en: {{count}} bucket(s) — whiskers show min/max, dot shows the average
schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.bucketD.context: Small grey caption under a chart's heading, saying how many reporting windows are plotted and how to read the marks: the vertical lines span the lowest and highest figures in a window and the dot marks the mean. A bucket is one reporting window's worth of figures; whiskers are those vertical lines. The card is narrow, so keep it brief.

placeholders.count: How many reporting windows are plotted, e.g. 12. English fakes the plural with '(s)'

schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.minAvgM.context: Label in the chart's hover bubble against three figures printed in this order — lowest, mean, highest — followed by how many samples the window held. Abbreviate all three as English does and keep the slashes and the order; the bubble is extremely tight on space.

schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.noNumer.en: This schema has no numeric values, so there's nothing to chart. Add a Number or Integer value to see a timeline.
schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.noNumer.context: Shown in a blue information bar in place of every chart, because charts can only be drawn for data points that hold figures. Number and Integer name two of the data types in the editor, so use exactly the words the type picker uses for them; a timeline is the chart itself.

schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.noSampl.context: Centred in the card where a data point's chart would be, when no figures have ever been filed for it. Samples are the individual figures filed against the data point; yet leaves room for some arriving later.

schemasSubmissions.schemaHistory.title.context: Heading of the screen charting how a schema's figures have moved over time; the schema's own name is appended after a dash, so end without punctuation. Historical means past-and-present record, not merely old.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.action.context: Spoken by a screen reader for the three-dots button at the end of a row in the list of stored copies of a schema, which opens that row's menu. Describe what the button leads to; never abbreviate.

placeholders.version: The version number the schema had at that save, e.g. 3

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.author.context: Heads the column naming the account that performed the save, and is reused as a column heading in the exported spreadsheet. Author means whoever made the change, not a writer. Very short noun.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.bumped.context: Small pill printed beside the version number when that save was the one that raised it, as opposed to a save that left the number alone. A past participle describing the number; keep it lower case as the English does, and very short — it shares a 110-pixel column with the number itself.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.change.context: Heads the column giving when the save happened, and is reused as a column heading in the exported spreadsheet. Date here covers the time of day as well. Very short; the column is 180 pixels wide.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.delete.context: Red entry in the page menu that throws away every stored copy of this schema's past saves. All means the whole history, not the schema itself, which is left in place. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.delete.en: This removes every saved snapshot for this schema. The current schema is unaffected. This cannot be undone.
schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.delete.context: The consequence spelled out in the confirmation the browser puts up before that clearing goes ahead: every stored copy of past saves goes, the definition in use is untouched, and there is no way back. Snapshot means one stored copy of the definition as it stood at a save. Keep all three statements — the reader is deciding on the strength of them.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.delete.en: This removes the snapshot from the history only. The current schema is unaffected. This cannot be undone.
schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.delete.context: The consequence spelled out in the confirmation before one stored copy is thrown away: only the record of that past save goes, the definition in use is untouched, and there is no way back. Snapshot means that stored copy.
Red entry in a row's menu that throws away the one stored copy that row stands for. This entry means that row, not the schema. Imperative and short.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.empty.context: Fills the table when no past saves are on file for this schema, either because none has happened in the chosen span of dates or because the history was cleared. Recorded means kept on file. Not an error.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.entire.context: Names what is about to be deleted inside the browser's confirmation question, where it is followed by the schema's name in quotation marks. Keep it lower case and a bare noun phrase so it reads on from the verb that precedes it.

joins.before: The schema's name in quotation marks, then a question mark, a blank line and the warning about what will be lost
joins.after: The word 'Delete' and a space, from the confirmation template

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.entry.context: Names what is about to be deleted inside the browser's confirmation question, where it is followed in quotation marks by the version number and date of the save concerned. Keep it lower case and a bare noun phrase so it reads on from the verb that precedes it.

joins.before: The version and date label in quotation marks, then a question mark, a blank line and the warning about what will be lost
joins.after: The word 'Delete' and a space, from the confirmation template

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.entryL.context: Identifies one past save inside the browser's confirmation question, appearing there in quotation marks. The lower-case v abbreviates version and can be replaced by whatever short marker your language uses before a version number; from introduces the moment of the save.

placeholders.version: The version number the schema had at that save, e.g. 3
placeholders.date: The date and time of the save, already formatted for the reader's language, e.g. 11 Aug 2026, 14:32

joins.after: The name of the thing being deleted, then an opening quotation mark

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.export.context: Entry in the page menu that writes the list of past saves to a spreadsheet file the reader downloads. Export means write out to a file; CSV names the file format and stays in English. While the file is being prepared the entry is replaced by a progress wording.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.newVer.context: Heads the column giving the version number the schema had after that save, beside the column for the number it had before. New means after the change, not recent. Very short; the column is 110 pixels wide.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.oldVer.context: Heads the column giving the version number the schema had before that save; it is empty for the save that created the schema. Old means previous, not obsolete. Very short; the column is 110 pixels wide.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.title.context: Heading of the screen listing every past save of one schema, one row per save. Version history means the record of numbered revisions; the dash separates it from the schema's own name.

placeholders.name: The schema's machine name as it appears in the address, never translated, e.g. waste_monthly

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.viewTh.context: Entry in a row's menu that opens the stored copy of the definition as it stood at that save, for reading only. View is a verb — look at without changing anything; this version means the one that row stands for.

schemasSubmissions.schemaVersions.viewVe.context: Spoken by a screen reader for a row in the list of past saves, whose whole surface opens the stored copy of that revision for reading. Describe the action the row performs; never abbreviate.

placeholders.version: The version number the schema had at that save, e.g. 3

schemasSubmissions.schemas.audience.context: Names who a schema is offered to — every service, or only the ones an administrator has picked. Audience means the set of services allowed to file against it, never a group of spectators. The same word heads a narrow column, labels a group of controls in the editor, and heads a column in the exported spreadsheet, so keep it short.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.bumpedAt.context: Trails the version number in the read-only view of a schema, saying when that number was last raised. Keep <bumpedAt /> exactly as it is, since the date and time are rendered in its place in the reader's own format, and keep the lower case — it continues a line that has already begun.

joins.after: The version number, a space, a middle dot and a space

schemasSubmissions.schemas.deleteType.context: Names the kind of object in the browser's delete confirmation prompt; the schema's own label is quoted after it. A schema is the definition of what may be submitted, not a database schema. Lower case, singular, and in whatever grammatical form your locale needs directly after the verb "delete".

joins.after: the delete verb of shell.confirm.delete; supplied as the {{noun}} of shell.confirm.namedSubject, followed by the schema's label in quotes
joins.example:
Delete schema "Monthly waste KPIs"?

This cannot be undone.
joins.note: Exists separately from the Schema column header because that one starts a sentence and this one sits inside one. Rendered by the browser's own confirmation dialog, so no markup is possible.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.empty.en: No schemas yet — click "New schema" to create one.
schemasSubmissions.schemas.empty.context: Fills the table when no schema has been defined in this deployment yet. The quoted words repeat the caption of the button at the top of the screen, so use exactly the wording you gave it, quotation marks included.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.exampleJson.context: Entry in the download menu that saves a specimen filled-in submission for this schema, of the shape a program would send. Example describes the file, and submission is one filled-in instance of the schema; JSON names the file format and stays in English.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.frozen.context: Pill shown instead of the modifiable one when data already filed against this schema can never be replaced. Frozen is a figure of speech for fixed and unalterable, nothing to do with temperature. One word; badges do not wrap.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.globalAudienc.context: Labels the tick box that opens a schema to every service rather than to a chosen few, and is shown as the audience in the read-only view when it is ticked. Global means without restriction here; the bracketed phrase glosses it, so keep both. A service is an organisational unit that submits data.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.importFailed.context: Bold headline of the red bar when a schema definition read from a file could not be taken in; the reason from the file itself follows. Import means bringing a definition in from a file. Short phrase, no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.jsonObjectErr.en: JSON root must be an object.
schemasSubmissions.schemas.jsonObjectErr.context: Reason given when the chosen file cannot be read as a schema definition because its outermost content is not a single set of named properties — a list or a bare number, for instance. JSON is the file format and object is its technical term for such a set of properties; keep both in English. Root means the outermost level of the file.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.modifiableApp.en: Re-submitting data for a window that already has a submission replaces it and resets approval to Pending — even if it was previously approved — so the earlier values are withdrawn from live reporting and ultimately overwritten. Mark the schema (or value) as not modifiable if approved figures should never change mid-cycle.
schemasSubmissions.schemas.modifiableApp.context: Amber bar in the read-only view of a schema that both allows replacement and needs sign-off, explaining the consequence: filing again for a window that already has a submission supersedes it and sends it back for sign-off, so figures already approved drop out of live reporting until somebody approves them again. Pending is the name of the awaiting-sign-off state, so use the same word the console uses for it, and the words in brackets refer to the two tick boxes the administrator can untick.

Bold headline of that amber bar, naming the combination of settings that causes the problem: the schema accepts replacements and also requires sign-off. Approval-gated means nothing counts until a reviewer approves it. Short phrase, no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.new.context: Caption of the button that starts a brand-new schema, and also the heading of the screen it opens, so it has to work both as something to press and as a title. New qualifies schema; no verb in the English, and adding one would read oddly as a heading.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.noServices.context: Stands where the read-only view lists the services a schema is offered to, when it is restricted but no service has actually been picked — so nobody can file against it. Keep the brackets and the lower case, which mark it as a remark rather than a name.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.noValuesDefin.context: Shown in a blue bar where the list of a schema's data points would be, when it defines none. Values are the data points; defined means declared by the administrator. Not an error.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.schemaJson.context: Entry in the download menu that saves the schema's own definition to a file, which can later be read back in to recreate it. JSON names the file format and stays in English; as means in the form of.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.schemaPdf.context: Entry in the download menu that saves a printable document describing the schema, for circulating to whoever has to fill the form in. PDF stays in English; as means in the form of.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.serviceCount.context: Stands in the audience column for a schema offered only to particular services, saying how many were picked, and appears in the same column of the exported spreadsheet. Very tight on space — the column is 160 pixels wide — so keep it to the figure and one short noun.

placeholders.count: How many services the schema is offered to, e.g. 4. English fakes the plural with '(s)'

schemasSubmissions.schemas.submissionVal.context: Small-capitals heading over the rules that judge a whole filled-in submission at once, both in the editor and in the read-only view. Plural noun naming the checks; keep it distinct from the rule attached to a single data point.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.testSubmissio.context: Entry in a row's menu that opens a rehearsal of filing data against this schema: the real checks run on the server and nothing is stored. Test qualifies submission — a submission made only as a trial — and the same wording headlines the window it opens, so keep the two identical.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.title.context: Heading of the screen listing every schema in the deployment, and the same word names the entry in the sidebar. A schema is a form definition an administrator writes; plural here.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.upload.context: Entry in the page menu that asks for a definition file from the reader's computer and opens the editor filled in from it; nothing is stored until the administrator saves. Upload means send from this computer to the product. Imperative.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.validationRul.context: Spoken by a screen reader for one of the numbered boxes holding a rule that judges a whole submission, since the boxes carry no visible label of their own. Never abbreviate.

placeholders.number: The rule's position in the list, counting from one, e.g. 2

schemasSubmissions.schemas.valuesCount.context: Small-capitals heading over the list of a schema's data points in the read-only view, with how many there are in brackets. Values are the data points defined by the schema.

placeholders.count: How many data points the schema defines, e.g. 7

schemasSubmissions.schemas.viewHistorica.context: Opens the charts of how this schema's figures have moved over the reporting windows. It appears as an entry in a row's menu and as the caption of a split button in the read-only view, so keep it short. View is a verb; historical data means the figures already filed, not old versions of the definition.

schemasSubmissions.schemas.viewSchema.context: Spoken by a screen reader for a row in the list of schemas, whose whole surface opens a read-only panel about that schema. Describe the action the row performs; never abbreviate.

placeholders.name: The schema's display name, or its machine name when it has none. Author-written and never translated, e.g. Monthly waste KPIs

schemasSubmissions.schemas.viewVersionHi.context: Opens the list of past saves of this schema's definition, one row per save. Deliberately not the same thing as the charts of filed figures offered next to it: this is the record of how the definition itself changed. View is a verb here.

schemasSubmissions.submissionDetail.chan.context: Heads the column saying what sort of alteration was recorded against a submission. A noun naming the kind of event, never a verb telling the reader to change something. Very short.
Green pill in that column marking the event where the submission was first filed. A noun naming the event, not a command; keep it to one word, since badges do not wrap.
Red pill in that column marking the event where the submission was removed. A noun naming the event, not a command; one word, since badges do not wrap.

Pill in that column marking the event where a fresh filing for the same service and reporting window took the place of this one wholesale. Replace is the product's word for superseding a submission rather than editing it; a noun naming the event, and one word only.
Pill in that column marking the event where the submission was altered in place, as opposed to being superseded by a fresh filing. A noun naming the event, not a command; one word only.

Heads the column naming whoever made the recorded change; it may show a person or a machine account, and falls back to a bare identifier when no name is known. Passive phrase naming the actor. Very short.

schemasSubmissions.submissionDetail.deta.context: First tab of a single submission's screen, holding its particulars and the table of figures it carries; the other tab holds the record of changes. Plural noun; short and stable, since reviewers navigate here by habit.

schemasSubmissions.submissionDetail.noCh.context: Fills the table on the changes tab when nothing has been recorded against this submission since it was filed. Recorded means kept on file. Not an error.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.accept.context: Bold headline of the amber bar after a submission has been stored but the server raised cautions about some figures; the cautions themselves are listed underneath. Accepted means it went through — this is not a failure — and the wording of each caution comes from the rule the administrator wrote.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.cloned.en: The service, schema and values were pre-filled and the timestamp reset to now. Review them, adjust the service or schema if needed, then Submit to create a new submission.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.cloned.context: Explanation under that headline: the service, the schema and the figures were copied from the earlier submission and the moment was set to now, and nothing is stored until the reader presses the button named at the end. Use exactly the caption you gave that button. Second person and imperative, addressing whoever is filling the form in.

Bold headline of the blue bar when the form has been filled in from an earlier submission as a starting point. Cloned means copied; despite the past tense, nothing has been filed yet — this is still a new, unsaved submission.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.editDr.context: Heading of the screen when the submission being worked on is still a draft: a work in progress that counts towards nothing until it is published. Draft is a state, not a document type; edit is a verb.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.editTi.context: Heading of the screen when the submission being changed has already been filed. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a reporting window; edit is a verb.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.missin.context: Bold headline of the red bar when the reader tries to file the form while data points the schema insists on are still empty; their labels are listed immediately underneath. Required means demanded by the schema. Nothing was stored.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.multiS.en: Saving will keep only the values for {{name}}. Pick another schema first if you need those values instead.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.multiS.context: Explanation under that amber headline: only the figures belonging to the named schema will be kept, and the others will be dropped, so the reader should change the schema first if it is the others they wanted. Second person; the schema named is whichever one is chosen in the picker above.

placeholders.name: The chosen schema's display name, or its machine name when it has none. Author-written and never translated, e.g. Monthly waste KPIs

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.multiS.en: The source submission contained values from multiple schemas.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.multiS.context: Bold headline of the amber bar when the submission this form was filled in from carried figures belonging to more than one schema, which the form itself cannot hold. Source submission means the one the figures were copied from.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.newTit.context: Heading of the screen where a submission is filled in from scratch. New qualifies submission; no verb in the English, and one would read oddly as a heading.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.noValu.en: This schema has no values defined.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.noValu.context: Shown in an amber bar where the boxes to fill in would be, because the chosen schema declares no data points, so there is nothing to enter. Values are the data points; not an error in what the reader has done.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSc.context: Ghost text in the empty schema picker, prompting the reader to choose which form definition they are filling in. Pick means choose from a list; a schema is a form definition an administrator wrote.
Red bar at the foot of the form when filing is attempted with no schema chosen; nothing was stored. Second person imperative, and first means before anything else can be done.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSc.en: Pick a schema to see the values you can submit.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSc.context: Blue bar standing where the boxes to fill in will appear, telling a submitter that choosing a form definition is what makes them appear. Values means the individual data points they will be asked for. Second person imperative.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSe.context: Ghost text in the empty service picker, prompting an administrator to say which service the data is being filed on behalf of. A service is an organisational unit that submits data, and the choice cannot be changed once the submission exists.
Red bar at the foot of the form when filing is attempted with no service chosen; nothing was stored. Second person imperative, and first means before anything else can be done.

Ghost text in the schema picker while it is still greyed out, because which schemas are on offer depends on the service chosen in the picker beside it. Keep it short: it sits inside a disabled control and carries no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSe.en: Pick a service and a schema to start entering values.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.pickSe.context: Blue bar standing where the boxes to fill in will appear, telling an administrator that both a service and a form definition are needed before anything can be entered. Second person imperative; values means the individual data points.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.saveAs.context: Choice under the main filing button that stores the form as a work in progress: it is kept, but counts towards no reporting and goes to nobody for sign-off until it is published later. As draft means in the draft state; imperative.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.saveFa.context: Bold headline of the red bar when the server refused the submission; its reasons follow underneath. Could not is a plain statement of failure, not the reader's fault, and nothing was stored.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.submit.context: Main button that files the entered figures for real: every rule is checked and, where the schema demands it, sign-off begins. Imperative verb — hand in, not merely save — and deliberately distinct from the draft choice beside it. It is named in the explanation shown when the form was filled in from an earlier submission, so keep the two identical.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.timest.context: Labels the date-and-time box saying when the figures were measured, which is what decides the reporting window they fall into. UTC is the universal time standard and stays in English in brackets, because the box is not adjusted to the reader's own time zone.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.timest.en: Applied to every sample in this submission.
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.timest.context: Guidance under that box: one moment is stamped on every figure in this submission — they cannot be timed individually. A sample is one figure inside a submission.

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.valueC.en: {{count}} values — leave optional ones empty to skip them
schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.valueC.context: Small grey line under the chosen schema's name, saying how many data points it declares and that anything not compulsory may simply be left blank. Skip means leave out of this submission, not postpone.

placeholders.count: How many data points the schema declares, e.g. 7

schemasSubmissions.submissionEdit.viewTi.context: Heading of the screen showing a submission laid out exactly like the form it was filled in on, but with every box locked. View is a verb — look at without changing.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.actionsFo.context: Spoken by a screen reader for the three-dots button at the end of a row in the list of submissions, which opens that row's menu. Describe what the button leads to; never abbreviate.

placeholders.id: The submission's internal identifier, a long string of letters and digits, e.g. 6f0a1c94-2f0b-4a11-9c1e-2b4d5f6a7b8c

schemasSubmissions.submissions.allSchema.context: Serves both as the ghost text in the schema filter and as its first choice, the one that stops the list being narrowed to a single form definition. All in the sense of no restriction; keep it short, since it sits inside a filter control.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.allServic.context: Serves both as the ghost text in the service filter and as its first choice, the one that stops the list being narrowed to a single service. All in the sense of no restriction; keep it short, since it sits inside a filter control.
