schemasSubmissions.submissions.approvals.context: Line in the panel about one submission, counting how many of the people who must sign it off already have. Shown only while it is still waiting; required approvals are the sign-offs the policy insists on, as the policy stood when sign-off began.

placeholders.approved: How many required approvers have signed off so far, e.g. 1
placeholders.count: How many are required in total, e.g. 2

schemasSubmissions.submissions.cloneNew.context: Entry in a row's menu that opens a blank filing form already filled in from this submission — same service, same schema, same figures, with the moment set to now. Clone means copy as a starting point; nothing is stored until the reader files it.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.createNew.context: Hover text on the button that starts a new submission, spelling out what the button does. Create means start and file a fresh one. No closing period.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.deleteTyp.context: Names the kind of object in the browser's delete confirmation prompt; the submission's own label is quoted after it. A submission is one set of reported values for one period, not the act of submitting. Lower case, singular, and in whatever grammatical form your locale needs directly after the verb "delete".

joins.after: the delete verb of shell.confirm.delete; supplied as the {{noun}} of shell.confirm.namedSubject, followed by the submission's label in quotes
joins.example:
Delete submission "Waste KPIs · March 2026"?

This cannot be undone.
joins.note: Exists separately from the Submission column header because that one starts a sentence and this one sits inside one. Rendered by the browser's own confirmation dialog, so no markup is possible.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.draftHelp.en: This submission is a work-in-progress draft. It is excluded from reporting and approval until it is published.
schemasSubmissions.submissions.draftHelp.context: Grey paragraph under the draft marker in the panel about one submission: while it stays a draft it is left out of reporting and nobody is asked to sign it off, and publishing is what ends that. Work-in-progress describes the state; published means filed for real.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.empty.context: Fills the table when nothing matches the service, schema, status and date-span filters above it. Match these filters points at those controls, so the reader knows to widen them; not an error.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.exportPdf.context: Entry in the panel's menu that saves a printable document of this one submission. Export means write out to a file; PDF stays in English; as means in the form of.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.exportXls.context: Entry in the page menu that writes the filtered submissions to a spreadsheet laid out as one grid, which is only possible for a single form definition at a time — hence the gloss in brackets. XLSX names the spreadsheet format and stays in English; while the file is being prepared the entry is replaced by a progress wording.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.exportXls.en: Export the filtered submissions to XLSX
schemasSubmissions.submissions.exportXls.context: Hover text on that entry when it can be used, saying that what gets written out is exactly the submissions the filters have left on screen. No closing period.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.importBul.context: Entry in the page menu that opens the window for filing many submissions at once from a file, instead of one form at a time. Import means bringing data in from a file; bulk means in quantity, not unrefined.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.interval..context: Choice in the date-span filter that lifts the limit on dates altogether, and the wording shown in the closed control once chosen. All time means from the very first submission to the latest; keep it short, since it must fit the filter control.
Choice in the date-span filter that reveals two boxes for a start and an end of the reader's own choosing. Custom means defined by the reader; range means the span between two moments. Keep it short.

Labels the picker that limits the list to submissions filed within a span of dates. Interval means a span of time; keep it distinct from the reporting window a submission belongs to, which is not what this filters on.

Choice in the date-span filter covering the thirty days up to now — counted back day by day, not the previous calendar month. Keep the figure, which is what makes that clear, and keep it short enough for the filter control.
Choice in the date-span filter covering the seven days up to now — counted back day by day, not the previous calendar week. Keep the figure and keep it short enough for the filter control.
Choice in the date-span filter covering the three hundred and sixty-five days up to now — counted back day by day, not the previous calendar year. Keep the figure and keep it short.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.manualEnt.context: Shown as the origin of a submission when a person typed the figures into this console; the alternative, for figures sent in by a program, is the untranslated word API. Manual means by hand, as opposed to automatically. Very short — it sits in a narrow column of the panel.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.myTitle.context: Heading of the list when the reader is a service and therefore sees only what its own account has filed; other readers get a plain heading instead. My is first person singular from the reader's point of view.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.new.context: Caption of the button that opens a blank filing form. New qualifies submission; the English has no verb, and it is greyed out with a hover explanation while filing is closed. Short — it shares the toolbar with a menu.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.pickSchem.en: Pick a single schema to enable the XLSX export
schemasSubmissions.submissions.pickSchem.context: Hover text on the greyed-out spreadsheet export, telling the reader that narrowing the schema filter to exactly one form definition is what makes it available. Single means one and only one; enable means make available, and it is the reader's own filter choice that does so.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectHel.en: This submission will be marked rejected and excluded from the OData feed and Explore, but stays visible here. You can leave an optional reason for the submitter and other reviewers.
schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectHel.context: Body of the window asking a reviewer to confirm turning a submission down: it is marked as rejected and drops out of the data feed and the analysis screens, but stays visible in this list, and a note explaining why may be left for the submitter and other reviewers. OData names the machine-readable data feed and Explore is the name of the analysis screen — keep both as proper names.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectPla.en: e.g. Week 22 figures look transposed — please re-check the night-shift totals.
schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectPla.context: Ghost text in the box for the reason, showing the sort of note a reviewer would leave. It stands for the reviewer's own words, so put it into natural wording of your language rather than translating it literally; keep it plausible as a remark about suspect figures.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectRea.context: Labels the box for the reviewer's explanation of why the submission was turned down. Reason means grounds or justification; the bracketed word says it may be left empty, and whatever is written is stored as typed and never translated.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejectTit.context: Heading of the window in which a reviewer turns a submission down. Reject means refuse to accept the figures; it does not delete them. Imperative verb plus object, no closing period.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejecting.context: Takes the place of the confirming button's caption while the refusal is being recorded. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, and it must fit the same button as the resting caption.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.rejection.context: Bold heading above the note a reviewer left when turning this submission down. The note itself is that reviewer's own wording and is shown as written, never translated.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.source.context: Labels the entry saying where a submission came from: typed into this console by a person, or sent in by a program. Source means origin, not source code.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.status.al.context: First choice in the status filter, the one that lifts the restriction so drafts and every stage of sign-off are listed together. All in the sense of no restriction; keep it short enough for the filter control.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.temporari.context: Hover text on the greyed-out button for starting a submission, when an administrator has stopped the product accepting data for the time being; an administrator can replace it with wording of their own. Closed means not accepting submissions at present, and temporarily says the block is expected to lift.

schemasSubmissions.submissions.viewFrom.context: Spoken by a screen reader for a row in the list of submissions, whose whole surface opens a panel about it. From introduces when it was filed and, in brackets, by which service. Describe the action; never abbreviate.

placeholders.label: The moment the submission was filed, already formatted for the reader's language, with the service's name in brackets when it is known, e.g. 11 Aug 2026, 14:32 (Northern depot)

schemasSubmissions.submissions.warningsC.context: Small-capitals heading over the cautions the server raised about this submission, with how many there are in brackets. Warnings never stopped the submission being accepted; the wording of each one comes from the rule an administrator wrote.

placeholders.count: How many cautions were raised, e.g. 2

analytics.common.actions.context: Header of the last, very narrow column of a data grid, the one holding each row's three-dot action menu. Plural noun naming the operations available on a row (edit, delete), never shares or stocks. In the audit grid the header is invisible and this text is only announced by screen readers, so keep it a full word rather than an abbreviation.

analytics.common.all.context: Top option of a filter picker (change type, target type, delivery status), meaning the list is not narrowed down and every value is included. It is short for 'all entries', so use the form that agrees with the records being listed, not a neuter 'everything'. Also shown as the collapsed text of the closed picker, which is about 180 px wide.

analytics.common.allServices.context: Option and checkbox label meaning the data or the event is not restricted to particular services but covers every one of them. A service is an organisational unit that submits data (a plant, a department), never a software service. The same wording is reused as the name of the single combined line on trend charts and as a table column header, so it must stay short enough not to wrap.

analytics.common.cadence.context: Labels the picker that chooses which reporting frequency to look at, and also heads a narrow table column. Cadence is the product term for how often a service is expected to submit a value: daily, weekly, fortnightly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annually or yearly. It is an expectation about frequency, not a speed or a rhythm, and each language should settle on one word and use it everywhere.

analytics.common.cancel.context: Closes the event editing panel and discards the unsaved changes. Imperative, and it abandons an edit in progress rather than cancelling anything that was already recorded.

analytics.common.delete.context: Row action and panel toolbar caption that permanently removes the event; a confirmation prompt follows. Imperative verb, as short as the English, because it shares a narrow menu with the edit action.

analytics.common.edit.context: Row action and panel toolbar caption that opens the event in an editable form. Imperative verb, not the noun for a change that was made.

analytics.common.exportCsv.context: Overflow-menu command that downloads the rows of the current audit tab as a spreadsheet file. Imperative. Leave CSV as the Latin acronym; it is a file format, not a word to translate.

analytics.common.exporting.context: Replaces the download command's caption while the file is being assembled, and the command is disabled until it finishes. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, and no longer than the resting caption because it sits in the same menu row.

analytics.common.exportListCsv.context: Overflow-menu command on the event log that downloads the complete event list as a spreadsheet file, not only the page currently on screen. Imperative; keep CSV as the Latin acronym and keep the parenthesis, which flags the file format.

analytics.common.exportView.context: Overflow-menu command that downloads exactly the rows the filters currently produce, that is the selected reporting frequency and reporting window. Imperative. 'View' means the current on-screen selection, not a visual appearance.

analytics.common.failedToLoad.context: Bold first line of a red message bar shown when a request for the page's data comes back with an error; the technical detail from the server is printed underneath. States what happened to the fetch, so it stays impersonal and does not tell the user what to do.

analytics.common.loading.context: Placeholder line shown inside a table body or a chart card while its data is still being fetched. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, and short enough to sit in one grid row; 'loading' means retrieving data, not putting a load on something.

analytics.common.moreActions.context: Announced by screen readers for the three-dot button that opens a page's overflow menu of commands such as refresh and download. Name the action the button performs; never abbreviate, because it is read aloud.

analytics.common.no.context: The 'off' choice in the picker that decides whether a chart also draws the same measurement from an earlier window for comparison; choosing it means no comparison line is drawn. A standalone negative answer to the picker's question, not a word glued into a sentence.

analytics.common.noData.context: Stands in for the trend chart when the selected reporting frequency has no windows to plot yet. A neutral statement that there is nothing to draw, not an error and not a failure to load.

analytics.common.period.context: Labels the control that limits the data to one reporting window, and also heads a table and spreadsheet column listing one window per row. A period is a reporting window over which submissions are collected, such as a single day, week or month; never a full stop, an era or a school lesson. Use the same word here as in the reporting-window notes elsewhere in the console.

analytics.common.refresh.context: Overflow-menu command that re-runs the page's queries so the figures reflect the latest data. Imperative, in the sense of fetching again; it does not restore, reset or renew anything.

analytics.common.save.context: Primary button that writes the event being edited to storage. Imperative, and 'save' means to store, never to economise or to rescue.

analytics.common.saving.context: Replaces the primary button's caption while the event is being written to storage. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, fitting the same button; it describes storing data, never saving money.

analytics.common.schema.context: Heads the column naming the schema a row belongs to, and also labels the schema picker. A schema is an administrator-defined form definition, a package of related values a service reports together; it is not a diagram, a plan or a database schema. Column width follows the data, so keep it to a single short noun.

analytics.common.selectedCount_one.context: Collapsed summary shown inside a closed multiple-choice picker once the user has ticked entries in it, counting the ticked services or schemas. Singular form, for exactly one ticked entry; 'selected' means ticked in this list. Space inside the closed control is tight, so keep it compact.

placeholders.count: Whole number of entries ticked in the picker, always 1 for this form, e.g. 1

analytics.common.selectedCount_other.context: Collapsed summary shown inside a closed multiple-choice picker once the user has ticked entries in it, counting the ticked services or schemas. Plural form; 'selected' means ticked in this list. Space inside the closed control is tight, so keep it compact.

placeholders.count: Whole number of entries ticked in the picker, two or more, e.g. 4

analytics.common.sending.context: Replaces the caption of the command that flushes queued notification e-mails or webhook deliveries, for as long as that flush is running. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, and no wider than the resting caption in the same menu row.

analytics.common.service.context: Heads the column naming the service a row belongs to, and also labels the service picker and a spreadsheet column. A service is an organisational unit with an account that submits data, such as a plant or a department, and never a software service or a service rendered to a customer. Keep it to one short noun; the column is sized by the data.

analytics.common.services.context: Title of the dashboard card whose big number is how many service accounts exist, and also the label of the service picker on the exploration screen. Plural of the organisational unit that submits data. Keep it short: the card is only about 220 px wide.

analytics.common.yes.context: Single-word cell value in the anomaly column of a trend table, marking that this window's figure was flagged as unusual; unflagged rows leave the cell empty. It is also written lower-cased into the exported spreadsheet. Keep it to one short word, and note it is not paired with the 'No' option of the comparison picker, which answers a different question.

analytics.cadence.daily.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per calendar day, so a service is expected to submit once a day. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.weekly.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per calendar week, running Monday to Sunday, so a service is expected to submit once a week. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.fortnightly.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per fourteen days, always starting on a Monday, so a service is expected to submit once every two weeks. Say every two weeks, never twice a week. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.monthly.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per calendar month, so a service is expected to submit once a month. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.quarterly.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per calendar quarter (January to March, April to June, July to September, October to December), so a service is expected to submit four times a year. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.semiannually.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per half calendar year (January to June, July to December), so a service is expected to submit twice a year. Twice a year, never once every two years. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.cadence.yearly.context: Reporting frequency in a cadence picker: one reporting window per calendar year, so a service is expected to submit once a year. Also inserted lower-cased into sentences of the form 'per … period', so prefer a form that reads correctly both alone in a list and inside a phrase.

analytics.periodFilter.intervals.all.context: Option in the date-range filter that applies no date limit at all, so records from the whole history of the system are listed. Neither a duration nor a window: it is the absence of any cut-off.

analytics.periodFilter.intervals.lastDay.context: Option in the date-range filter for a rolling window: the twenty-four hours ending at the present moment, counted backwards from now. It is not yesterday and not today so far, so avoid an idiom that can only mean the previous calendar day.

analytics.periodFilter.intervals.lastWee.context: Option in the date-range filter for a rolling window: the seven days ending at the present moment, counted backwards from now. It is emphatically not the previous calendar week, and several languages have a single idiom that can only carry the calendar sense, so choose wording that clearly means the last seven days.

analytics.periodFilter.intervals.lastMon.context: Option in the date-range filter for a rolling window: the thirty days ending at the present moment, counted backwards from now. It is not the previous calendar month, so avoid an idiom that can only carry the calendar sense; keep the figure thirty rather than converting it to 'a month'.

analytics.periodFilter.intervals.custom.context: Option in the date-range filter that lets the user type an explicit start and end instead of a rolling window; picking it reveals two date-and-time fields. 'Custom' means defined by the user for this occasion, and 'range' is a span of time.

analytics.periodFilter.from.context: Labels the date-and-time field holding the earliest moment to include when the user has chosen an explicit range; the moment itself is included. A preposition is used as a label here, so if that reads oddly, a short noun such as 'Start' is preferable. It sits above a narrow field, so keep it to one word.

analytics.periodFilter.to.context: Labels the date-and-time field holding the cut-off moment when the user has chosen an explicit range; records at exactly that moment are already excluded. A preposition is used as a label here, so if that reads oddly, a short noun such as 'End' is preferable. It sits above a narrow field, so keep it to one word.

analytics.dashboard.title.context: Heading of the landing screen that operators and administrators see first, a grid of summary cards plus the missing-submission panels. A neutral noun phrase for a summary of the whole system, not a verb and not 'summary of a document'.

analytics.dashboard.welcome.context: Replaces the landing screen's heading for signed-in accounts that only submit their own data. A greeting, so use the register a product would use with a logged-in user; keep the comma placement natural for the language.

placeholders.name: Display name of the signed-in account, which may be a person or an organisational unit rather than a human name, e.g. Rossi Plant

analytics.dashboard.cards.pendingApprova.context: Title of the summary card whose big number is how many submissions are waiting for a reviewer to approve or reject them. 'Pending' means awaiting a decision, not imminent or unresolved in any other sense, and an approval here is the decision itself. The card is about 220 px wide, so keep it short.

analytics.dashboard.cards.operators.context: Title of the summary card whose big number is how many accounts hold the operator role, the staff who monitor and manage reported data across services. It counts people's accounts, not machines or plant operators. Keep it short; the card is about 220 px wide.

analytics.dashboard.cards.admins.context: Title of the summary card whose big number is how many accounts hold the administrator role, the ones allowed to configure the system. The English is deliberately the short form; use the equivalent short form if the language has one, because the card is only about 220 px wide.

analytics.dashboard.cards.submissions.context: Title of the summary card whose big number is how many submissions exist in total. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for one service and one reporting period, so it is a delivered set of reported values, not the act of sending nor an application form. Keep it short; the card is about 220 px wide.

analytics.dashboard.cards.mySubmissions.context: Title of the card shown to accounts that only file their own data, counting the submissions that account has filed. First-person possessive, referring to the signed-in account; a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a reporting period.

analytics.dashboard.cards.submitData.context: Title of the card that leads to the form for filing a new submission. 'Submit' means to file or send in reported values, never to surrender or to submit oneself; 'data' is the reported values themselves. It titles a card, so keep the same brevity as the other card titles.

analytics.dashboard.actions.review.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the pending-approvals card, which opens the list of submissions awaiting a decision. Imperative, in the sense of examining them in order to approve or reject; not 'revise' and not a written review.

analytics.dashboard.actions.manage.context: Caption of the link at the foot of several count cards, opening the administration screen for whatever that card counts. Imperative and deliberately generic, because the same word sits under the services, operators, administrators and schemas cards. Very tight on space at the foot of a card.

analytics.dashboard.actions.browse.context: Caption of the link at the foot of the submissions cards, opening the full list so the user can look through it. Imperative, in the sense of leafing through a list; it does not mean to search for something specific, and it has nothing to do with a web browser.

analytics.dashboard.actions.newSubmissio.context: Caption of the link that opens the form for filing a submission that does not exist yet. 'New' modifies the submission being created; keep the trailing arrow, which is decoration signalling navigation and must not be translated or moved before the words.

analytics.dashboard.actions.viewByPeriod.context: Caption of the link beside the missing-submissions heading, which opens the screen that breaks the same figures down one reporting window at a time. 'View' is the imperative verb, and 'by period' means grouped per reporting window. Keep the trailing arrow, which is untranslated decoration signalling navigation.

analytics.dashboard.missing.overdueTitle.context: Heading over the group of cards covering the reporting window that has already ended, where anything still not filed is late. 'Overdue' means the deadline has passed; 'previous period' is the reporting window immediately before the one now in progress. Keep the dash as the separator between the two ideas, and keep it short since it heads a row of cards.

analytics.dashboard.missing.overdueDescr.context: One quiet line under that heading explaining why those cards are marked late: the reporting windows they cover have ended, so nothing more can be filed inside them. 'Closed' is used of a reporting window that has ended, not of a dialog being dismissed.

analytics.dashboard.missing.currentTitle.context: Heading over the group of cards covering the reporting window now in progress. 'This period' means the window containing today, the one still open; 'current' here is about the present time and never about electricity. Keep it short since it heads a row of cards.

analytics.dashboard.missing.currentDescr.context: One quiet line under that heading explaining that nothing is late yet: the reporting window is still open, so the outstanding values can still arrive in time. Reassuring and factual, not a warning.

analytics.dashboard.missing.servicesShor.context: Caption printed directly beneath a large number on a card, completing it. Singular form, used when the number is one. Being short on submissions means the service has not filed every required value the window expects of it; the figure counts one entry per service and schema still incomplete.

joins.after: The large count rendered on the line immediately above it, inside the same card in Dashboard.tsx
joins.note: Has no number of its own, so it must agree with the numeral shown above it; it carries no leading space because it starts its own line, but it must read as the continuation of that numeral.

analytics.dashboard.missing.servicesShor.context: Caption printed directly beneath a large number on a card, completing it. Plural form, used for zero and for two or more. Being short on submissions means the service has not filed every required value the window expects of it; the figure counts one entry per service and schema still incomplete.

joins.after: The large count rendered on the line immediately above it, inside the same card in Dashboard.tsx
joins.note: Has no number of its own, so it must agree with the numeral shown above it; it carries no leading space because it starts its own line, but it must read as the continuation of that numeral.

analytics.dashboard.trend.title.context: Heading above the chart that plots, window after window, how many required values were never filed. 'Over time' means the figure is followed across consecutive reporting windows; 'missing' means expected but not filed.

analytics.dashboard.trend.loading.context: Sits beside a small spinner in the empty chart area while the history is being fetched. Present progressive with the ellipsis kept, and very tight on space: 'trend' means the series of figures over consecutive windows, so shorten or drop that word rather than let the label wrap.

analytics.dashboard.trend.empty.context: Fills the chart area when the chosen frequency and service combination has no windows to plot. A neutral statement that there is nothing to draw, not an error and not a failed request.

analytics.dashboard.trend.seriesName.context: Names the plotted line and appears in the small box that follows the pointer over the chart, above the value for the window under the cursor. 'Missing' is the count of required values not filed. Space is extremely tight and the service name is appended to it, so keep the leading word to a minimum and keep the dash separator rather than adding words.

placeholders.service: Display name of the service the chart is scoped to, or the translation of 'All services' when it is not scoped, e.g. Rossi Plant

analytics.missing.title.context: Heading of the screen that shows, one reporting window at a time, which required values were never filed. 'Missing' means expected but not filed; 'by period' means broken down per reporting window. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a period.

analytics.missing.titleShort.context: Heading of the block of cards on the landing screen that summarises what has not been filed. The shorter counterpart of the full screen heading, so use the same terms minus the breakdown; keep it noticeably shorter than that heading.

analytics.missing.columns.missing.context: Heads a very narrow column whose cells read as a ratio such as 2/5: how many of the required values the window expects are still not filed, out of how many it expects in total. Also used as a spreadsheet column heading. One short word only; 'missing' means expected but not filed.

analytics.missing.columns.totalRequired.context: Heading of a downloaded spreadsheet column holding how many values the window requires from that service and schema in total, the denominator of the missing ratio. 'Required' means the schema marks the value as mandatory, as opposed to optional; 'total' is the whole count expected, not a sum of amounts.

analytics.missing.trend.title.context: Header of the card holding the bar chart of how many required values were never filed in each of the last twelve reporting windows. 'Over time' means across consecutive windows. It shares a narrow card header with nothing else, but the card is only about 360 px wide, so stay brief.

analytics.missing.trend.description.en: Total missing required values per {{cadence}} period · click a bar to inspect it
analytics.missing.trend.description.context: Quiet line under that card header explaining what a bar is worth and how to use the chart: each bar totals the required values not filed in one window of the chosen frequency, and clicking one selects that window for the panels below. Keep the middle dot separating the two statements, and keep it to one line if the language allows.

placeholders.cadence: Name of the selected reporting frequency, already translated and converted to lower case before it is inserted, e.g. monthly

analytics.missing.chart.missing.context: Names the quantity in the small box that follows the pointer over both bar charts, printed after the number, so it reads as '12 missing'. Lower case, no article, and extremely tight on space; it means required values expected but not filed.

analytics.missing.byService.title.context: Header of the card that breaks the same figures down one bar per service for a single reporting window, whose label is appended. 'By service' means grouped per service. Keep the dash as the separator and keep the leading words short, because the window label can be long.

placeholders.period: Label of the selected reporting window, sometimes with a hint in brackets, e.g. 2026-07 (previous); falls back to the translated frequency name such as Monthly

analytics.missing.byService.description.en: Missing required values per service in the selected period
analytics.missing.byService.description.context: Quiet line under that card header saying what a bar measures: how many values the schemas require of that service, in the one selected window, that were never filed. 'Per service' means one bar for each service.

analytics.missing.byService.empty.context: Fills the card when every required value for the selected window has been filed, so there is nothing to chart. Good news rather than an error; keep the celebratory emoji, which needs no translation.

analytics.missing.summary.en: {{missing}} missing required value(s) across {{services}} service(s) in {{period}}
analytics.missing.summary.context: Quiet sentence printed immediately to the right of the same total rendered as a large red number, summarising the selected window: how many required values are not filed, how many services they are spread across, and which window is meant. English marks the optional plural with '(s)' because the sentence is not plural-aware, so choose a form that reads correctly for any count instead of copying the brackets.

placeholders.missing: Whole number of required values not filed in the window, the same figure as the large number beside it, e.g. 17
placeholders.services: Whole number of distinct services those values belong to, e.g. 4
placeholders.period: Label of the selected reporting window, e.g. 2026-07 (previous); when no window is selected the translation of 'the selected period' is inserted instead

analytics.missing.selectedPeriod.context: Vague stand-in used when the reporting window has no label to print, dropped into the same slot of the summary sentence where a window label such as 2026-07 would otherwise go. Lower case, no final full stop, and worded so it follows the preposition that precedes that slot.

joins.after: The word 'in' at the end of analytics.missing.summary, whose {{period}} placeholder it fills, in MissingSubmissionsPage.tsx
joins.example: 17 missing required value(s) across 4 service(s) in the selected period
joins.note: Substituted into another sentence, so it must not start with a capital or end with punctuation; the surrounding sentence supplies both.

analytics.missing.detail.complete.en: All required submissions are in for this period.
analytics.missing.detail.complete.context: Green message bar that replaces the detail table when nothing is outstanding for the selected window. 'All required submissions are in' means every mandatory value has been filed; 'in' here means received, not inside anything. Confirmation rather than a warning.

analytics.explore.title.context: Names the whole ad-hoc analysis screen, where an administrator picks a schema and one of its numeric values and charts it across reporting periods and services. 'Explore' is the free, unguided examination of collected data; render it as the noun your language uses for that activity rather than as a command aimed at the user.

analytics.explore.tabs.scorecard.context: First tab of the Explore screen; opens the red/amber/green board that shows, for every schema and every numeric value, whether each service's figure sits inside the target range an administrator defined. A scorecard here is a board of status indicators, never a sports score or a rating given to a person. Sits in a tab strip beside Analysis and Anomalies, so keep it to one short word if possible.

analytics.explore.tabs.analysis.context: Middle tab of the Explore screen; opens the detailed area where one schema at a time is charted (Trend, Compare services, Snapshot). Names the activity of examining one schema's numbers in depth — not the product area as a whole, and not a report document.

analytics.explore.tabs.anomalies.context: Last tab of the Explore screen; opens the board that flags figures lying far from a service's own recent history. The same wording also captions the button that opens the detector settings above the trend chart, so it has to work both as a tab and as a button. An anomaly is a statistical outlier — an unusually high or low figure — not an error, a fault or a data defect.

analytics.explore.actions.exportCsv.context: Row in the overflow menu of the Explore screen that downloads the numbers currently on screen as a CSV file. The parenthesis restricts the download to the view that is selected right now (Trend, Compare services or Snapshot) with the filters as they stand, rather than the whole data set; keep it as a parenthetical. 'Export' is the imperative of writing data out to a file, and CSV stays untranslated.

analytics.explore.actions.exportPng.context: Row in the same overflow menu that saves the chart currently drawn as an image file. 'Chart' means the graphic itself, so use the word for a plotted diagram; the table form of the same data is downloaded by the CSV command instead. Leave PNG untranslated.

analytics.explore.errors.nothingToExport.en: Nothing to export for this view yet.
analytics.explore.errors.nothingToExport.context: Message bar shown after an export command when the current filters produced no rows to write out. It reports an empty result, not a mistake by the user, and 'yet' implies rows will appear once services have submitted data.

analytics.explore.filters.schemas.context: Labels the multi-select above the anomaly board that chooses which schemas are examined; the same wording also heads the dashboard card counting how many schemas exist. A schema is an admin-defined form definition, so use the product's established plural for it. Short noun phrase in a crowded row of filter labels.

analytics.explore.filters.selectSchema.context: Ghost text in the schema dropdown on the Analysis tab before anything is chosen. Imperative, addressed to the operator; a schema is an admin-defined form definition, and the indefinite article signals that any one of several may be picked.

analytics.explore.filters.allSchemas.context: Stands in the schemas multi-select while no schema is ticked, and states the resulting behaviour: every schema will be examined. A statement of the current selection rather than an instruction, and it must fit inside a closed dropdown roughly 200 pixels wide.

analytics.explore.filters.value.context: Labels the dropdown that chooses which numeric value of the selected schema is charted. 'Value' here names a numeric field declared in the schema, such as Headcount or Temperature — not a particular number a service entered; use the same word the product uses for a schema's values everywhere else.

analytics.explore.filters.selectValue.context: Ghost text in that same dropdown before a numeric field is chosen. Imperative, addressed to the operator, and 'value' keeps the sense of a numeric field defined by the schema rather than a figure submitted for it.

analytics.explore.filters.show.context: Labels the dropdown on the scorecard that decides which submission is read for each service: the most recent one that exists, or one specific reporting period. Shorthand for 'what to display', so a short noun phrase is preferable if the bare verb reads oddly above a dropdown.

analytics.explore.filters.latestAvailabl.context: Option of the Show dropdown that takes each service's most recent submission whatever period it belongs to, so two services may be shown at different periods. 'Latest' means most recent in time and 'available' means whatever exists, however old; the neighbouring option instead pins a single period for everyone.

analytics.explore.filters.lastPeriod.context: Option of the Show dropdown that reads one single reporting period for every service and marks the services that did not submit it. A period is a reporting window such as a week, a month or a quarter, and 'last' means the most recent one, not the final one ever.

analytics.explore.filters.latestClosed.context: Option naming the most recent reporting period that has already ended and been closed to further submissions. 'Closed' means finished and no longer accepting data, not shut down or cancelled; it is the settled counterpart of Current, the option beside it, which is still open.

analytics.explore.filters.current.context: Option naming the reporting period that is in progress right now, whose figures may still change. 'Current' means present or ongoing, never electrical. Elsewhere the same word is lower-cased and appended in brackets after a period label, as in '2026-08 (current)', so it must also read naturally in lower case.

analytics.explore.filters.aggregation.context: Labels the dropdown that chooses the arithmetic used to reduce many submitted samples down to one number per period. Use the established statistical term in your language: it names a computation over numbers, not a written summary or a grouping of items.

analytics.explore.filters.comparePreviou.context: Labels the dropdown that draws the same selection a second time, shifted back in time, over the trend chart. 'Compare with previous' means reading the chosen window against an earlier window of the same length; 'previous' refers to earlier time, not to an earlier version of a record.

analytics.explore.help.schemas.en: Which schemas to scan for anomalies. Leave empty to scan every schema with numeric values.
analytics.explore.help.schemas.context: Hover help for the schemas multi-select on the anomaly board. 'Scan' means examine the submitted figures looking for outliers, and the second sentence tells the operator that an empty selection covers every schema that has at least one numeric value. Keep the imperative of 'Leave empty' and keep the field name identical to the label it explains.

analytics.explore.help.schemasAria.context: Spoken name of the small information icon beside the Schemas filter, phrased as the question the hover help answers. Keep the field name identical to the visible label next to it, and keep it a natural spoken question rather than an abbreviation.

analytics.explore.help.show.en: Latest available shows each service's most recent submission, however old. Last period shows a single period and marks services that didn't submit it as gray “no submission” cards.
analytics.explore.help.show.context: Hover help for the Show dropdown on the scorecard, contrasting its two options: one takes each service's most recent submission however old it is, the other pins a single period and represents the services that did not report it as grey cards. Keep both option names word-for-word identical to the dropdown options, and keep the quoted state matching the 'No submission' label used on those cards.

analytics.explore.help.showAria.context: Spoken name of the information icon beside the Show dropdown, phrased as the question the hover help answers. Keep the field name identical to the visible label next to it.

analytics.explore.help.aggregation.en: How the samples that fall in each period are reduced to one number — and how several services are combined into the overall figure. Average is count-weighted; Sample count just tallies how many were submitted.
analytics.explore.help.aggregation.context: Hover help for the Aggregation dropdown, explaining that the chosen arithmetic does two jobs: it reduces the samples falling inside one period to a single number, and it merges several services into one overall figure. It then says that the average weights each period by how many samples it contains, and that the sample-count option only tallies how many submissions arrived and ignores their size. Keep both option names identical to the dropdown options.

analytics.explore.help.aggregationAria.context: Spoken name of the information icon beside the Aggregation dropdown, phrased as the question the hover help answers. Keep the field name identical to the visible label next to it.

analytics.explore.help.comparePrevious.en: Overlay the same selection shifted back in time so you can read this period against an earlier one. Needs a Period range (not All time); the two windows may overlap.
analytics.explore.help.comparePrevious.context: Hover help for the Compare dropdown: it draws the same selection shifted back in time on top of the current one so the two can be read against each other. It also states the precondition — a bounded period range must be chosen instead of the All time default — and reassures the operator that the two windows are allowed to overlap. 'Period range' and 'All time' name the period filter and its default option, so keep them identical to those controls.

analytics.explore.help.compareAria.context: Spoken name of the information icon beside the comparison dropdown. It uses the short name Compare for the control whose visible label is longer; keep it brief and recognisably the same control.

analytics.explore.shifts.1m.context: Option of the comparison dropdown stating how far back the overlaid window is shifted. The same wording is also interpolated into the chart's series names, where it is followed by a word meaning 'ago', so it must read naturally there too: express it as a plain quantity of time and use whatever singular or plural form your language requires after the numeral.

analytics.explore.shifts.6m.context: Option of the comparison dropdown stating how far back the overlaid window is shifted. The same wording is also interpolated into the chart's series names, where it is followed by a word meaning 'ago', so it must read naturally there too: express it as a plain quantity of time and use whatever plural form your language requires after the numeral.

analytics.explore.shifts.1y.context: Option of the comparison dropdown stating how far back the overlaid window is shifted. The same wording is also interpolated into the chart's series names, where it is followed by a word meaning 'ago', so it must read naturally there too: express it as a plain quantity of time and use whatever singular or plural form your language requires after the numeral.

analytics.explore.views.trend.context: Inner tab of the Analysis area that plots one numeric value period by period as a line chart. 'Trend' is the movement of the figure over time; use the noun, not a verb, and keep it stable because operators switch between these three tabs by habit.

analytics.explore.views.compare.context: Inner tab that ranks the services against one another on a single figure rolled up over the whole selected window. The same wording also heads the card holding that chart. 'Compare' means setting the services side by side; 'services' are the organisational units that submit data.

analytics.explore.views.snapshot.context: Inner tab showing a plain table of the most recent period's figure for every service and every numeric value of the schema. A snapshot is a single point-in-time picture of the current state — not a photograph, and not a saved copy or backup.

analytics.explore.aggregation.average.context: Option of the Aggregation dropdown: the arithmetic mean of the samples, weighted by how many samples each period contributed, as opposed to Sum which adds them, Minimum and Maximum which pick one extreme, and Sample count which ignores their size entirely. Use the same term you use for the mean in the anomaly baseline options so an operator recognises them as one statistic. It is also rendered in lower case inside card captions, so it must read naturally uncapitalised.

analytics.explore.aggregation.sum.context: Option of the Aggregation dropdown: every sample in the period added together, with no division by how many there were. Use the standard arithmetic term for a total; it is the counterpart of Average, which divides by the number of samples. Also rendered in lower case inside card captions.

analytics.explore.aggregation.min.context: Option of the Aggregation dropdown: the smallest sample value in the period. Not the earliest sample, and not a lower limit or threshold that anything is checked against — use the standard statistical word for the least value. Also rendered in lower case inside card captions.

analytics.explore.aggregation.max.context: Option of the Aggregation dropdown: the largest sample value in the period. Not the latest sample, and not an upper limit or capacity — use the standard statistical word for the greatest value, mirroring the wording chosen for Minimum. Also rendered in lower case inside card captions.

analytics.explore.aggregation.count.context: Option of the Aggregation dropdown: how many samples were submitted in the period, disregarding how large they are. A sample is one submitted figure for the chosen value, and 'count' is a noun naming a quantity, not an instruction to count. Also rendered in lower case inside card captions.

analytics.explore.status.green.context: The healthy state on the scorecard: the service's figure falls inside the acceptable or ideal range an administrator set for that value. Appears beside a green dot in the legend and as the hover text of a green card, so keep it to one or two words. 'Target' means that intended range, not a goal to be reached later.

analytics.explore.status.amber.context: The middle state on the scorecard: the figure has left the ideal range but is still inside the acceptable one, so it deserves attention without being a failure. Appears beside an amber dot in the legend and as the hover text of an amber card; one word, and it must sit clearly between the on-target and off-target wordings.

analytics.explore.status.red.context: The failing state on the scorecard: the figure is outside the acceptable range an administrator set for that value. Appears beside a red dot in the legend and as the hover text of a red card. Keep it short and recognisably the exact opposite of the on-target wording, using the same word for 'target'.

analytics.explore.status.normal.context: The healthy state on the anomaly board: the figure is consistent with that service's own recent history, so nothing was flagged. Appears beside a green dot in the legend and as the hover text of a green card. It says that no outlier was found, rather than judging the figure as ordinary or acceptable in quality.

analytics.explore.status.anomaly.context: Heads the very narrow column that marks the flagged periods in the trend table and in the CSV export, and also labels the amber entry in the anomaly board legend. One word: a figure that lies statistically far from the service's own recent history, not an error, a fault or an alarm.

analytics.explore.status.noSubmission.context: The grey state used wherever a service filed nothing for the requested period: in the legend, inside the compact cards, and after a number in the one-line summaries. A submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a period, so this says none exists — not that a value is empty or zero. Must stay short enough for a card roughly 220 pixels wide.

analytics.explore.status.hideMissing.context: Label of the toggle switch that removes the grey no-submission cards from the scorecard and the anomaly board. Imperative 'hide'; 'missing' describes services that have not submitted anything for the period, not data that was lost or damaged. Sits inline beside another switch, so keep it to two short words.

analytics.explore.presets.label.context: Caption of the small button that opens the saved-views menu on the Explore screen. A preset is a stored combination of every filter and setting on the screen, which the operator can reload later; use the plural noun for such saved configurations and keep it short beside a bookmark icon.

analytics.explore.presets.empty.context: Shown inside that menu while the operator has not saved any view yet. States the absence and implies saving is possible; not an error.

analytics.explore.presets.namePrompt.context: Message of the small browser prompt that appears when the operator saves the current view, above the box where the name is typed. Names what has to be entered; keep it a short noun phrase rather than a command, and use the same word for 'preset' as the button that opens the menu.

analytics.explore.presets.limit_one.en: You can keep at most {{count}} preset. Delete one first.
analytics.explore.presets.limit_one.context: Browser alert refusing to store another saved view because the fixed maximum has been reached, telling the operator to remove one first. Full sentences addressed to the operator; the singular form here is only used by languages that inflect for exactly one.

placeholders.count: The maximum number of saved views the browser keeps, a fixed small number, currently 5

analytics.explore.presets.limit_other.en: You can keep at most {{count}} presets. Delete one first.
analytics.explore.presets.limit_other.context: Browser alert refusing to store another saved view because the fixed maximum has been reached, telling the operator to remove one first. Full sentences addressed to the operator; this is the plural form, and the second sentence is an instruction meaning 'delete one of the existing ones'.

placeholders.count: The maximum number of saved views the browser keeps, a fixed small number, currently 5

analytics.explore.presets.deleteAria.context: Spoken name of the small bin button beside each saved view in the menu; the deletion happens immediately, with no confirmation step. Describe the action on that named view rather than the icon.

placeholders.name: The name the operator typed when saving the view, e.g. Weekly headcount

analytics.explore.presets.saveCurrent.context: Last row of the saved-views menu: it stores the filters and settings as they stand under a name the operator then types. 'Save' means store, never the sense of economising, and 'current' means as things are right now. Keep the trailing ellipsis, which signals that a prompt for the name follows.

analytics.explore.anomaly.historyWindow.context: Labels the dropdown choosing how many earlier reporting periods are used as the baseline the detector measures against. 'Window' is a span of consecutive periods, not a window on screen, and the parenthesis states the unit in which the number is expressed. Sits above a narrow dropdown in a row of filters.

analytics.explore.anomaly.sensitivity.context: Labels the dropdown choosing how far a figure has to sit from the baseline before it is flagged; a lower setting flags more figures. Leave the notation in brackets exactly as it is — it is the mathematical symbol for the absolute standardised distance from the baseline — and translate only the word before it.

analytics.explore.anomaly.baselineMode.context: Labels the dropdown choosing how the comparison baseline is calculated from the recent history. 'Baseline' is the expected level derived from earlier periods; 'mode' is a method setting chosen by the operator, not a state the system is in.

analytics.explore.anomaly.robustHelp.en: Robust mode resists a few extreme spikes skewing the baseline. Standard mode uses the mean and standard deviation.
analytics.explore.anomaly.robustHelp.context: Hover help for the Baseline mode dropdown, contrasting its two options: one is barely moved by a few extreme spikes, the other is built from the arithmetic mean and the standard deviation. Keep both option names identical to the dropdown options, and use the standard statistical terms for mean and standard deviation so they match the aggregation wording.

analytics.explore.anomaly.robustAria.context: Spoken name of the information icon beside the Baseline mode dropdown, phrased as a question about its outlier-resistant option. Keep the option name identical to the dropdown option it refers to.

analytics.explore.anomaly.robust.context: Option of the Baseline mode dropdown: the baseline is built from the median and the median absolute deviation, so a handful of extreme spikes hardly shift it. Translate the leading word in the sense of resistant to outliers; keep the two statistical names in brackets, using the standard term for the median and leaving the established abbreviation as it is.

analytics.explore.anomaly.standard.context: Option of the Baseline mode dropdown: the baseline is built from the arithmetic mean and the standard deviation — the same statistic the Average aggregation computes. The leading word means the ordinary, default method rather than a norm or a specification; keep the abbreviation in brackets as the usual short form for standard deviation in your language.

analytics.explore.anomaly.detection.context: Heading at the top of the small panel above the trend chart that holds the highlight switch and the detector settings. Names the process of finding statistical outliers in the plotted figures; noun phrase, no verb.

analytics.explore.anomaly.highlight.context: Label of the switch that turns outlier marking on for the trend chart: flagged points are drawn with a ring around them. Imperative 'highlight', in the sense of marking something visually so it stands out; it changes only how the chart is drawn, it does not alter the data.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryAnomaly.context: One item of the one-line tally shown on a collapsed schema card on the anomaly board, counting how many service figures were flagged as statistical outliers. Singular form, used only by languages that inflect for exactly one; no full stop, because further items may follow.

placeholders.count: How many figures were flagged for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Items whose count is zero are left out, so this one may appear first, last or alone. Keep the wording matching the Anomaly state label used in the legend.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryAnomaly.context: One item of the one-line tally shown on a collapsed schema card on the anomaly board, counting how many service figures were flagged as statistical outliers. Plural form; no full stop, because further items may follow.

placeholders.count: How many figures were flagged for this schema, a whole number, e.g. 2

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Items whose count is zero are left out, so this one may appear first, last or alone. Keep the wording matching the Anomaly state label used in the legend.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryNormal_.context: One item of the same tally, counting the service figures that sit within their own recent history and were therefore not flagged. English uses the same wording for one and many, but use whichever singular form your language requires; no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many figures were not flagged for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Keep the wording recognisably the same state as the green 'No anomalies' legend entry, shortened to fit one line.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryNormal_.context: One item of the same tally, counting the service figures that sit within their own recent history and were therefore not flagged. Plural form; no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many figures were not flagged for this schema, a whole number, e.g. 5

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Keep the wording recognisably the same state as the green 'No anomalies' legend entry, shortened to fit one line.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryMissing.context: One item of the same tally, counting the services that filed nothing at all for the period being examined. Singular form; keep the wording identical to the grey 'No submission' state used in the legend and on the cards, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many services did not submit for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. This item is always last when it appears, but it can also stand alone.

analytics.explore.anomaly.summaryMissing.context: One item of the same tally, counting the services that filed nothing at all for the period being examined. Plural form; keep the wording identical to the grey 'No submission' state used in the legend and on the cards, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many services did not submit for this schema, a whole number, e.g. 3

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. This item is always last when it appears, but it can also stand alone.

analytics.explore.anomaly.empty.en: No numeric KPIs to scan yet. Pick one or more schemas with numeric values to check the latest period for anomalies.
analytics.explore.anomaly.empty.context: Fills the anomaly board when no schema in scope has any numeric value to examine. The second sentence tells the operator what to select instead; 'numeric KPIs' means the numeric values declared in a schema, and 'scan' means examine them for outliers. Not an error.

analytics.explore.anomaly.hideNormal.context: Label of the toggle switch that removes the cards which were not flagged, leaving only the outliers and, unless the neighbouring switch is on, the services that did not submit. Imperative 'hide'; 'normal' means not flagged as an outlier, and should match the wording of the green state in the legend. Two short words, inline beside another switch.

analytics.explore.anomaly.noneInPeriod.context: Replaces the anomaly board when the data loaded fine but the active filters leave nothing to show. Reports a clean result rather than an error, and names the reporting period that was examined.

placeholders.period: The chosen period option, already translated and converted to lower case, e.g. current or latest closed

analytics.explore.anomaly.openAnalysis.context: Hover text of a card on the anomaly board; clicking it opens the detailed chart for that service and value with outlier marking already switched on. Keep the tab name identical to the Analysis tab it refers to, and keep the middle dot separator that precedes the current state.

placeholders.state: The card's own state label, already translated, one of the anomaly board states, e.g. Anomaly or No anomalies

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryOnTar.context: One item of the one-line tally shown on a collapsed schema card on the scorecard, counting the service figures that fall inside their acceptable range. Singular form, used only by languages that inflect for exactly one; no full stop, because further items may follow.

placeholders.count: How many figures are within range for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, since this item is always the first one shown when it appears
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Keep the wording identical to the green 'On target' state used in the legend.

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryOnTar.context: One item of the one-line tally shown on a collapsed schema card on the scorecard, counting the service figures that fall inside their acceptable range. Plural form; no full stop, because further items may follow.

placeholders.count: How many figures are within range for this schema, a whole number, e.g. 3

joins.after: Nothing, since this item is always the first one shown when it appears
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Keep the wording identical to the green 'On target' state used in the legend.

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryWarni.context: One item of the same tally, counting the figures that have left the ideal range but are still inside the acceptable one. Singular form; keep the wording identical to the amber state in the legend, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many figures are in the amber middle state for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Items whose count is zero are left out, so this one may appear first or alone.

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryOffTa.context: One item of the same tally, counting the figures that fall outside the acceptable range altogether. Singular form; keep the wording identical to the red 'Off target' state in the legend, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many figures are outside the acceptable range for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. Items whose count is zero are left out, so this one may appear first or alone.

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryMissi.context: One item of the same tally, counting the services that filed nothing for the period the scorecard is reading. Singular form; keep the wording identical to the grey 'No submission' state used in the legend and on the cards, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many services did not submit for this schema, a whole number, here always 1

joins.after: Nothing, or the middle dot separator that follows an earlier tally item
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. This item is always last when it appears, but it can also stand alone.

analytics.explore.scorecard.summaryMissi.context: One item of the same tally, counting the services that filed nothing for the period the scorecard is reading. Plural form; keep the wording identical to the grey 'No submission' state used in the legend and on the cards, and add no full stop.

placeholders.count: How many services did not submit for this schema, a whole number, e.g. 2
