joins.note: The separator ' · ' is added by the code between items, so add no leading or trailing space and no punctuation of your own. This item is always last when it appears, but it can also stand alone.

analytics.explore.scorecard.empty.en: No KPIs with a target band yet. Add an acceptable/ideal range to a numeric schema value to see it here.
analytics.explore.scorecard.empty.context: Fills the scorecard when no numeric value anywhere has a target range defined, so there is nothing to judge as good or bad. The second sentence tells the administrator what to add to a schema's numeric value; 'acceptable/ideal range' names the two nested bands configured there, and 'target band' means the same thing. Not an error.

analytics.explore.scorecard.hideOnTarget.context: Label of the toggle switch that removes the healthy cards from the scorecard so only the ones needing attention remain. Imperative 'hide'; keep the state wording identical to the green 'On target' label, hyphenated or not as your language prefers. Two or three short words, inline beside another switch.

analytics.explore.scorecard.allOnTarget.context: Replaces the scorecard when the hide switches leave nothing to show because every figure is inside its acceptable range. A reassuring statement of a clean result, not an error; 'KPI' means one numeric value being tracked, and the wording for being on target should match the green state label.

analytics.explore.scorecard.asOf.context: Dates the figure shown on a scorecard card: it says which reporting period the number belongs to. 'as of' marks the point in time a value was true.

joins.before: The figure and its unit, followed by a middle dot separator added by the code
joins.after: Nothing; this ends the small grey line under the service name
joins.note: Keep the self-closing <periodDate /> tag exactly as written and do not put anything inside it: it is replaced at runtime by the period's start date, formatted for the reader's locale. You may move the tag if your language needs the date in a different position, but the words around it must stay outside it. The line sits inside a card about 220 pixels wide, so keep it very short.

analytics.explore.scorecard.viewSubmissi.context: Hover text of a scorecard card that links to the submission behind the figure; a submission is one filled-in instance of a schema for a service and a period. 'View' is the imperative of opening something to read it, not of watching. Keep the middle dot separator that precedes the current state.

placeholders.state: The card's own state label, already translated, one of the scorecard states, e.g. On target or No submission

analytics.explore.content.pickSchema.en: Pick a schema to start exploring.
analytics.explore.content.pickSchema.context: Fills the Analysis area before any schema has been chosen, telling the operator that choosing one is the first step. Imperative addressed to the operator; a schema is an admin-defined form definition, and 'exploring' echoes the name of this screen.

analytics.explore.content.noNumeric.en: This schema has no numeric values, so there's nothing to chart. Add a Number or Integer value to explore it.
analytics.explore.content.noNumeric.context: Information bar shown in place of the chart when the chosen schema declares no numeric value, so nothing can be plotted. The second sentence tells the administrator to add one, and Number and Integer are the names of two schema value types as they appear when defining a schema — keep them identical to those type names. 'Chart' is used as a verb here, meaning to plot on a graph.

analytics.explore.content.trendOverTime.context: Heading of the card holding the line chart on the Trend tab. Noun phrase naming what the chart shows: how the chosen figure moves from one reporting period to the next.

analytics.explore.content.aggregationOf.context: One-line description under the chart's heading, stating which arithmetic is applied to which numeric value. A short fragment beginning with a middle dot may be appended after it, so do not close it with a full stop.

placeholders.aggregation: The chosen aggregation name, already translated and capitalised as in the dropdown, e.g. Average or Sample count
placeholders.value: The numeric value's display name, with its unit in brackets when it has one, e.g. Headcount (people)

analytics.explore.content.perCadencePeri.context: Completes the chart's description by stating how long each plotted period lasts. 'per' distributes the figure over each period, and a period is one reporting window.

placeholders.cadence: The schema's reporting frequency, already translated and converted to lower case, e.g. weekly, monthly or quarterly

joins.before: The description of the aggregation and value, plus a middle dot separator added by the code
joins.example: Average of Headcount (people) · per monthly period
joins.note: The separator and the surrounding spaces are added by the code, so add none yourself, and end without a full stop. If your language cannot place a frequency word before the noun, rephrase within this fragment only.

analytics.explore.content.combineService.context: Label of the switch that merges every selected service into one line on the chart instead of drawing a line per service. 'Combine' means aggregating them into a single series using the chosen aggregation, not comparing them; the Compare services tab is the separate place where they are set side by side.

analytics.explore.content.projection.context: Label of the switch that extends each line a couple of periods into the future as a dashed forecast fitted to the existing points. A projection here is a statistical forecast of where the figure is heading — not an image being projected, and not a budget plan. One word, inline in a row of switches.

analytics.explore.content.viewAsTable.context: Label of the switch that replaces the chart with a table of the same numbers, one row per period. 'View' is used in the sense of displaying it in another form; keep it short, since it sits inline among several switches.

analytics.explore.content.showEvents.context: Label of the switch that overlays administrator-recorded events on the chart as vertical markers and shaded bands. An event is a noted occurrence, such as an outage or a policy change, that may explain a movement in the figures; it is not a calendar appointment. Two short words, inline in a row of switches.

analytics.explore.content.noSamples.context: Shown in place of the chart or the snapshot table when the current combination of schema, value, services and period range returns nothing. A sample is one submitted figure for the chosen value; the sentence says none matched, which is not an error.

analytics.explore.content.overallAggrega.context: Caption of the first small statistics card above the chart, whose big number is the chosen arithmetic applied across the whole selected range rather than to a single period. 'Overall' means for everything currently in scope, all periods and all services together. The card is only about 120 pixels wide, so keep it to two or three words.

placeholders.aggregation: The chosen aggregation name, already translated and converted to lower case, e.g. average or sample count

analytics.explore.content.latestPeriod.context: Caption of the statistics card whose big number is the figure for the most recent reporting period on the chart. 'Latest' means most recent in time, and a period is one reporting window. The card is only about 120 pixels wide, so keep it very short.

analytics.explore.content.samples.context: Caption of the statistics card whose big number is how many individual submitted figures lie behind the chart. A sample is one submitted figure for the chosen value, so this counts data points, not services or periods. One short plural noun; the card is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.explore.content.periodsService.context: Caption of the statistics card whose value is two numbers separated by a slash: how many reporting periods are plotted and how many services are in scope. Keep the slash and the same order of the two nouns as the numbers below them; both are plural, and the card is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.explore.trend.noAnomalies.en: No anomalies in the current selection.
analytics.explore.trend.noAnomalies.context: Small grey line above the chart, shown while outlier marking is on and nothing in the current selection was flagged. 'Selection' means the filters as they stand — schema, value, services and period range.

analytics.explore.trend.anomaliesHighlig.en: {{count}} anomaly highlighted in the current selection.
analytics.explore.trend.anomaliesHighlig.context: Small grey line above the chart, shown while outlier marking is on, reporting how many plotted points are ringed. Singular form, used only by languages that inflect for exactly one; 'highlighted' means visually marked on the chart, and 'selection' means the filters as they stand.

placeholders.count: How many plotted points were flagged as outliers, a whole number, here always 1

analytics.explore.trend.anomaliesHighlig.en: {{count}} anomalies highlighted in the current selection.
analytics.explore.trend.anomaliesHighlig.context: Small grey line above the chart, shown while outlier marking is on, reporting how many plotted points are ringed. Plural form; 'highlighted' means visually marked on the chart, and 'selection' means the filters as they stand.

placeholders.count: How many plotted points were flagged as outliers, a whole number, e.g. 4

analytics.explore.trend.ago.context: Marks the dashed comparison line on the chart as the same data from that much earlier. 'ago' measures backwards from the period range on screen.

placeholders.period: The chosen shift, already translated, e.g. 1 month, 6 months or 1 year

joins.before: The name of the line — a service name, or the label meaning all services combined — plus an opening bracket
joins.after: A closing bracket
joins.note: The brackets and the space before them are added by the code, so do not add them yourself and do not add a leading space. This ends up in the chart legend and tooltip, where space is extremely tight, so abbreviate rather than let it wrap.

analytics.explore.trend.previous.context: Marks the dashed comparison line on the chart as the earlier of the two windows, used when the shift is not named explicitly. 'Previous' means the immediately preceding time window, never an earlier version of a record.

joins.before: The name of the line — a service name, or the label meaning all services combined — plus an opening bracket
joins.after: A closing bracket
joins.note: The brackets are added by the code, so do not add them yourself. Elsewhere the same word is converted to lower case and appended after a period label, as in '2026-07 (previous)', so it must also read naturally in lower case. Space in the chart legend is extremely tight; one short word.

analytics.explore.trend.projectionName.context: Names the dashed forecast line in the chart's tooltip, distinguishing it from the solid line of real figures with the same name. Keep the bracketed word matching the Projection switch, in the sense of a statistical forecast; space is extremely tight, so abbreviate rather than let it wrap.

placeholders.name: The name of the line the forecast extends: a service name, or the label meaning all services combined, e.g. North Plant

analytics.explore.trend.overallTrend.context: Legend entry for the single straight dashed line that shows the direction of travel of all the plotted services taken together, drawn alongside the per-service forecasts. 'Overall' means everything in scope combined, and 'trend' is the direction the figures are moving in. Legend space is extremely tight; abbreviate rather than wrap.

analytics.explore.snapshot.title.context: Heading of the card holding the Snapshot table, which gives one row per service and one column per numeric value of the schema. 'Latest' means most recent in time, 'value' means a numeric field declared in the schema, and 'per service' means one entry for each reporting unit.

analytics.explore.snapshot.description.en: Most recent period per value · cells show the {{aggregation}} for that period
analytics.explore.snapshot.description.context: One-line description under that heading: each column shows its own most recent reporting period, and each cell holds the chosen arithmetic applied to that period's samples. Keep the middle dot separator between the two statements and do not end with a full stop; 'value' means a numeric field of the schema, and 'cells' are the table's individual boxes.

placeholders.aggregation: The chosen aggregation name, already translated and converted to lower case, e.g. average or sample count

analytics.events.title.context: Heading of the screen listing the timeline annotations administrators record so that later readings of the charts can be explained: maintenance windows, incidents, deployments. An event here is such a recorded occurrence, never a social occasion and never a software or user-interface event.

analytics.events.singular.context: Heading of the side panel that shows one recorded occurrence in read-only form, used only when that record has no name of its own to show instead. Singular noun naming the kind of object on display.

analytics.events.ongoing.context: Value in the duration column, and in the duration field of the read-only panel, for a recorded occurrence that has no known end and is still in effect. The column is only 110 px wide and never wraps, so one short word; it describes something still running, not something being processed.

analytics.events.removed.context: Stands in for the name of an affected service whose account no longer exists, inside the comma-separated list of services an occurrence applies to. Past participle meaning the account was deleted from the system. Keep it bracketed and very short, because the list is truncated to one line.

joins.after: Other service names in the comma-separated list built by serviceSummary in EventsPage.tsx; it can appear first, last or between two names
joins.note: The comma and space between items are added by the code, so the string itself carries no leading or trailing space; use the bracket characters the language normally uses for an aside.

analytics.events.notApplicable.context: Ghost text in the greyed-out duration field, shown when the selected kind of occurrence cannot have a duration at all. It says the field is meaningless here, not that it is empty or optional; keep it short enough for a half-width field.

analytics.events.durationHours_one.context: Whole hours of an occurrence's length, in the abbreviated form used inside a 110 px column that never wraps. Singular form, for exactly one hour. Use the shortest conventional abbreviation for hours in the language, with no space between the number and the unit if that is idiomatic.

placeholders.count: Whole number of hours, already rounded down from the total minutes, e.g. 2

joins.before: The minutes part of the same duration, when there is one, in durationSummary in EventsPage.tsx
joins.note: The single space between the hours and the minutes parts is added by the code; this string must not add one of its own on either side.

analytics.events.durationHours_other.context: Whole hours of an occurrence's length, in the abbreviated form used inside a 110 px column that never wraps. Plural form. Use the shortest conventional abbreviation for hours in the language, with no space between the number and the unit if that is idiomatic.

placeholders.count: Whole number of hours, already rounded down from the total minutes, e.g. 27

joins.before: The minutes part of the same duration, when there is one, in durationSummary in EventsPage.tsx
joins.note: The single space between the hours and the minutes parts is added by the code; this string must not add one of its own on either side.

analytics.events.durationMinutes_one.context: Leftover minutes of an occurrence's length, in the abbreviated form used inside a 110 px column that never wraps. Singular form, for exactly one minute. Use the shortest conventional abbreviation for minutes in the language, and keep it distinct from the abbreviation chosen for hours.

placeholders.count: Whole number of minutes left over after the hours have been taken out, e.g. 1

joins.after: The hours part of the same duration, when there is one, in durationSummary in EventsPage.tsx
joins.note: The single space between the hours and the minutes parts is added by the code; this string must not add one of its own on either side. It can also stand alone when the duration is under an hour.

analytics.events.durationMinutes_other.context: Leftover minutes of an occurrence's length, in the abbreviated form used inside a 110 px column that never wraps. Plural form, also used for zero when a recorded length rounds down to nothing. Use the shortest conventional abbreviation for minutes in the language, and keep it distinct from the abbreviation chosen for hours.

placeholders.count: Whole number of minutes left over after the hours have been taken out, and 0 when the whole duration rounds to nothing, e.g. 45

joins.after: The hours part of the same duration, when there is one, in durationSummary in EventsPage.tsx
joins.note: The single space between the hours and the minutes parts is added by the code; this string must not add one of its own on either side. It can also stand alone when the duration is under an hour.

analytics.events.kinds.pointintime.context: One of three kinds of recorded occurrence, offered in a picker and shown back in the read-only panel: something that happened at a single instant and therefore has no length. Also names one colour in the legend of the event markers drawn on trend charts, so keep it short.

analytics.events.kinds.interval.context: One of three kinds of recorded occurrence: something that started at its recorded moment and lasted a known length of time, which the user must then enter. 'Interval' means a span of time between two moments, not a pause, a break or a musical interval. Also names one colour in the legend of the event markers drawn on trend charts, so keep it short.

analytics.events.kinds.fromnowon.context: One of three kinds of recorded occurrence: something that starts at its recorded moment and stays in effect indefinitely, with no end recorded. 'Now' refers to that recorded moment, not to the moment the reader is looking at the screen. Also names one colour in the legend of the event markers drawn on trend charts, so keep it short.

analytics.events.fields.label.context: Labels the required field holding the short name the user gives a recorded occurrence, and heads the corresponding grid and spreadsheet column. A label here is a name for display, not a sticker and not a classification.

analytics.events.fields.timestamp.context: Labels the required date-and-time field for the moment the occurrence happened, and heads the corresponding grid and spreadsheet column. It is the moment being recorded, not the moment the record was saved, and it carries both a date and a time.

analytics.events.fields.kind.context: Labels the required picker that chooses between the three shapes an occurrence can take: a single instant, a span of known length, or something continuing indefinitely. 'Kind' means type or category; keep it short, since it shares a row with the duration field.

analytics.events.fields.duration.context: Labels the field holding how long the occurrence lasted, and heads a grid column only 110 px wide. It is a length of time, not a deadline or a validity period; keep it short for the sake of that column.

analytics.events.fields.description.context: Labels the optional multi-line field for free text explaining the occurrence in more detail, and heads the corresponding grid and spreadsheet column. A noun naming the text itself, not an instruction to describe something.

analytics.events.fields.affects.context: Labels the control that picks which services the occurrence applies to, and heads the corresponding grid column. It is the third-person verb 'it affects', so a noun phrase such as 'affected services' is usually the better label; a service is an organisational unit that submits data. Nothing to do with emotion.

analytics.events.fields.created.context: Labels the date and time the record itself was first saved, in the audit block of the read-only panel and as a spreadsheet column heading. It refers to the creation of the record, not to when the occurrence happened, which has its own field. A past participle used as a label, so a noun phrase may read better.

analytics.events.fields.createdBy.context: Heading of a downloaded spreadsheet column holding which account first saved the record. 'By' attributes the action to a person, so the natural rendering is 'created by whom'; it refers to the record, not to the occurrence it describes.

analytics.events.fields.modified.context: Labels the date and time the record was last changed, in the audit block of the read-only panel. It refers to a change to the record, not to a change in the occurrence; a past participle used as a label, so a noun phrase may read better. It sits beside the creation label, so keep the two visibly parallel.

analytics.events.actions.add.context: Primary toolbar button that opens an empty form for recording a new occurrence, and the heading of that form's panel while it is open. Imperative, in the sense of creating a new record. Because it doubles as a heading, avoid a form that only works as a command.

analytics.events.actions.edit.context: Heading of the side panel when an existing recorded occurrence is open for changes, as opposed to a new one being created. It reads as a command in English but only ever appears as a heading, so a noun phrase such as 'editing an event' is often the better choice.

analytics.events.validation.labelRequire.context: Shown in a red bar at the foot of the form when the user tries to save without giving the occurrence a name. States the rule about the field named by the label field label; keep the two wordings consistent.

analytics.events.validation.timestampReq.context: Shown in a red bar at the foot of the form when the user tries to save without a date and time for the occurrence. States the rule about the field named by the timestamp field label; keep the two wordings consistent.

analytics.events.validation.serviceRequi.en: Pick at least one affected service, or choose “All services”.
analytics.events.validation.serviceRequi.context: Shown when the user has switched off the every-services tick box but has not picked any service, so the form does not know what the occurrence applies to. The quoted words are the tick box's own caption and must be translated exactly as that caption is, with the typographic quotation marks kept or replaced by the language's own quoting convention.

analytics.events.validation.durationForm.en: Duration format not recognized. Use minutes (45), hours:minutes (1:30), or days hours:minutes (2 03:15).
analytics.events.validation.durationForm.context: Shown when the text typed into the duration field matches none of the three accepted shapes, and lists them. Leave the examples exactly as they are: the digits, the colon and the space between the day count and the clock time are the literal syntax the field accepts, so only the words minutes, hours and days are translated.

analytics.events.validation.durationRequ.en: Duration is required for interval events.
analytics.events.validation.durationRequ.context: Shown when the chosen kind is the one with a known length but no length has been entered. Name that kind exactly as its picker option is named, so the user can see which choice is imposing the rule.

analytics.events.help.fromNowOn.en: Runs from the timestamp above until further notice.
analytics.events.help.fromNowOn.context: Quiet explanation under the kind picker, shown only while the open-ended kind is selected: the occurrence is in effect from the date and time entered in the field above it and has no recorded end. 'Runs' means remains in effect over time, not executes; 'until further notice' means for an indefinite period.

analytics.events.help.duration.context: Quiet explanation under the duration field listing the three shapes it accepts. Leave the examples exactly as they are, including the colon and the space between the day count and the clock time; only the words minutes, hours and days are translated. It must stay compact, because it sits under a half-width field.

analytics.events.placeholders.duration.context: Ghost text in the empty duration field showing two of the accepted shapes: a plain minute count, or hours and minutes separated by a colon. Keep the figures and the colon exactly; translate only the 'for example' abbreviation and the conjunction.

analytics.events.placeholders.selectServ.context: Ghost text in the empty multiple-choice picker of services the occurrence applies to. A short prompt to make a choice; a service is an organisational unit that submits data.

analytics.events.deleteConfirm.en:
Delete event "{{label}}"?

This cannot be undone.
analytics.events.deleteConfirm.context: Text of the browser's own confirmation box shown before a recorded occurrence is deleted for good. Keep the blank line between the question and the warning: the two line breaks are what separates them in that plain box. Keep the quotation marks around the name, and state plainly that the deletion cannot be reversed.

placeholders.label: Name of the occurrence about to be deleted, exactly as the user typed it, e.g. Network maintenance

analytics.events.empty.context: Fills the width of the grid when no occurrences have been recorded yet, for readers who are not allowed to record any. 'Yet' matters: it says the list is merely still empty, not that anything failed.

analytics.events.emptyManage.en: No events yet — click “Add event” to create one.
analytics.events.emptyManage.context: Shown instead of the plain empty message to readers who are allowed to record occurrences, pointing them at the button that does it. The quoted words are that button's own caption and must match its translation exactly, with the typographic quotation marks kept or replaced by the language's own quoting convention.

analytics.events.viewAria.context: Announced by screen readers for a whole grid row, which can be activated to open the occurrence's details. Name the action first so the listener knows the row is clickable; never abbreviate, because it is read aloud.

placeholders.label: Name of the occurrence in that row, as the user typed it, e.g. Network maintenance

analytics.events.actionsAria.context: Announced by screen readers for the three-dot button at the end of a grid row, which opens that row's menu of commands. 'Actions' are the operations available on the row; never abbreviate, because it is read aloud.

placeholders.label: Name of the occurrence in that row, as the user typed it, e.g. Network maintenance

analytics.events.byActor.context: Attributes a saved change to the account that made it, printed after the date and time of that change in the audit block of the read-only panel. 'By' means performed by, so it needs whatever case or preposition the language uses for the agent.

placeholders.actor: Name of the account that created or last changed the record, e.g. A. Rossi

joins.after: A rendered date and time followed by a middle dot, added by the code in EventViewBody in EventsPage.tsx
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is supplied by the code, so this string must not add a leading space or dot of its own.

analytics.audit.title.context: Names the screen holding the trail of recorded changes — who changed what, when — together with the outgoing email and webhook logs. The same word also heads the small block of created-and-modified details on the event screen. Use the established term for an audit trail of administrative actions, not for a financial audit.

analytics.audit.email.context: Spoken by screen readers, before a middle dot and the delivery state, to say what kind of record the row's coloured initials stand for. Never visible on screen; one word naming an email message as an object, not the act of sending one.

analytics.audit.delivery.context: Spoken by screen readers, before a middle dot and the delivery state, to say what kind of record the row's coloured initials stand for. Never visible on screen; it names one attempt to hand a webhook notification to an external address, so use a noun about delivering a message rather than about goods.

analytics.audit.actionError.context: Heading of the red bar shown when a command triggered from this screen failed; the technical reason is printed underneath it. 'Action' means the command the operator just invoked, such as sending queued messages or re-sending one. States the failure plainly without blaming the operator or promising a retry.

analytics.audit.deliveryActionsAria.context: Spoken name of the three-dot menu button at the end of a webhook delivery row, which holds that row's commands. Describe it as the actions available for that record rather than describing the icon.

placeholders.id: The delivery record's internal identifier, a long opaque string, e.g. 8f1c2a5e-…

analytics.audit.tabs.changes.context: First tab of the Audit screen; opens the log of recorded modifications, one row per change. Plural noun naming the modifications themselves, not the act of changing something. Sits in a tab strip, so keep it short and stable.

analytics.audit.tabs.sentEmails.context: Tab opening the log of email messages the system produced, including those still queued or failed despite the wording. Short plural noun phrase; 'sent' describes the outgoing direction of the mail rather than guaranteeing every row succeeded.

analytics.audit.tabs.webhookDeliveries.context: Tab opening the log of webhook calls, one row per attempt to hand a notification to an external address. A webhook is an automatic HTTP call to a URL an administrator configured, and the term is normally left untranslated; a delivery is one such attempt. Keep it short — it shares a tab strip with two other tabs.

analytics.audit.actions.sendPending.context: Row in the overflow menu that immediately attempts every queued message instead of waiting for the background sender. 'Pending' means the records whose state is the queued one, so keep it consistent with that state label, and 'now' stresses that the attempt happens straight away. Imperative.

analytics.audit.actions.redeliver.context: Command in a webhook delivery row's own menu that attempts the same notification again, whatever its current state. Imperative built on the noun used for a delivery attempt, meaning to send it once more; it does not create a new notification.

analytics.audit.filters.changeType.context: Labels the dropdown that narrows the log to one kind of recorded modification, such as creations or deletions. 'Type' means category or kind here; keep the noun consistent with the Change column it filters.

analytics.audit.filters.targetType.context: Heads the column naming what kind of object each recorded change was made to, and also labels the dropdown that filters by it. The target is the object acted upon — a schema, a submission, an account and so on — never a goal or a quota. The column is only about 120 pixels wide, so it must stay very short in both places.

analytics.audit.columns.created.context: Heads the column holding the moment the message or delivery record was first queued, and is reused as a CSV export heading. Past participle used as a short label for the creation time; distinct from the Sent and Delivered columns, which record when it actually left.

analytics.audit.columns.to.context: Heads the column naming the person the email was addressed to, showing the display name with the address on hover. It is the recipient field of an email, so use the wording your locale's mail clients use for the addressee. Extremely short label above data that is truncated to fit.

analytics.audit.columns.subject.context: Heads the column showing the email's subject line. Use the mail-specific term for the subject of a message, not the sense of a topic of study or a person under discussion. Very short label above truncated text.

analytics.audit.columns.status.context: Heads the column holding the current state of each email or webhook delivery, and also labels the dropdown that filters by that state. One short noun; the column is only about 110 pixels wide and holds a badge, so keep it as tight as the state labels themselves.

analytics.audit.columns.attempts.context: Heads the narrow numeric column counting how many times sending has been tried for that record, successful or not. Plural noun naming the tries themselves; the column is only about 90 pixels wide, so abbreviate rather than let it wrap.

analytics.audit.columns.sent.context: Heads the column holding the moment the email actually left the system, which stays empty while it is still queued or has failed. Past participle used as a short label for that time; distinct from Created, which is when it was queued.

analytics.audit.columns.event.context: Heads the column naming which occurrence triggered the webhook call. The values below are technical identifiers shown in a monospaced font and are never translated; only the heading is. Very short noun.

analytics.audit.columns.url.context: Heads the column holding the external address the webhook was sent to. Leave the abbreviation as it is unless your locale has an established equivalent; the addresses below are shown in a monospaced font and truncated.

analytics.audit.columns.delivered.context: Heads the column holding the moment the external address accepted the webhook call, which stays empty while it is queued or failing. Past participle used as a short label for that time; the webhook counterpart of the email log's Sent column.

analytics.audit.columns.lastStatusCode.context: Heading of a CSV export column holding the numeric HTTP response returned by the most recent attempt, such as 200 or 503. 'Last' means most recent, not final; 'status code' is the standard HTTP term for that number, so keep it recognisable to an administrator reading the export.

analytics.audit.columns.lastError.context: Heading of a CSV export column holding the failure message from the most recent attempt, which is also shown when hovering a failed badge in the grid. 'Last' means most recent, not final; 'error' is the technical failure reason, not a mistake made by a person.

analytics.audit.columns.timestamp.context: Heads the first column of the change log, holding the date and time the change was recorded, shown in the reader's own time zone. Use the established word for a recorded point in time; the column is about 210 pixels wide and also carries a small avatar.

analytics.audit.columns.change.context: Heads the column holding a badge naming what kind of modification was recorded — a creation, an edit, a deletion, an approval or a rejection. Noun naming the modification itself, not a verb; the column is only about 100 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.columns.target.context: Heads the column naming the specific object the change was made to, by its display name when there is one and by its raw identifier otherwise. The target is the object acted upon, never a goal or a quota; keep it consistent with the Target type heading beside it. Very short label above truncated text.

analytics.audit.columns.changedBy.context: Heads the column naming the account that performed the change, by display name or by raw identifier. 'By' attributes the action to whoever carried it out; a short label such as an equivalent of 'author' or 'performed by' works if a literal rendering is too long for the column.

analytics.audit.columns.note.context: Heads the last column of the change log, holding the optional free-text remark saved with the change — a rejection reason, for instance — or a dash when there is none. One short noun for a written comment; the text below is truncated and shown in full on hover.

analytics.audit.empty.changes.context: Fills the change log when no modification matches the current filters and period range. 'Recorded' means written to the audit trail, so this says the trail holds nothing for that selection rather than reporting a failure.

analytics.audit.empty.emails.context: Fills the email log when no message matches the current state filter and period range. States the absence of records, not an error.

analytics.audit.empty.deliveries.context: Fills the webhook log when no delivery attempt matches the current state filter and period range. A delivery is one attempt to hand a notification to an external address; this states that none was recorded, not that one failed.

analytics.audit.changeTypes.create.context: Names the kind of change where an object was recorded for the first time. It appears in a badge in the narrow Change column and as an option in the filter dropdown, so it must read as the name of a category rather than as a command to the reader — a noun or a past participle is usually better than a bare imperative. One word: the badge is about 100 pixels wide and does not wrap.

analytics.audit.changeTypes.edit.context: Names the kind of change where an object that already existed was modified, as opposed to being created or removed. Reads as a category name in a badge and in the filter dropdown, so prefer a noun or past participle over a bare imperative, and keep it clearly distinct from the creation wording. One word; the badge does not wrap.

analytics.audit.changeTypes.delete.context: Names the kind of change where an object was removed; for API keys, which cannot truly be removed, it also covers revoking them. Reads as a category name in a badge and in the filter dropdown, so prefer a noun or past participle over a bare imperative. One word; the badge does not wrap.

analytics.audit.changeTypes.approve.context: Names the kind of change where a reviewer accepted a submission in the approval workflow, so its figures count as agreed. Recorded separately from an ordinary edit; reads as a category name in a badge and in the filter dropdown, so prefer a noun or past participle over a bare imperative. One word; the badge does not wrap.

analytics.audit.changeTypes.reject.context: Names the kind of change where a reviewer refused a submission in the approval workflow, sending it back rather than accepting it; the reason, when given, appears in the Note column. Reads as a category name in a badge and in the filter dropdown, so prefer a noun or past participle over a bare imperative. One word; the badge does not wrap.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.user.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: an interactive account, belonging to a person who can sign in to the console. Distinct from the neighbouring option, which covers accounts that only hold credentials for machine access. Shown as an option in the Target type dropdown and inside a column only about 120 pixels wide, so keep it to one short word.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.account.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: an account that exists only for programmatic access and cannot sign in to the console. Use the product's generic word for an account, kept clearly distinct from the interactive-user option beside it. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.schema.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: an admin-defined form definition that lays down which values services report. Use the same word the product uses for schemas everywhere else. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.apiKey.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a credential used to call the API. 'Key' means a secret credential, never a keyboard key or a database key, and API stays untranslated. Very short; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.submission.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: one filled-in instance of a schema, for one service and one reporting period. Use the same word the product uses for submissions everywhere else. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.report.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a saved report definition in the reporting area. Use the same word the product uses for reports elsewhere. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.schemaHistor.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a stored earlier version of a schema, kept in that schema's version history. Deliberately separate from the plain schema option, so that tidying up old versions is not mistaken for changing the live definition; make that distinction visible in the wording. Two short words at most; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.approvalRule.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a rule stating whether submissions for a given service and schema must be reviewed before they count. 'Rule' is a configured requirement, and 'approval' is the review decision it demands. Keep it to two short words; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.settings.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: any configuration area saved from the Settings screen, such as the default approval policy, the email configuration or an outgoing template. Recorded as one generic kind, so keep the wording identical to the name of the Settings screen. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.backup.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: the restoring of a saved copy of the data or of the configuration. Use the established noun for a saved copy; the entry records that a restore happened, not that a copy was taken. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.event.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: an occurrence an administrator noted on the timeline, such as an outage, which can be overlaid on the trend charts. Not a calendar appointment and not a system log line. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.commentThrea.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a whole discussion attached to an object, covering its creation, its resolving or reopening and its removal. A thread is the chain of remarks taken as a unit, as distinct from the individual reply covered by the next option. Two short words; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.targetTypes.comment.context: One of the kinds of object a change can be recorded against: a single remark inside a discussion thread. Keep it clearly distinguishable from the thread option beside it, which covers the discussion as a whole. One short word; the column is only about 120 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.statuses.pending.context: State of an email or webhook that is queued and waiting for its first attempt; nothing has been tried yet. Shown in an amber badge and as an option in the state filter. One word, no wrapping — the badge sits in a column about 110 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.statuses.sending.context: State of an email or webhook whose attempt is under way right now, between being queued and finishing. Present progressive, without an ellipsis; it is a state label, not a button caption. One word, no wrapping — the badge sits in a column about 110 pixels wide.

analytics.audit.statuses.sent.context: State of an email or webhook that was handed over successfully; the moment it happened appears in the Sent or Delivered column. Past participle in a green badge, so keep it recognisably the same word used for that column heading. One word, no wrapping.

analytics.audit.statuses.failed.context: State of an email or webhook whose attempts did not succeed; hovering the badge reveals the reason from the most recent try. Past participle in a red badge, describing the record rather than accusing anyone. One word, no wrapping — the badge sits in a column about 110 pixels wide.

analytics.serviceStatus.title.context: Heading of the screen that lists, one row per schema, how complete a single service's submissions currently are. 'Status' is the state of its reporting, not a rank or a legal standing; keep the dash as the separator before the name, and keep the leading word short because the name can be long.

placeholders.service: Display name of the service being inspected, e.g. Rossi Plant

analytics.serviceStatus.mixed.context: Value in the frequency column when the schema's enabled values do not all share one reporting frequency, so no single frequency can be named for the row. One short word for 'several different ones', not for something blended or unclear, and it must fit a narrow column.

analytics.serviceStatus.disabled.context: Small outlined badge beside the name of a schema that has been switched off, so nothing can be submitted against it. Describes the state the schema is in, and is never a command to switch something off. Badges do not wrap, so one word if possible.

analytics.serviceStatus.empty.en: No schemas visible to this service.
analytics.serviceStatus.empty.context: Fills the table when this service is not permitted to submit against any schema, so there is nothing to report on. 'Visible to' means made available to that service by an administrator; a schema is an administrator-defined form definition. Not an error.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.day.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: a single day. A noun for the window itself, and it must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list, which say how often a service submits rather than how long one window lasts.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.week.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: one week. A noun for the window itself, and it must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list, which say how often a service submits rather than how long one window lasts.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.fortnigh.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: two weeks. A noun for the window itself; where the language has no single word for a two-week span, a short phrase meaning 'two weeks' is right. It must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.month.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: one month. A noun for the window itself, and it must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list, which say how often a service submits rather than how long one window lasts.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.quarter.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: a quarter of a year, that is three months. A noun for the window itself, never a district of a town or a fraction of something else, and clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.halfyear.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: half a year, that is six months. A noun for the window itself, and it must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list, which say how often a service submits rather than how long one window lasts.

analytics.serviceStatus.periods.year.context: Option naming the length of the reporting window the screen is asked about: one year. A noun for the window itself, and it must stay clearly distinct from the reporting-frequency names in the cadence list, which say how often a service submits rather than how long one window lasts.

analytics.serviceStatus.columns.submitte.context: Heads the column whose cells read as a ratio, such as 3/5: how many of the schema's enabled values have arrived inside their current reporting window, out of how many are enabled. A past participle standing for 'values received', so a noun phrase may read better; the column is narrow, and the same English word is also used on a badge in the last column, where a different rendering is acceptable.

analytics.serviceStatus.columns.lastSamp.context: Heads the column holding the date and time of the most recent value this service sent for that schema, whatever window it fell in. 'Last' means most recent, never final or ultimate; a sample is one reported measurement. Keep it to two short words at most.

analytics.serviceStatus.columns.status.context: Heads the narrow last column holding a coloured badge that sums up the row's state. 'Status' is the state of the reporting for that schema, not a rank; keep it to one short word.

analytics.serviceStatus.submittedHelp.en: {{submitted}} of {{total}} active value(s) submitted in the current cadence window — {{requiredSubmitted}}/{{requiredTotal}} required.
analytics.serviceStatus.submittedHelp.context: Revealed on hovering the ratio in the submitted column, spelling out what its two parts mean. An active value is one that is switched on, on a schema that is switched on; the current cadence window is the window of that value's own reporting frequency that contains today. English marks the optional plural with '(s)' because the sentence is not plural-aware, so choose a form that reads for any count instead of copying the brackets, and keep the dash before the second figure.

placeholders.submitted: Whole number of active values that have arrived in their current window, e.g. 3
placeholders.total: Whole number of active values on the schema, the denominator, e.g. 5
placeholders.requiredSubmitted: Whole number of those arrived values that the schema marks as mandatory, e.g. 2
placeholders.requiredTotal: Whole number of mandatory active values on the schema, e.g. 2

analytics.serviceStatus.requiredRatio.context: Narrows the ratio in front of it down to the mandatory values only: how many of the values the schema marks as required have arrived, out of how many it requires. 'Required' is the opposite of optional. Grey and very small, and the whole cell must stay on one line, so keep the trailing word as short as possible.

placeholders.submitted: Whole number of mandatory values that have arrived in their current window, e.g. 2
placeholders.total: Whole number of mandatory values on the schema, e.g. 3

joins.after: The overall submitted-to-enabled ratio and a middle dot, both rendered by the code in SchemaRow in ServiceStatusPage.tsx
joins.note: The separator ' · ' is supplied by the code, so this string must not add a leading space or dot; the figures must stay in front of the qualifying word if the language allows it, because the eye reads the two ratios as a pair.

analytics.serviceStatus.statuses.inert.context: Grey badge for a row whose schema is switched off: nothing can be submitted against it and nothing is expected, so the row is neither complete nor late. One word meaning incapable of activity by configuration, not idle, lazy or broken. Badges do not wrap.

analytics.serviceStatus.statuses.noValue.context: Grey badge for a row whose schema is switched on but has no values switched on inside it, so there is nothing for the service to send. A value is one individual measurement the schema defines; 'no values' is about the definition being empty, not about data being absent. Badges do not wrap, so keep it to two short words.

analytics.serviceStatus.statuses.submitt.context: Green badge for a row that is in good order: every mandatory value has arrived inside its current reporting window, or, where the schema requires nothing, at least something has arrived. A past participle describing the state reached, not an action to take; the same English word also heads a column, where a different rendering is acceptable. Badges do not wrap.

analytics.serviceStatus.statuses.optiona.context: Grey badge for a row where the schema marks nothing as mandatory and nothing has arrived yet, so there is no obligation to meet. It describes the obligation, not the data: nothing is owed. Badges do not wrap, so one word.

analytics.serviceStatus.statuses.missing.context: Red badge for a row where at least one mandatory value has not arrived inside its current reporting window. 'Missing' means expected but not filed, not lost or mislaid, and it must match the word used for the same idea on the missing-submissions screens. Badges do not wrap, so one word.
